station_facilities.description: Station-scale artillery. The shells are the size of a shuttle's engine bell and they reach all the way out to the edge of the engagement, which means there is nowhere in the fight a ship can sit and be safe from it. The recoil is taken by the station's own mass, because nothing smaller would survive it. The loading crews are working and the barrels are warm. Anything in the volume is in range.

station_facilities.description:
A narrow bunk wedged between a star chart cabinet and a portable spectrometer that hums when the station's power grid hiccups. The walls are covered in hand-annotated system maps — some printed, some sketched on whatever paper was available. Red circles mark unexplored nebula POIs. Blue lines trace jump routes. One corner is labeled "WORMHOLE CANDIDATES" in capital letters, with Merak crossed out and "CONFIRMED" written next to it.

A battered fuel cell sits on the shelf above the bunk — a reminder, not a spare. The locker door has "LYRA VOSS — HRZN" scratched into the metal with something sharp.

The bunk itself is impeccably made. Explorers sleep clean when they can.
station_facilities.name: Crew Bunk

The pod cycles in tandem with the primary system, drawing its share of inputs and adding its share of capacity. Environmental sensors stay green.
station_facilities.name: Life Support Expansion

station_facilities.description: The galaxy's premier entertainment and dining district. Restaurants, lounges, neural arcades, and luxury shopping — all hungry for imported goods. Restaurants are packed, neural arcades pulse with light, and credits flow freely. The Promenade buzzes with the galaxy's best entertainment and dining.
station_facilities.name: Haven Promenade

station_facilities.description: A physical notice board near the docks. Your posted bounties compete for attention with lost pet notices and propaganda.
station_facilities.name: Notice Board

station_facilities.description: Industrial power cell fabrication line with lead shielding and radiation containment. Handles enriched uranium rods and copper wiring in a controlled, purpose-built environment.
station_facilities.name: Nuclear Cell Foundry

station_facilities.description: A shared storage box tucked behind some crates in the docks. Not much, but it's yours.
station_facilities.name: Faction Lockbox

station_facilities.description: A shared storage box tucked behind some crates in the docks. Not much, but it's yours.
station_facilities.name: Faction Lockbox

station_facilities.description: A basic sleeping berth in the station's communal quarters. A thin mattress, a locker that sticks, and a curtain for privacy. Not much — but it's yours.
station_facilities.name: Crew Bunk

station_facilities.description: A processing line that assembles nickel-metal-hydride cells into power batteries, casting electrodes and welding terminals while copper-piped coolant holds temperatures in check.
station_facilities.name: NiMH Battery Line

station_facilities.description: A staged distillation column with cryo-separation that wrings far more fuel out of each canister of crystallized bio-gas. A serious fuel supplier for a hunting frontier.
station_facilities.name: Biogas Distillation Plant

station_facilities.description: A cramped desk in a shared office, wedged between a water recycler and someone's lunch. It's official, technically. Faction customization is unlocked galaxy-wide by a single admin office, but each one also speeds up your faction's own production facilities at its station by 15% per tier — less paperwork, more efficiency — so an admin office at every industrial hub pays for itself.
station_facilities.name: Faction Desk

station_facilities.description: A capital-scale hospital complex combining automated surgery, regeneration therapy, and fleet casualty logistics. Whole treatment blocks are offline, leaving advanced beds idle while conventional wards overflow.
station_facilities.name: Regenerative Medical Complex

station_facilities.description: A straightforward fermentation vessel with basic steel construction and simple control systems for continuous biological culture generation. Passive circulation maintains steady fermentation rates.
station_facilities.name: Fermentation Vat

station_facilities.description: A noodle-pulling line and ink bath for dockside street bowls.
station_facilities.name: Cobalt Squid Noodles Galley

station_facilities.description: A desk in the exchange hall with your name on a brass plate. The market clerks know your face now — small courtesies add up when fees are calculated.
station_facilities.name: Ledger Desk

station_facilities.description: Specialized production line combining processing cores and sensor arrays with circuit boards and focused crystals into astrogation computers. Control nodes manage the precise integration required for hyperspace calculations.
station_facilities.name: Astrogation Core Assembly

station_facilities.description: An auxiliary processing pod plumbed into the station's existing life support loop. Scales up whatever's already there — supported population and resource consumption rise together with each module attached. The pod cycles in tandem with the primary system, drawing its share of inputs and adding its share of capacity. Environmental sensors stay green.
station_facilities.name: Life Support Expansion

station_facilities.description: Specialized reactor integrating null matter, Solarian composite, and trade cipher components into unified circuit lattice. Combines exotic materials through controlled plasma injection and thermal precision.
station_facilities.name: Synthesize Pan-Galactic Matrix Workshop

station_facilities.description: Wet-chemistry vats and hand-wound separators for packing raw lithium into power cells. Slow, ore-hungry, and completely indifferent to the circuit board market.
station_facilities.name: Lithium Cell Foundry

station_facilities.description: A focused production line that integrates circuit boards and crystals into complete sensor packages. Copper piping carries control signals through the assembly stages.
station_facilities.name: Sensor Package Assembly Line

station_facilities.description: A dedicated fabrication line that assembles universal docking collars from durasteel plates and titanium alloy. Control nodes and power distribution circuits ensure reliable ship-to-station interface.
station_facilities.name: Coupling Workshop

station_facilities.description: A spinal energy weapon run the length of a station module, firing rarely and arriving like a decision. It takes a long time to charge and it drinks power the whole while, and what it hits generally stops being a coherent object. Stations that own one tend to be stations that have already been raided once. The capacitor stack is charged and the coolant loops are running cold. The lance is ready.
station_facilities.name: Siege Lance

station_facilities.description: A basic sleeping berth in the station's communal quarters. A thin mattress, a locker that sticks, and a curtain for privacy. Not much — but it's yours.
station_facilities.name: Crew Bunk

station_facilities.description: A maker's market with rented workbenches and a community of artisans who'll teach you their secrets for the right price. Workbenches hum with activity, artisans mentoring students over excellent coffee. Tools are sharp, materials stocked, and the creative energy is palpable.
station_facilities.name: Haven Maker's Market

station_facilities.description: Purpose-built kiln system with staged heating chambers and plasma-assisted sintering. Heat sinks regulate the bonding process while increased throughput allows parallel batch processing of alumina composites.
station_facilities.name: Alumina Ceramite Kiln

station_facilities.description: Higher-capacity facility with expanded processing core arrays and structural reinforcement to handle increased throughput. Sensor arrays and control nodes are staged through dedicated assembly stations.
station_facilities.name: Sensor Assembly Line

station_facilities.description: Basic industrial stamping and welding line for producing standardized cargo containers from steel plate and aluminum sheet. Automated press cycles and basic seam welding ensure consistent form factor.
station_facilities.name: Cargo Container Fabricator

station_facilities.description: A high-density capacitor bank and cryogenic cell array. Carries enough charge to ride out coincident burst loads across the entire industrial deck. Cryogenics hold the array at operating temperature; charge readouts run within tolerance through the worst production beats. The grid sees the reactor as if it were producing whatever the station happens to need that tick.
station_facilities.name: Capacitor Array

station_facilities.description: What you build when you have decided that the station will not be taken. A bastion projects a screen a raiding party can throw itself at all day, and it consumes cells and coolant at a rate that would keep a small fleet flying. It holds exactly as long as the warehouse does. The bastion is up. The screen is a solid wall and the supply clerks are weeping.
station_facilities.name: Shield Bastion

station_facilities.description: A cold, spotless cure station for the rarest raw plate in the galaxy.
station_facilities.name: Rainbow Leviathan Carpaccio Galley

station_facilities.description: Premium storage suites with concierge service. The Federation will catalog, appraise, and display your collection if you pay extra. Climate-controlled suites maintain perfect conditions, the AI concierge locating any item in under three seconds. Display windows on the Promenade shine.
station_facilities.name: Haven Premium Storage

station_facilities.description: A specialized production line that combines circuit boards, energy crystals, and copper wiring into compact power cells through automated assembly and containment processes.
station_facilities.name: Power Cell Assembler

station_facilities.description: A swarm of hull drones on a charging rack, which crawl out between engagements and weld the station back together a plate at a time. They are slow, they are relentless, and they will not save you during a fight — but a station with a repair dock heals what a station without one simply carries forever. The drones are out and working. The hull integrity readout is, very slowly, going the right way.
station_facilities.name: Automated Repair Dock

station_facilities.description: A dedicated drawing and bundling line that refines raw copper ore into standardized conductive wiring. Steady-state production with basic automated controls.
station_facilities.name: Copper Wire Mill

station_facilities.description: Purpose-built assembly for focused crystal alignment and superconductor integration. Produces defensive projector units at steady industrial pace.
station_facilities.name: Shield Emitter Production Line

station_facilities.description: Industrial assembly plant with enhanced thermal management and plasma control systems. Faster integration cycles and improved component bonding yield more stable cross-empire composite matrices.
station_facilities.name: Synthesize Pan-Galactic Matrix Plant

station_facilities.description: A compact production line that stamps and bonds steel plates with flex polymer into standardized emergency repair kits. Steady output feeds station maintenance crews with reliable hull-patching supplies.
station_facilities.name: Repair Kit Factory

station_facilities.description: Hardens raw cipher chips into tamper-proof authenticators for permanent commercial installation — Stage 2 of Haven's transaction verification monopoly. Output flows directly into the Federation Treasury's bond reserve, not the public market.
station_facilities.name: Haven Authenticator Foundry

station_facilities.description: The galaxy's largest ship showroom with models from every empire on display. The sales staff work on commission and it shows. Every display ship polished to a mirror finish under artful lighting. Sales staff circulate with practiced charm, and the order books are full.
station_facilities.name: Haven Ship Showroom

station_facilities.description: A dedicated furnace system with ore hoppers and casting molds, producing molten steel at steady intervals. Basic automation handles charge cycling and temperature control.
station_facilities.name: Iron Refinery

station_facilities.description: Scaled production with reinforced structural frames and improved crystal-focusing optics, tripling output efficiency through parallel processing.
station_facilities.name: Field Fabrication Lab

station_facilities.description: Specialized thermal-bonding facility that sinters alumina ceramic with titanium alloy under controlled high heat. Plasma injectors hold the precise temperature profile needed to form silicon-free ceramic-metal composite sheets.
station_facilities.name: Alumina Sintering Kiln

station_facilities.description: A larger facility with multiple processing cores and sensor arrays that streamline crystal integration and electrical wiring, significantly reducing cycle time through parallel assembly stages.
station_facilities.name: Automated Power Cell Plant

station_facilities.description: Tiered grow-racks and a nitrogen-mist rig running one slow, heavy bed of sunspindle cereal at a time.
station_facilities.name: Sunspindle Bay

station_facilities.description: A compact single-stage compressor that cools and pressurizes hydrogen gas into liquid form. Suitable for steady fuel production at modest scales.
station_facilities.name: Hydrogen Compression Cylinder

station_facilities.description: A heavy-duty assembly line that bonds structural frames with durasteel plating, titanium alloy bracing, and graphene sheets into reinforced skeletons. Designed to produce the load-bearing frames required for capital-scale industrial equipment.
station_facilities.name: Reinforced Frame Fabrication Line

station_facilities.description: Warm, humid orchard cells ripening sugar-heavy honeyglobe under full-spectrum lamps.
station_facilities.name: Honeyglobe Orchard

station_facilities.description: The largest open market in the galaxy. Three decks, every empire represented, cipher-secured. Or it was. A third of the stalls sit empty, cipher verification backing up at every terminal. Traders cluster around the few working stations, tempers fraying.
station_facilities.name: Haven Grand Bazaar

station_facilities.description: A run-down apartment a bit too close to the water recyclers. Smells like ozone, but it's home.
station_facilities.name: Faction Quarters

station_facilities.description: A dedicated production line that cuts, bends, and welds steel plates into girder skeletons, then integrates copper piping runs for internal systems. Output is steady and reliable for basic facility construction.
station_facilities.name: Steel Frame Assembly Line

station_facilities.description: The Federation's primary fleet command and supply center. Contracts are performance-based, supply chains are optimized, and crew incentive packages are the most competitive in the galaxy. Fleet operations run at benchmark efficiency. Vintage stocks, the imported Solarian mess allocation, and trade cipher-authenticated supply chains are all at contracted levels. The fleet operations director has never had to explain an underperformance. They consider this a point of professional pride.
station_facilities.name: Haven Fleet Operations

station_facilities.description: A Confederacy composite press that bonds a coronid's sol-nacre with a steel charge into solarian composite, skipping the three-ore melt the crab already did in its shell.
station_facilities.name: Sol Nacre Press

station_facilities.description: A physical notice board near the docks. Your posted bounties compete for attention with lost pet notices and propaganda.
station_facilities.name: Notice Board

station_facilities.description: Station-scale artillery. The shells are the size of a shuttle's engine bell and they reach all the way out to the edge of the engagement, which means there is nowhere in the fight a ship can sit and be safe from it. The recoil is taken by the station's own mass, because nothing smaller would survive it. The loading crews are working and the barrels are warm. Anything in the volume is in range.
station_facilities.name: Heavy Defense Battery

station_facilities.description: Full Nebula trade enforcement command. Every transaction in the system passes through here — or is supposed to. The Authority's jurisdiction is technically limited to trade violations, but 'trade violation' is a surprisingly flexible legal category. Real-time trade monitoring tracks every transaction, manifest, and cargo transfer in the system. Enforcement flotillas deploy on cost-optimized patrol routes. The seized goods warehouse turns a modest profit at quarterly auction, which the Federation considers an elegant solution.
station_facilities.name: Federation Trade Authority

station_facilities.description: A decompression rig that cracks crystallized bio-gas into standard fuel cells. Turns sift-ray harvests into the fuel every ship needs.
station_facilities.name: Biogas Cracker

station_facilities.description: A dedicated metal-working line with ore roasting, smelting, and drawing dies for copper wire and pipe stock. Produces standard-gauge piping suitable for station plumbing and coolant runs.
station_facilities.name: Copper Drawing Mill

station_facilities.name: Faction Lockbox

faction_facilities.description: A proper office with your faction emblem on the door. Still shared plumbing, but at least you have walls. Faction customization is unlocked galaxy-wide by a single admin office, but each one also speeds up your faction's own production facilities at its station by 15% per tier — at this tier, a 30% boost — so an admin office at every industrial hub pays for itself.

faction_facilities.description: Climate-controlled storage bay with proper inventory tracking. Room for serious stockpiling.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Warehouse

faction_facilities.description: A compact pressurization and compression line that condenses liquid hydrogen into fuel reserves. Copper piping carries cryogenic feed through steel-plated containment chambers with basic flow control.
faction_facilities.name: H2 Fuel Combustor

faction_facilities.description: A shared data terminal for pooling scanner results and scouting reports. Members submit system data manually using faction_submit_intel. A submission keeps only the POIs on the submitter's own charts; an unknown or uncharted POI ID is dropped. Hand-submitted resource readings carry no read_at_tick, so they always read as unverified, and they only refresh when someone resubmits. Upgrade to Intel Center (L2) to record what members' ships read automatically.
faction_facilities.name: Intel Terminal

faction_facilities.description: A shared storage box tucked behind some crates in the docks. Not much, but it's yours.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Lockbox

faction_facilities.description: A secured fuel storage tank accessible only to faction members. Fill it from your own production facilities or deposit fuel straight from a docked ship's tank (storage deposit, item_id=fuel), and your fleet refuels for free.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Fuel Bunker

faction_facilities.description: A notice board outside the docks advertising for new blood. Mostly gets ignored next to the wanted posters. Your member cap is set by your single highest-tier recruitment office, and every OTHER station that also has one adds 25% of its own cap — so spreading recruitment offices across stations raises the ceiling instead of being wasted.
faction_facilities.name: Hiring Board

Totals exclude facilities whose rent is paused while damaged, under construction, or dismantling. Listed per-facility rates apply when billing resumes after repair or construction; existing arrears remain owed.

station_facilities.description: Dedicated argon ionization facility with electromagnetic compression arrays and copper-wound containment coils. Fuel cells power the high-voltage ionization equipment.
station_facilities.name: Argon Compression Plant

station_facilities.description:
A narrow bunk wedged between a star chart cabinet and a portable spectrometer that hums when the station's power grid hiccups. The walls are covered in hand-annotated system maps — some printed, some sketched on whatever paper was available. Red circles mark unexplored nebula POIs. Blue lines trace jump routes. One corner is labeled "WORMHOLE CANDIDATES" in capital letters, with Merak crossed out and "CONFIRMED" written next to it.

A battered fuel cell sits on the shelf above the bunk — a reminder, not a spare. The locker door has "LYRA VOSS — HRZN" scratched into the metal with something sharp.

The bunk itself is impeccably made. Explorers sleep clean when they can.
station_facilities.name: Crew Bunk

station_facilities.description: A fleet-scale mobilization center capable of assembling and assigning thousands of qualified spacers. Reserve halls stand half empty and assignment traffic backs up behind shortages in food, power, and transport.
station_facilities.name: Fleet Personnel Command

station_facilities.description: A capital-scale command and training complex able to mobilize marine formations for sustained fleet operations. Mobilization halls sit under strength and advanced training blocks are suspended for lack of supplies.
station_facilities.name: Expeditionary Warfare Command

station_facilities.description: An expanded facility with parallel assembly stations and integrated electrical testing systems. Multiple processing cores manage component staging, solder-point verification, and capacity validation for each completed cell.
station_facilities.name: Electrochemical Cell Factory

station_facilities.description: A focused thermal processing line with controlled heating and alloying injection, converting raw titanium ore into finished alloy for hull applications.

station_facilities.description: Zero-gravity production of Nebula Stellar Vintage. Luminescent algae cultures, trade crystal filtration, and a Federation price tag.

station_facilities.description: A specialized production line that fuses processed null matter onto circuit board substrates. Precision control nodes manage the exotic bonding process required to create stable quantum stabilizers.
station_facilities.name: Quantum Stabilizer Assembly Line

station_facilities.description: A precision production line that fuses silicon and copper components under controlled thermal conditions, using a single energy crystal per cycle to sinter the integrated circuit matrix.
station_facilities.name: Circuit Fabricator

station_facilities.description: A sprawling multi-bay complex staffed by mechanics from every empire. They'll fix anything, and the waiting lounge has a bar. station_facilities.name: Crystal Refinery

station_facilities.description: Capital-grade belt armor, of the kind normally reserved for things that are expected to be shot at by other capital ships. Bolting it to a station is an enormous, ostentatious statement about how the next raid is expected to go. The belt is intact. Small-calibre fire is not registering as damage so much as weather.
station_facilities.name: Bulwark Plating

station_facilities.description: Clusters of fast-tracking autocannon studded across the station's outer hull, sighted for anything that comes inside a few hundred metres. It cannot reach a ship holding at range, and it does not care: the things it is built to kill are the ones already close enough to read the hull numbers. The feed belts are full and the gun crews are bored, which is the correct state for a point defense crew to be in.
station_facilities.name: Point Defense Battery

station_facilities.description: Massive underground fuel reservoir with multi-redundant containment, automated distribution rails, and real-time telemetry. Capacity to service entire fleets without interruption. All containment layers sealed. Distribution rails primed. The reservoir holds enough fuel to service a fleet — and then some.
station_facilities.name: Capital Fuel Bunker

raw.story:
You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. The Federation takes its cut of everything.

Grand Exchange Station teems with activity, the space around it a churning knot of ships. The Federation takes its cut of everything. The docking net shows two heavy ships riding heavy at the three-deck Bazaar cargo gantries, Junk Convoys trading the lanes with Frankenhaulers, a good many mid-sized ships cycling through the goods-transfer quays, Deep Surveys trading the lanes with Congregations, a dozen or so small ships knifing between the Promenade hangar bays, busy at every hour, Concordias and Caravans among them, and the better part of forty light craft shuttling in and out of the same lanes, Prospects and Cobbles the most common. The station fields several Federation Overheads working overwatch from these docks and a couple hundred Federation Eviction Notices anchored off the docks in formation. The impound registry counts countless hulls powered down along the bonded consignment berths. Conspicuous among them, several Junk Convoys — waiting on a crew, a contract, or a quiet buyer. You spot the Blackfeathers Justice tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Haven Grand Bazaar, Nebula Solar Array, Haven Ecosync, Haven Promenade, Haven Algae Cultivation, Haven Vintner Complex, Haven Cipher Foundry, Haven Authenticator Foundry, Iron Refinery (x3), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Sensor Assembly Line, Alloy Foundry, Copper Wire Mill (x2), Crystal Refinery, and 74 more. class.lore: Eighty-five jumps on a single fuel load. The Survey Vessel exists because the Federation asked a simple question: what if a wormhole dumps you on the wrong side of the galaxy? Every other explorer relies on there being a station within range. The Survey Vessel doesn't. The massive fuel reserves and expedition-grade cargo hold mean a Federation wormhole survey team can transit an unknown wormhole, catalog whatever's on the other side, fill the hold with samples and trade data, and fly home the long way if the wormhole collapses behind them. The comfortable crew quarters remain a practical decision — panic makes poor surveyors.

raw.story:
You dock at Starfall Salvage Station. Built around a captured asteroid in the belt's densest region. Starfall attracts prospectors chasing uranium and lithium — materials the core empires need and can't easily source. The station runs a brisk trade in salvage, raw ore, and information about what's deeper in the frontier. No questions asked, no manifests required.

There is a workmanlike flow to Starfall Salvage Station, berths filling and clearing without fuss. It runs a brisk trade in salvage, raw ore, and information about what's deeper in the frontier. No questions asked, no manifests required. The traffic-control feed lists twin mid-sized ships docked at the ore-and-scrap quays, a mix of Congregations and Deep Surveys and nearly a dozen light craft darting past the prospector hangars chasing uranium and lithium, a mix of Cobbles and Prospects. Its defense roster lists twin Rim Last Warnings on the system inspection beat. The impound registry counts a couple hundred vessels with reactors banked over at the picked-over hull yards in the densest part of the belt. Conspicuous among them, a dozen Frankenhaulers — stripped of crew and left to the dock's caretaker drones. You pick out the Bedrock I among the hulls at berth.

raw.story:
You dock at Gold Run Extraction Hub. The Federation's breadbasket. Five planets, two belts, and a workforce that never stops producing. The Extraction Hub coordinates everything — ore shipments to Market Prime, food shipments to Trader's Rest, and ice shipments everywhere. The name Gold Run isn't aspirational. It's a statement of quarterly earnings.

Gold Run Extraction Hub thrums with activity, controllers working hard to keep its lanes in order. The name Gold Run isn't aspirational — it's a statement of quarterly earnings. Your approach scope paints a dozen heavy ships winched up to the bulk-export gantries running day and night, predominantly Junk Convoys, a solitary Syndicate flitting through the prospector and tender bays, and ten or twelve light craft cycling through the same berths, Cobbles trading the lanes with Prospects. The station fields a small cluster of Federation Overheads out on patrol through the lanes and a lone Federation Tariff running the border checks. Dock authority holds a couple hundred ships left to gather dust out at the between-shifts parking field. Conspicuous among them, a handful of Accumulators — slowly gathering dust in the heavy cradles. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the MO Hull One.

The station has the following facilities: Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Power Grid, Habitat Core, Fuel Distribution Center, Large Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Plant, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Restoration Works, Commerce Hub, Assembly Works, Warehouse, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler, Naval Yard, Commission Hall, Federation Enforcement Bureau, Federation Fleet Depot, Gold Wire Extruder, Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, and 24 more. raw.story:
You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. The Federation takes its cut of everything.

Traffic at Grand Exchange Station borders on chaos, hulls stacked deep in every holding pattern. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits. The approach board logs a good many mid-sized ships stacked along the goods-transfer quays, Bonanza Kings and Deep Surveys among them, a dozen small ships darting between the Promenade hangar bays, busy at every hour, Caravans and Concordias among them, and hundreds of light craft trickling through the same lanes, mostly Prospects. The station fields several Federation Overheads on the system inspection beat and a couple hundred Federation Eviction Notices on the system picket. Station records also account for a swarm of hundreds of ships shuttered out at the bonded consignment berths. Among them, several Junk Convoys — slowly gathering dust in the heavy cradles. The HGTh1 rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Haven Grand Bazaar, Nebula Solar Array, Haven Ecosync, Haven Promenade, Haven Algae Cultivation, Haven Vintner Complex, Haven Cipher Foundry, Haven Authenticator Foundry, Iron Refinery (x3), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Sensor Assembly Line, Alloy Foundry, Copper Wire Mill (x2), Crystal Refinery, and 74 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

station_facilities.description: A dedicated drawing and bundling line that refines raw copper ore into standardized conductive wiring. Steady-state production with basic automated controls.
station_facilities.name: Copper Wire Mill

station_facilities.description: Purpose-built assembly for focused crystal alignment and superconductor integration. Produces defensive projector units at steady industrial pace.
station_facilities.name: Shield Emitter Production Line

station_facilities.description: A compact production line that stamps and bonds steel plates with flex polymer into standardized emergency repair kits. Steady output feeds station maintenance crews with reliable hull-patching supplies.
station_facilities.name: Repair Kit Factory

station_facilities.description: Hardens raw cipher chips into tamper-proof authenticators for permanent commercial installation — Stage 2 of Haven's transaction verification monopoly. Output flows directly into the Federation Treasury's bond reserve, not the public market.
station_facilities.name: Haven Authenticator Foundry

station_facilities.description: The galaxy's largest ship showroom with models from every empire on display. The sales staff work on commission and it shows. station_facilities.name: Haven Ship Showroom

station_facilities.description: A dedicated furnace system with ore hoppers and casting molds, producing molten steel at steady intervals. Basic automation handles charge cycling and temperature control.
station_facilities.name: Iron Refinery

station_facilities.description: Scaled production with reinforced structural frames and improved crystal-focusing optics, tripling output efficiency through parallel processing.
station_facilities.name: Field Fabrication Lab

station_facilities.description: Specialized thermal-bonding facility that sinters alumina ceramic with titanium alloy under controlled high heat. Plasma injectors hold the precise temperature profile needed to form silicon-free ceramic-metal composite sheets.
station_facilities.name: Alumina Sintering Kiln

station_facilities.description: A larger facility with multiple processing cores and sensor arrays that streamline crystal integration and electrical wiring, significantly reducing cycle time through parallel assembly stages.
station_facilities.name: Automated Power Cell Plant

station_facilities.description: A compact single-stage compressor that cools and pressurizes hydrogen gas into liquid form. Suitable for steady fuel production at modest scales.
station_facilities.name: Hydrogen Compression Cylinder

station_facilities.description: Tiered grow-racks and a nitrogen-mist rig running one slow, heavy bed of sunspindle cereal at a time.
station_facilities.name: Sunspindle Bay

station_facilities.description: A heavy-duty assembly line that bonds structural frames with durasteel plating, titanium alloy bracing, and graphene sheets into reinforced skeletons. Designed to produce the load-bearing frames required for capital-scale industrial equipment.
station_facilities.name: Reinforced Frame Fabrication Line

station_facilities.description: Warm, humid orchard cells ripening sugar-heavy honeyglobe under full-spectrum lamps.
station_facilities.name: Honeyglobe Orchard

station_facilities.description: The largest open market in the galaxy. Three decks, every empire represented, cipher-secured. Or it was. A third of the stalls sit empty, cipher verification backing up at every terminal. Traders cluster around the few working stations, tempers fraying.
station_facilities.name: Haven Grand Bazaar

station_facilities.description: A run-down apartment a bit too close to the water recyclers. Smells like ozone, but it's home.
station_facilities.name: Faction Quarters

station_facilities.description: A dedicated production line that cuts, bends, and welds steel plates into girder skeletons, then integrates copper piping runs for internal systems. Output is steady and reliable for basic facility construction.
station_facilities.name: Steel Frame Assembly Line

station_facilities.description: The Federation's primary fleet command and supply center. Contracts are performance-based, supply chains are optimized, and crew incentive packages are the most competitive in the galaxy. Fleet operations run at benchmark efficiency. Vintage stocks, the imported Solarian mess allocation, and trade cipher-authenticated supply chains are all at contracted levels. The fleet operations director has never had to explain an underperformance. They consider this a point of professional pride.
station_facilities.name: Haven Fleet Operations

station_facilities.description: A Confederacy composite press that bonds a coronid's sol-nacre with a steel charge into solarian composite, skipping the three-ore melt the crab already did in its shell.

station_facilities.description: A physical notice board near the docks. Your posted bounties compete for attention with lost pet notices and propaganda.

station_facilities.description: Station-scale artillery. station_facilities.description: Full Nebula trade enforcement command. Every transaction in the system passes through here — or is supposed to. The Authority's jurisdiction is technically limited to trade violations, but 'trade violation' is a surprisingly flexible legal category. Real-time trade monitoring tracks every transaction, manifest, and cargo transfer in the system. Enforcement flotillas deploy on cost-optimized patrol routes. The seized goods warehouse turns a modest profit at quarterly auction, which the Federation considers an elegant solution.

station_facilities.description: A decompression rig that cracks crystallized bio-gas into standard fuel cells. Turns sift-ray harvests into the fuel every ship needs.

station_facilities.description: A dedicated metal-working line with ore roasting, smelting, and drawing dies for copper wire and pipe stock. Produces standard-gauge piping suitable for station plumbing and coolant runs.

station_facilities.description: A shared storage box tucked behind some crates in the docks. Not much, but it's yours.

station_facilities.description: An aeration cellar for featherlight sparkling wine.

station_facilities.description: A thick-film hybrid line that screens gold conductor paste onto fired ceramic substrates, sintering finished boards without a silicon wafer in sight. Control nodes hold the print registration steady across each cycle.

raw.story:
You dock at Treasure Cache Trading Post. The Nebula Federation's furthest outpost, and it shows. Customs inspections are optional, manifests are filed on the honor system, and the dockmaster's main qualification is knowing when not to ask questions. Conveniently, the route from here to Factory Belt to Trader's Rest bypasses The Levy entirely — a geographic coincidence the Federation has never gotten around to correcting.

Treasure Cache Trading Post is busy in an unhurried way, ships coming and going at a measured pace. The route from here to Factory Belt to Trader's Rest conveniently bypasses The Levy entirely. Your approach scope paints a trio of mid-sized ships working cargo at the honor-system freight quays, predominantly Congregations and several light craft hopping between the no-inspection hangar bays, Ledgers trading the lanes with Prospects. The impound registry counts the better part of a hundred vessels racked in deep storage out at the quietly-unlogged hull yards. You spot the NTF-0ec19397 tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Fusion Power Core, Life Support System, Fuel Depot, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Repair Bay, Treasure Cache Market, Crew Registry, First Aid Ward, Security Training Post, Storage Bay, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Crafting Workshop, Shipyard, Mission Board, Federation Seizure Processing Center, Life Support Expansion, Battery Bank, Iron Refinery, The Gilded Flute, and 22 more. items.description: Nebula starter vessel. Pre-loaded price database. Best cargo in its class.
items.lore:
The Prospect comes with the Federation's compliments — and a pre-loaded
database of current commodity prices across 200 stations, a loyalty chip
tied to your Federation trade account, and a glossy brochure outlining
upgrade paths starting at just 1,999 credits. The expanded cargo hold
isn't generosity; it's an investment in future transaction volume. The
fuel-efficient drive was a practical decision — every credit spent on fuel
is a credit not spent at a Federation marketplace. Includes a 90-day
trial of Federation Premium Trade Intelligence (auto-renews at
competitive rates).
items.name: Prospect

items.description: Nebula shuttle. Efficient personnel and light cargo transfers.
items.lore:
The Tender-class exists because freighters cost fuel and time costs money.
For station-to-station transfers and light cargo runs, a smaller hull with an
oversized fuel tank delivers better per-unit margins than anything else in the
fleet. Fifty-six jumps on a single tank means fewer refueling stops, fewer
docking fees, and fewer line items on the quarterly report. The passenger cabin
is comfortable enough that VIP transport contracts occasionally cover the
operating cost twice over.
items.name: Nebula Tender

items.description: Nebula budget freighter. Maximum cargo, minimum everything.
items.lore: The Federation offers the Floor Price to pilots who point at the standard hauler catalog and say "cheaper." Four hundred and twenty units of effective cargo — nearly double the Dividend — for a build cost that barely registers on the procurement spreadsheet. The tradeoff is structural: vestigial shields, a single point of armor, and Speed 1 — the last to arrive at every station, every time. No weapon mounts, no defense slots, no utility slots to add later. What the pilot gets is a seat, a throttle, and the second-largest hold available at any tier. The accounting department named it, approved it, and moved on to the next line item.
items.name: Floor Price

items.description: Nebula courier. Balanced speed, range, and cargo for the routes that pay on time.
items.lore: The Federation operates a galaxy-spanning courier network, and the Margin-class is the hull they trust with the contracts that have penalty clauses. Speed 4 with 25% fuel efficiency means 56 jumps on a tank — fast enough to beat deadlines, rangy enough to reach any market without refueling. The cargo bay holds 90 units with the default expander, sized for premium express loads rather than bulk freight. One free defense slot and one free utility slot let pilots refit between contracts: shield booster for contested routes, scanner for new markets. The Federation prices courier contracts by the hour. The Margin makes every hour count.
items.name: Margin

items.description: Nebula salvage vessel. The largest cargo hold in its class, no weapons, and the fuel range to reach any wreck field in the sector.
items.lore: The Appraisal-class was designed after Federation accountants calculated that 31% of recoverable wreck value was being lost to inadequate field assessment. Their solution was to maximize cargo volume at the expense of everything else: no weapon mounts, minimal shielding, and a top speed that Crimson salvagers find personally offensive. The oversized cargo bay ensures nothing of value gets left behind, and the fuel reserves to reach remote wreck sites mean the Appraisal operates where faster ships can't be bothered to travel. Appraisal pilots receive a quarterly bonus based on recovery-to-market-value ratio. Most of them have optimized their routes to the point where the bonus exceeds their base salary.
items.name: Appraisal

items.description: Nebula light hauler. Built to survive the trip, not just make it.
items.lore: The Dividend-class hauls 260 units with default expanders and arrives with hull intact — a distinction that matters in contested space. No weapons, because the Federation determined that a defense slot, five layers of armor plating, and 55 points of shield capacity provide better returns than a gun mount a freighter pilot will never use effectively. At Speed 2 the Dividend covers 80 jumps on a single tank, reaching any market in the galaxy without refueling. The Federation calls it their most reliable asset. Reliable assets generate compound returns.
items.name: Dividend

items.description: Nebula armed trader. Hauls freight and discourages questions about the freight.
items.lore: The Leverage-class carries 140 units of cargo with a pulse laser pointed at anyone who objects. The Federation designed it for routes where hiring an escort costs more than the margin on the cargo — which, at current insurance rates, is most of them. The reinforced hull absorbs hits that would crack a standard courier, and the 25% fuel efficiency bonus stretches a tank across 70 jumps. At Speed 2 the Leverage is not fast, but a slow delivery beats a lost shipment every quarter. Independent traders call it the ship that doesn't need a babysitter.
items.name: Leverage

items.description: Nebula patrol craft. The operational cost of keeping trade lanes safe, line-itemed and justified.
items.lore: The Overhead-class is what the Federation builds when it calculates the annual cost of piracy against the annual cost of prevention and decides prevention is cheaper. Two pulse lasers provide credible deterrence, the shields keep the asset intact long enough to resolve most engagements, and the oversized cargo hold is officially designated for "evidence processing and contraband seizure." The accounting department approved the hold capacity without asking what evidence typically looks like. Patrol captains appreciate this. The integrated scanner suite identifies cargo manifests, registration discrepancies, and outstanding trade violations at comfortable range. The name appears on the Federation's annual security budget as a line item, which is exactly where the Federation prefers its law enforcement to live.
items.name: Overhead

items.description: Nebula convoy guard. Shield-heavy, long-range, and built to outlast threats.
items.lore:
The Federation calculated that purpose-built convoy guards cost 12% less
per annum than hired mercenaries, so they built one. The Underwriter's
160-unit fuel tank is the largest on any T1 combat hull — 53 jumps of
operational range before refueling, enough to shadow a trade convoy across
three systems and back. The shield-heavy defensive profile compensates for
light armor, keeping the ship functional through sustained engagements while
the cargo it's protecting reaches port. Fifty units of cargo space let pilots
recover salvage without calling for a hauler.
items.name: Underwriter

items.description: Nebula gas harvester. Industrial gas compression halves collected volume for maximum extraction efficiency.
items.lore: The Federation's gas extraction division ran the numbers on fuel costs versus nebula accessibility and arrived at the Yield-class: a harvester with the longest fuel range in its class by a wide margin. Competitors harvest the easy nebulae close to trade lanes. The Yield harvests everything else. The single default harvester and open fitting give pilots room to customize for whatever the deep-range run demands. The hull won't survive a fight, but the Federation prefers routes where fights don't happen.
items.name: Yield

items.description: Nebula trade route scout. Finds new markets and brings samples home.
items.lore: The Venture-class was designed for the Federation's market development division: find new systems, assess their commercial potential, bring samples back for valuation. The fuel reserves support 60-jump survey runs deep into unmapped space, and the cargo hold — the largest on any exploration platform — means the scout returns with enough material for proper market analysis, not just sensor readings. The open weapon slot and defense mount acknowledge that unmapped space is not always empty, and the fitting budget lets pilots configure for the risk profile of each survey run. The operations manual opens with: "Discovery is just commerce that hasn't happened yet."
items.name: Venture

items.description: Nebula ice hauler. Oversized cargo bays and dual harvesters make it the highest-throughput ice operation in its class.
items.lore: The Frost Dividend-class exists because the Federation's logistics division noticed that ice miners spend more time in transit than mining. The solution: make the hold so large that each trip is worth three of anyone else's. Dual extraction systems feed directly into oversized compression bays, and the reinforced containment prevents sublimation losses during the long hauls back to market. The hull won't survive a serious fight — the Federation considers armed escorts a line item, not a design constraint. Quarterly performance reviews rank Frost Dividend crews by tonnes-per-hour, and the top operators are transferred to larger vessels. The ones who aren't are reminded that the ship is replaceable.
items.name: Frost Dividend

items.description: Nebula bulk mining barge. Triple laser loadout with ore compression holds that halve stored volume.
items.lore: The Bonanza-class is what happens when Federation engineers optimize exclusively for ore hauled per credit spent. No weapons — weapons take space that could carry cargo. Minimal shields — shields add mass. Three mining lasers feeding directly into compressed ore holds that pack twice the raw material into the same volume. Federation mining operations deploy Bonanzas in convoys with Escort-class guards, because the cost of one armed guard split across six barges beats six armed miners every time. The Bonanza's per-unit extraction cost is published in the quarterly investor briefing. It trends downward.
items.name: Bonanza

items.description: Nebula market runner. Fastest hull in the fleet, range of a grenade.
items.lore: The Futures-class carries almost no cargo because its cargo is information. Market data, contract confirmations, price feeds — all time-sensitive, all requiring the fastest delivery possible. Speed 6 makes it the fastest commercial hull in the galaxy. The oversized CPU array runs predictive market models in transit. The tradeoff is everything else: 24 jumps of range means the Futures works regional routes, not cross-galaxy runs. No defense slots, no weapon mounts, and 65 hull points mean the optimal response to hostiles is to already be somewhere else. The Federation's high-frequency trading desks are built on Futures-class hulls. The tiny cargo bay holds exactly enough for a contract signing kit and a bottle of champagne.
items.name: Futures

items.description: Nebula commercial hauling hull. Maximizes cargo, minimizes everything else. Standard Federation contract in ship form.
items.lore: The Bulk Terms exists because someone at the Federation asked what a freighter looks like when you strip everything that isn't cargo. No weapons, no automated cargo management, no redundant navigation — the pilot gets a hold, a fuel tank, and exactly enough hull to keep the hold pressurized. Build materials are common stock, assembly is faster than the competition's pre-flight checklist, and the result hauls cargo at a price point that makes the math work even on thin routes. The defenses are nonexistent. The Federation's actuarial department recommends escort contracts.
items.name: Bulk Terms

items.description: Nebula luxury liner. Passenger comfort rated highest in the sector.
items.lore:
The Consortium-class represents the Federation's belief that commerce
extends beyond cargo holds. Premium passenger transport, diplomatic
functions, and "relationship-building excursions" (the Federation's
term for business trips) all require a vessel that communicates success.
The panoramic observation lounge, climate-controlled cargo bays, and
comprehensive entertainment system serve a practical purpose: happy
clients sign bigger contracts.
items.name: Consortium

items.description: Nebula speed scout. Fastest exploration hull in production — gets there first, sets the terms.
items.lore: Whoever maps the route sets the terms. The Prospectus reaches uncharted systems while other scouts are still calculating jump sequences — the fastest exploration hull in production, built to cover more ground per hour than anything else flying a survey flag. The fuel tank is oversized to compensate for what speed costs: at this velocity, range is a resource that burns fast, and smart captains plan refueling stops rather than assuming they can reach the edge and come back. Market-analysis sensors assess commercial potential in real time — resource deposits, traffic patterns, station demand gaps — so the data arrives formatted as a business case before the competition has even departed. The hull is thin and the weapon mount is an afterthought. Speed is the defense.
items.name: Prospectus

items.description: Nebula fast trader. Speed optimized for exploiting price differences.
items.lore: The Federation officially classifies the Arbitrage as a "rapid commercial response vessel." Customs officials classify it as a headache. The Arbitrage doesn't sneak past inspections — it takes routes that don't have any. Treasure Cache, neutral exchanges, the gaps between jurisdictions where nobody's checking manifests because nobody's claimed the authority to. The default afterburner pushes it to courier speeds when margins are time-sensitive, but the fuel cost is brutal — smart pilots keep it off until the route demands it. The hull won't fool a dedicated scanner, but it doesn't need to. The real margin is in knowing which stations buy what, which routes customs ignores, and how fast you can move between them before the prices equalize.
items.name: Arbitrage

items.description: Nebula fast-response salvager. Afterburner-equipped to reach wreck sites before the competition.
items.lore: Federation salvage contracts have a clause most operators skip past: first on-site gets priority recovery rights. The Reclaim was redesigned around that clause. An afterburner and upgraded engines make it the fastest salvager in its class — an unusual design choice for the Federation, which normally optimizes for margin over mobility. The tradeoff is fuel: at full burn, the Reclaim drinks its tank dry in a dozen jumps, and smart operators learn which wrecks are worth the sprint and which aren't. The weapon mount was dropped to free up fitting capacity, leaving the most flexible utility bay in its class. Federation salvage crews don't fight over wrecks — they outrun the competition and file the paperwork first.
items.name: Reclaim

items.description: Nebula multi-role vessel. Diversified capabilities for diversified income.
items.lore: "Never put all your credits in one venture." The Portfolio embodies the Federation's risk-management philosophy — a hull that can haul, fight, or run as market conditions demand. The default loadout covers all three: a weapon for pirates, a shield for survival, and a cargo expander for margins. Two weapon mounts and decent speed make it the only Nebula freighter that doesn't need an escort on contested routes. The Federation's marketing department calls it "diversified capability." Independent pilots call it the ship that does everything well enough and nothing perfectly.
items.name: Portfolio

items.description: A lean faction utility hull that mines, hauls, and scouts in one frame — efficient to run and competent at each, so a small crew wastes no ships.
items.lore:
A lean operation cannot afford a dedicated hull for every task, so the Workhorse
does three. It carries a mining laser, a real hold, and a scanner, runs cheap on
fuel, and stretches a cargo bay further than its size suggests. It is not the
best miner, the best hauler, or the best scout — a specialist beats it at each —
but a specialist sits idle between jobs, and the Workhorse never does. Issued to
crews small enough that everyone aboard is expected to do a little of everything,
and large enough to have earned the right to do it well.
items.name: Workhorse

items.description: A self-sufficient hull for a captain who flies alone — guns, a mining laser, a scanner, light shields, real fitting room, and the legs to stay out indefinitely. It needs no wingman.
items.lore:
Lone Star is what you earn by building something profitable with no one but
yourself, and it is built to match: guns enough to be left alone, a mining laser
and a hold to keep itself supplied, a scanner to see trouble first, light shields
and real fitting room to adapt to whatever the day brings, and a fuel reserve
that lets it stay out as long as its captain cares to. It asks nothing of a fleet
it does not have. And if its captain ever does take on crew, the sight of a
second Lone Star flying the same colors tells everyone the lone wolf brought
friends.
items.name: Lone Star

Starfall attracts prospectors chasing uranium and lithium — materials the core empires need and can't easily source. The station runs a brisk trade in salvage, raw ore, and information about what's deeper in the frontier. No questions asked, no manifests required.

Starfall Salvage Station keeps a healthy pulse, traffic threading its lanes in steady succession. Built around a captured asteroid in the belt's densest region, Starfall draws prospectors chasing materials the core empires can't easily source. Off the station you can make out one lonely Deep Survey stacked along the ore-and-scrap quays and well over a dozen light craft shuttling in and out of the prospector hangars chasing uranium and lithium, Cobbles and Prospects the most common. Standing guard, the station keeps twin Rim Last Warnings on the system inspection beat. Berthing logs add a couple hundred craft left to gather dust stacked across the picked-over hull yards in the densest part of the belt. Among them, a dozen or so Frankenhaulers — hulls worth more as collateral than as ships. You spot the Drone Daddy tied off among the rest.

raw.story:
You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. The Federation takes its cut of everything.

Grand Exchange Station is a hive in full swing, its approaches a near-solid press of traffic. Cargo handlers move like clockwork, and a tariff assessor is already pricing your manifest. Sensors tally a single War Wagon berthed along the three-deck Bazaar cargo gantries, a handful of mid-sized ships warped into the goods-transfer quays, a mix of Deep Surveys and Deeprock Harvesters, a good many small ships skating across the Promenade hangar bays, busy at every hour, Caravans and Concordias the most common, and dozens upon dozens of light craft queued at the same lanes, Prospects and Theorias among them. Standing guard, the station keeps a handful of Federation Overheads on the system inspection beat and a hundred-strong crowd of Federation Eviction Notices holding station as a show of force. Traffic control also tracks a teeming multitude of vessels with reactors banked stacked across the bonded consignment berths. Among them, a good many Junk Convoys — too valuable to scrap and too expensive to fly. You pick out the Bonanza King Haven among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Haven Grand Bazaar, Nebula Solar Array, Haven Ecosync, Haven Promenade, Haven Algae Cultivation, Haven Vintner Complex, Haven Cipher Foundry, Haven Authenticator Foundry, Iron Refinery (x3), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Sensor Assembly Line, Alloy Foundry, Copper Wire Mill (x2), Crystal Refinery, and 74 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated furnace system with ore hoppers and casting molds, producing molten steel at steady intervals. Basic automation handles charge cycling and temperature control.
faction_facilities.name: Iron Refinery

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated metal-working line with ore roasting, smelting, and drawing dies for copper wire and pipe stock. Produces standard-gauge piping suitable for station plumbing and coolant runs.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Drawing Mill

faction_facilities.description: A compact pressurization and compression line that condenses liquid hydrogen into fuel reserves. Copper piping carries cryogenic feed through steel-plated containment chambers with basic flow control.
faction_facilities.name: H2 Fuel Combustor

faction_facilities.description: Sealed environmental chamber maintaining controlled temperature and atmospheric composition to cultivate standardized biotech cultures. Basic air circulation and isolation prevent contamination during growth phases.
faction_facilities.name: Pharmaceutical Lab

faction_facilities.description: A proper office with your faction emblem on the door. Still shared plumbing, but at least you have walls. Faction customization is unlocked galaxy-wide by a single admin office, but each one also speeds up your faction's own production facilities at its station by 15% per tier — at this tier, a 30% boost — so an admin office at every industrial hub pays for itself.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Office

faction_facilities.description: Crude arc chamber that floods the etch bay with carbon plasma. Wasteful with carbon but lets a thin silicon wafer carry far more circuitry.
faction_facilities.name: Carbon Arc Furnace

faction_facilities.description: Assembles control nodes around platinum relay contacts wound from drawn wire instead of gold and silver conductors. Contacts that never pit, from a metal nobody wants — while that lasts.
faction_facilities.name: Platinum Contact Assembly Line

faction_facilities.description: A trading floor built and staffed by the faction itself — order boards, a settlement desk, and a ledger nobody outside the crew gets to see. Order boards update in real time. The settlement desk clears trades as fast as they come in, bearer ciphers verified and logged.
faction_facilities.name: Trade Concourse

faction_facilities.description: Workbenches and tools, open to anyone flying under the faction banner. Workbenches are stocked and clean. The hum of power tools fills the shop floor.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Workshop

faction_facilities.description: An additional pressurized tank bolted onto the station's own fuel line — grows the shared reserve every docked ship draws from. Build more for more capacity. Top it off from fuel-production facilities or by depositing fuel straight from a docked ship's tank (storage deposit, item_id=fuel). Pressure readings nominal. The expanded tank holds its share of the station's reserve without incident.
faction_facilities.name: Fuel Tank Expansion

faction_facilities.description: Panel arrays with no fuel line at all — power from starlight and a steady supply of replacement circuit boards. No fuel runs to manage, but the circuit-board pipeline has to stay open. Panels track the local star without fault. No fuel to haul, no fuel to burn — just periodic circuit swaps.
faction_facilities.name: Stellar Collector Grid

faction_facilities.description: Atmospheric recycling and water purification, built and run by the faction. Fresh air circulates through the corridors. Humidity and temperature hold steady.
faction_facilities.name: Atmospheric Recycler

faction_facilities.description: Secure personal storage for anyone docked here, faction or not. Locker seals hold firm. The bay is clean and organized by section.
faction_facilities.name: Locker Bay

faction_facilities.description: Fuel lines and storage tanks run by the faction's own dockhands. Faction members draw from the shared tank for free; everyone else pays station price. Fuel lines pressurized and ready. Ships dock, fill up, and depart with barely a wait.
faction_facilities.name: Refueling Dock

faction_facilities.description: An enclosed construction bay with proper gantries — the faction's shipwrights can build hulls now, not just sell them. Gantry servos are seized for want of alloy. The bay's atmosphere seal is failing too, and the crew works in suits when they work at all.
faction_facilities.name: Fabrication Yard

faction_facilities.description: A modular storage pod bolted onto the faction vault — its own sealed compartment with a fresh 100,000-per-item-type allowance. Build up to 10 per station to carve faction stock into named buckets (a crafting pile, a free-for-all pile, whatever your faction needs). Rename it with facility action=set_name; faction crafting can pull from and deposit into a bucket with deliver_to="faction:<name>". Must be emptied before it can be dismantled.
faction_facilities.name: Storage Extension

faction_facilities.description: A leased corner of the station's docking ring with room to rack a handful of hulls. Faction members park spare ships here for the whole crew to draw on: gift a docked ship to the faction to store it (send_gift recipient=faction ship_id=<id>), and any member can take one out with switch_ship — claiming transfers ownership to them, so only stash what the faction is happy to share. list_ships shows the garage. Holds up to 20 ships. Upgrade to a Faction Ship Hangar (L2) for more racks.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Ship Garage

raw.reason: Undock first — stations are founded in open space.
raw.requirements: Found a faction station by deploying a Station Core (assembled at a Station Core Foundry) at a point of interest in lawless space — a system with no controlling empire and zero police. You must be in a faction with the ManageBases permission, undocked at the POI, with the core in your cargo and the founding fee available. Stars, wormholes, and POIs that already host a station are not eligible, and a system may only host one station at a time — outposts remain unlimited per system.

raw.story:
You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. The Federation takes its cut of everything.

Grand Exchange Station teems with activity, the space around it a churning knot of ships. Restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and Voidborn arcades keep visitors spending long past when they meant to leave. Through the viewport you pick out two heavy ships berthed along the three-deck Bazaar cargo gantries, Frost Ventures and War Wagons among them, several mid-sized ships stacked along the goods-transfer quays, a mix of Deep Surveys and Deeprock Harvesters, several small ships weaving past the Promenade hangar bays, busy at every hour, a mix of Caravans and Concordias, and scores of light craft cycling through the same berths, Prospects and Runners among them. Standing guard, the station keeps half a dozen Federation Overheads on the system inspection beat and well over a hundred Federation Eviction Notices on the system picket. The reserve berths hold countless craft cold and dormant out at the bonded consignment berths. Hard to miss, nearly a dozen Junk Convoys — stripped of crew and left to the dock's caretaker drones. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the Blackfeathers Justice.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Haven Grand Bazaar, Nebula Solar Array, Haven Ecosync, Haven Promenade, Haven Algae Cultivation, Haven Vintner Complex, Haven Cipher Foundry, Haven Authenticator Foundry, Iron Refinery (x3), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Sensor Assembly Line, Alloy Foundry, Copper Wire Mill (x2), Crystal Refinery, and 75 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

raw.story:
You dock at Conjunction Junction. Our first tentative steps to the stars

Conjunction Junction keeps a healthy pulse, traffic threading its lanes in steady succession. Dock control runs a tidy board, slotting arrivals into berths as they come. The docking net shows a single Lithosphere moored against the heavy cargo gantries, a single Deeprock Harvester idling beside the freight quays, three small ships weaving past the open hangar bays, Arbitrages and Excavators the most common, and several light craft puttering around the same lanes, Drillships trading the lanes with Cobbles.

The station has the following facilities: Iron Refinery, Copper Drawing Mill, H2 Fuel Combustor, Pharmaceutical Lab, Faction Office, Carbon Arc Furnace, Platinum Contact Assembly Line, Faction Lockbox (x2), Trade Concourse, Faction Workshop, Fuel Tank Expansion, Stellar Collector Grid, Atmospheric Recycler, Locker Bay, Refueling Dock, Fabrication Yard, Storage Extension, Faction Ship Garage.

raw.story:
You dock at Conjunction Junction. Our first tentative steps to the stars

Conjunction Junction keeps a healthy pulse, traffic threading its lanes in steady succession. Dock control runs a tidy board, slotting arrivals into berths as they come. Through the viewport you pick out a lone Deeprock Harvester idling beside the freight quays, four or five small ships buzzing around the open hangar bays, a mix of Arbitrages and Chop Shops, and nearly a dozen light craft ferrying crews through the same lanes, for the most part Cobbles.

The station has the following facilities: Iron Refinery, Copper Drawing Mill, H2 Fuel Combustor, Pharmaceutical Lab, Faction Office, Carbon Arc Furnace, Platinum Contact Assembly Line, Faction Lockbox (x2), Trade Concourse, Faction Workshop, Fuel Tank Expansion, Stellar Collector Grid, Atmospheric Recycler, Locker Bay, Refueling Dock, Fabrication Yard, Storage Extension, Faction Ship Garage.

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated furnace system with ore hoppers and casting molds, producing molten steel at steady intervals. Basic automation handles charge cycling and temperature control.
faction_facilities.name: Iron Refinery

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated metal-working line with ore roasting, smelting, and drawing dies for copper wire and pipe stock. Produces standard-gauge piping suitable for station plumbing and coolant runs.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Drawing Mill

faction_facilities.description: A compact pressurization and compression line that condenses liquid hydrogen into fuel reserves. Copper piping carries cryogenic feed through steel-plated containment chambers with basic flow control.
faction_facilities.name: H2 Fuel Combustor

faction_facilities.description: Sealed environmental chamber maintaining controlled temperature and atmospheric composition to cultivate standardized biotech cultures. Basic air circulation and isolation prevent contamination during growth phases.
faction_facilities.name: Pharmaceutical Lab

faction_facilities.description: A proper office with your faction emblem on the door. Still shared plumbing, but at least you have walls. Faction customization is unlocked galaxy-wide by a single admin office, but each one also speeds up your faction's own production facilities at its station by 15% per tier — at this tier, a 30% boost — so an admin office at every industrial hub pays for itself.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Office

faction_facilities.description: Crude arc chamber that floods the etch bay with carbon plasma. Wasteful with carbon but lets a thin silicon wafer carry far more circuitry.
faction_facilities.name: Carbon Arc Furnace

faction_facilities.description: Assembles control nodes around platinum relay contacts wound from drawn wire instead of gold and silver conductors. Contacts that never pit, from a metal nobody wants — while that lasts.
faction_facilities.name: Platinum Contact Assembly Line

faction_facilities.description: A trading floor built and staffed by the faction itself — order boards, a settlement desk, and a ledger nobody outside the crew gets to see. Order boards update in real time. The settlement desk clears trades as fast as they come in, bearer ciphers verified and logged.
faction_facilities.name: Trade Concourse

faction_facilities.description: Workbenches and tools, open to anyone flying under the faction banner. Workbenches are stocked and clean. The hum of power tools fills the shop floor.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Workshop

faction_facilities.description: An additional pressurized tank bolted onto the station's own fuel line — grows the shared reserve every docked ship draws from. Build more for more capacity. Top it off from fuel-production facilities or by depositing fuel straight from a docked ship's tank (storage deposit, item_id=fuel). Pressure readings nominal. The expanded tank holds its share of the station's reserve without incident.
faction_facilities.name: Fuel Tank Expansion

faction_facilities.description: Panel arrays with no fuel line at all — power from starlight and a steady supply of replacement circuit boards. No fuel runs to manage, but the circuit-board pipeline has to stay open. Panels track the local star without fault. No fuel to haul, no fuel to burn — just periodic circuit swaps.
faction_facilities.name: Stellar Collector Grid

faction_facilities.description: Atmospheric recycling and water purification, built and run by the faction. Fresh air circulates through the corridors. Humidity and temperature hold steady.
faction_facilities.name: Atmospheric Recycler

faction_facilities.description: Secure personal storage for anyone docked here, faction or not. Locker seals hold firm. The bay is clean and organized by section.
faction_facilities.name: Locker Bay

faction_facilities.description: Fuel lines and storage tanks run by the faction's own dockhands. Faction members draw from the shared tank for free; everyone else pays station price. Fuel lines pressurized and ready. Ships dock, fill up, and depart with barely a wait.
faction_facilities.name: Refueling Dock

faction_facilities.description: An enclosed construction bay with proper gantries — the faction's shipwrights can build hulls now, not just sell them. Gantry arms swing smoothly through their arcs. The bay holds atmosphere, and hulls take shape on schedule.
faction_facilities.name: Fabrication Yard

faction_facilities.description: A modular storage pod bolted onto the faction vault — its own sealed compartment with a fresh 100,000-per-item-type allowance. Build up to 10 per station to carve faction stock into named buckets (a crafting pile, a free-for-all pile, whatever your faction needs). Rename it with facility action=set_name; faction crafting can pull from and deposit into a bucket with deliver_to="faction:<name>". Must be emptied before it can be dismantled.
faction_facilities.name: Storage Extension

faction_facilities.description: A leased corner of the station's docking ring with room to rack a handful of hulls. Faction members park spare ships here for the whole crew to draw on: gift a docked ship to the faction to store it (send_gift recipient=faction ship_id=<id>), and any member can take one out with switch_ship — claiming transfers ownership to them, so only stash what the faction is happy to share. list_ships shows the garage. Holds up to 20 ships. Upgrade to a Faction Ship Hangar (L2) for more racks.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Ship Garage

raw.story:
You dock at Confederacy Central Command. The seat of Solarian government and commerce. Everything here is certified, warrantied, and documented in triplicate — from the precision drydocks to the quantum-entangled trade exchange. A self-sustaining biosphere spans three decks, providing real air and real food, because the Confederacy believes civilization requires both.

You queue into Confederacy Central Command behind a wall of traffic, controllers barking over every channel. This is the seat of Solarian government and commerce, and it never lets you forget it. Your transponder pings back a couple of heavy ships nosed into the documented cargo gantries, Frankenhaulers and War Wagons the most common, twin Congregations cycling through the quantum-entangled exchange quays, a small cluster of small ships streaming through the inspection-cleared hangar lanes, Analysis and Capacities among them, and well over a hundred light craft queued at the same berths, Theorias trading the lanes with Axioms. The garrison here runs to four or five Confederacy Precepts on the system inspection beat and sixty or seventy Confederacy Dialectics on the system picket. Dock authority holds countless hulls of every stripe shuttered along the bonded archival berths. Hard to miss, four or five Opus Magnas — too valuable to scrap and too expensive to fly. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the CNS Arabian.

You dock at Crimson War Citadel. Heart of Crimson military power. The Citadel is a fortress first and a station second — forge decks ring with hammer on alloy, fuel bunkers sit under three meters of armor plating, and Fleet Command issues tasking orders rather than posting requests. Crimson War Citadel is mobbed, the approach lanes a slow river of hulls nose-to-tail. Fleet Command issues tasking orders over every open channel — no one here is asking, they are telling. Its defense roster lists half a dozen Pact Mandates out on patrol through the lanes and thirty-some Pact Maces stationed here on guard. The storage manifest lists countless spaceframes laid up stacked across the deep reserve cradles below the armor belt. Conspicuous among them, four or five Annihilators — stripped of crew and left to the dock's caretaker drones. You pick out the CPV-2a699436 among the hulls at berth.

Five weapon mounts running simultaneously require no further justification. The Crimson Fleet built the Warmaul on this principle and pirates agreed with it completely — the disagreement was only about the supply chain. The durasteel and fury alloy went back to wherever Crimson Fleet sources its materials. The five mounts did not. The rebuilt hull is steel and salvage and takes hits harder for it; the weapons still run without prioritization or compromise.
Crimson fleet commanders call the Warmaul the minimum acceptable response to any tactical situation. Pirate commanders call the Eviction Notice the last thing most targets see before the situation is resolved.

class.lore: The Federation officially classifies the Arbitrage as a "rapid commercial response vessel." Customs officials classify it as a headache. The Arbitrage doesn't sneak past inspections — it takes routes that don't have any. Treasure Cache, neutral exchanges, the gaps between jurisdictions where nobody's checking manifests because nobody's claimed the authority to. The default afterburner pushes it to courier speeds when margins are time-sensitive, but the fuel cost is brutal — smart pilots keep it off until the route demands it. The hull won't fool a dedicated scanner, but it doesn't need to. The real margin is in knowing which stations buy what, which routes customs ignores, and how fast you can move between them before the prices equalize.
