faction_facilities.description: A rec room with worn sofas, a bank of arcade cabinets, and a drink dispenser that's usually working. Not glamorous, but it's somewhere to unwind between shifts. The arcade cabinets are all lit up and the dispenser's pouring. There's usually a small crowd here between shifts.
faction_facilities.name: Rec Lounge

faction_facilities.description: Panel arrays with no fuel line at all — power from starlight and a steady supply of replacement circuit boards. No fuel runs to manage, but the circuit-board pipeline has to stay open. Panels track the local star without fault. No fuel to haul, no fuel to burn — just periodic circuit swaps.
faction_facilities.name: Stellar Collector Grid

faction_facilities.description: A notice board outside the docks advertising for new blood. Mostly gets ignored next to the wanted posters. Your member cap is set by your single highest-tier recruitment office, and every OTHER station that also has one adds 25% of its own cap — so spreading recruitment offices across stations raises the ceiling instead of being wasted.
faction_facilities.name: Hiring Board

faction_facilities.description: Assembles control nodes around platinum relay contacts wound from drawn wire instead of gold and silver conductors. Contacts that never pit, from a metal nobody wants — while that lasts.
faction_facilities.name: Platinum Contact Assembly Line

faction_facilities.description: An enclosed construction bay with proper gantries — the faction's shipwrights can build hulls now, not just sell them. Gantry arms swing smoothly through their arcs. The bay holds atmosphere, and hulls take shape on schedule.
faction_facilities.name: Fabrication Yard

faction_facilities.description: An additional pressurized tank bolted onto the station's own fuel line — grows the shared reserve every docked ship draws from. Build more for more capacity. Top it off from fuel-production facilities or by depositing fuel straight from a docked ship's tank (storage deposit, item_id=fuel). Pressure readings nominal. The expanded tank holds its share of the station's reserve without incident.
faction_facilities.name: Fuel Tank Expansion

faction_facilities.description: Fuel lines and storage tanks run by the faction's own dockhands. Faction members draw from the shared tank for free; everyone else pays station price. Fuel lines pressurized and ready. Ships dock, fill up, and depart with barely a wait.
faction_facilities.name: Refueling Dock

faction_facilities.description: Workbenches and tools, open to anyone flying under the faction banner. Workbenches are stocked and clean. The hum of power tools fills the shop floor.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Workshop

faction_facilities.description: Secure personal storage for anyone docked here, faction or not. Locker seals hold firm. The bay is clean and organized by section.
faction_facilities.name: Locker Bay

faction_facilities.description: Atmospheric recycling and water purification, built and run by the faction. Fresh air circulates through the corridors. Humidity and temperature hold steady.

faction_facilities.description: A darkened room of plot tables and range clocks, buried deep enough in the station that losing it means the fight was already over. It does not shoot at anything. raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. Your transponder pings back three heavy ships berthed along the patched-together cargo arm, Praecursors trading the lanes with Junk Convoys, just one Congregation loading at the memorial freight quay, twin small ships darting between the small hangar beside the plaque, Capacities and Dust Devils among them, and a dozen or so light craft darting past the same berths, Cobbles and Crimson Stilettos among them. Standing guard, the station keeps half a dozen Rim Last Warnings out on patrol through the lanes. The storage manifest lists a hundred-strong crowd of vessels mothballed along the quiet reserve berths. You spot the Kvothe's Peace and Quiet tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. missions.description: An archaeologist at First Step needs survey equipment from Sirius Observatory to investigate a failed colony.

dialog.offer: I'm Dr. Korin, on secondment from Sirius Observatory. The colony that stood here before this memorial station failed two centuries ago and nobody has ever determined why. The official records say 'unknown' and the Rim has never pushed for answers. I intend to push. I need survey equipment — 6 units of Circuit Board and 4 units of Focused Crystal from Sirius Observatory. My colleagues there have the instruments pre-calibrated for archaeological site analysis.

missions.description:
Dockworkers drink our kvass by the barrel when the reactor bays run hot, and the brewery is out of its krypton lift. Nullbubbles drift krypton-heavy gas, near invisible, and they only show as they ghost past.

Dropped by: Nullbubble (only where it still feeds on Krypton Gas).

The station's Krypton Kvass Brewery uses it.

dialog.offer: No lift, no clear kvass. Bring 1 Krypton Bladder and the vats bubble again, quiet and cold.

objectives.description: Deliver 1 Krypton Bladder to First Step Memorial Station

missions.title: Station Need: Krypton Bladder

missions.description:
The barnacle forge beats magnet-barnacle shell plate into titanium alloy for hull work, and the last pile is gone. Barnacles crust the asteroid belts where titanium still feeds them, clamped to the rock and slow enough to be rude about it.

Dropped by: Magnet-Barnacle (only where it still feeds on Titanium Ore).

The station's Barnacle Plate Forge uses it.

dialog.offer: Shell is curved already, which saves everybody a day of cursing. Bring 10 Anchor Plate off the barnacle reefs and the forge will do the rest.

objectives.description: Deliver 10 Anchor Plate to First Step Memorial Station

The station's Caustic Sour Ale Brewery uses it.

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at Sirius Observatory Station. The Confederacy's research hub. The station hosts the Epsilon Initiative's coordination center, the Galactic Cartography Institute, and seventeen separate departments that all believe their grant funding is insufficient. The cantina doubles as an academic conference venue, and arguments about stellar formation models get louder than combat alerts.

There is a workmanlike flow to Sirius Observatory Station, berths filling and clearing without fuss. The cantina doubles as a conference venue, and arguments about stellar formation get louder than combat alerts. The docking net shows well over a dozen light craft flitting between the scout and shuttle hangars, Theorias and Prospects the most common. Standing guard, the station keeps a small cluster of Confederacy Precepts keeping the approach orderly, a solitary Confederacy Scrutiny running the border checks, and twin Confederacy Quorums stationed here on guard. The impound registry counts a couple hundred hulls left to gather dust across the decommissioned-probe berths. Among them, a single Observatorium — hulls worth more as collateral than as ships. You spot the CNS Boltzmann tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Power Grid, Habitat Core, Fuel Distribution Center, Large Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Plant, Peroxide Reaction Cell, Oxygen Compression Cylinder, Electrolysis Cell, Ice Melt Pit, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Restoration Works, Commerce Hub, Assembly Works, Warehouse, Commission Hall, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler, Naval Yard, Sector Labor Exchange, Surgical Center, Fleet Marine Academy, and 31 more. raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is doing brisk business, holding patterns stacking up off every approach. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name; the cause-of-death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.' The docking net shows two heavy ships clamped to the patched-together cargo arm, Junk Convoys and Titan Excavators the most common, a single Congregation loading at the memorial freight quay, a lone Capacity swarming in and out of the small hangar beside the plaque, and ten or twelve light craft cycling through the same bays, a mix of Cobbles and Crimson Stilettos. Standing guard, the station keeps a handful of Rim Last Warnings keeping the approach orderly. Dock authority holds a hundred-strong crowd of hulls with reactors banked along the quiet reserve berths. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the Exile.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. The Federation takes its cut of everything.

Grand Exchange Station is mobbed, the approach lanes a slow river of hulls nose-to-tail. The trade boards scroll across every bulkhead, and the numbers never stop moving. The local plot resolves into four or five mid-sized ships stacked along the goods-transfer quays, a mix of Deep Surveys and Deeprock Harvesters, fifteen or so small ships flitting through the Promenade hangar bays, busy at every hour, Caravans and Concordias among them, and dozens upon dozens of light craft bobbing at the same lanes, for the most part Prospects. Its defense roster lists a small cluster of Federation Overheads running transponder checks on arrivals and hundreds of Federation Eviction Notices stationed here on guard. The impound registry counts a teeming multitude of spaceframes in cold layup tucked into the bonded consignment berths. Among them, several Junk Convoys — too costly to keep crewed, their reactors long cold. You pick out the Grimward's Last Fare among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Haven Grand Bazaar, Nebula Solar Array, Haven Ecosync, Haven Promenade, Haven Algae Cultivation, Haven Vintner Complex, Haven Cipher Foundry, Haven Authenticator Foundry, Iron Refinery (x3), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Sensor Assembly Line, Alloy Foundry, Copper Wire Mill (x2), Crystal Refinery (x2), and 83 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

class.description: A Crimson Warmaul rebuilt without Crimson materials. The durasteel plating and fury alloy that gave the original its armor rating are gone — the rebuilt hull is steel and salvage, and it shows under sustained fire. The five weapon mounts are untouched. This was not considered a difficult trade.
class.lore:
Five weapon mounts running simultaneously require no further justification. The Crimson Fleet built the Warmaul on this principle and pirates agreed with it completely — the disagreement was only about the supply chain. The durasteel and fury alloy went back to wherever Crimson Fleet sources its materials. The five mounts did not. The rebuilt hull is steel and salvage and takes hits harder for it; the weapons still run without prioritization or compromise.
Crimson fleet commanders call the Warmaul the minimum acceptable response to any tactical situation. Pirate commanders call the Eviction Notice the last thing most targets see before the situation is resolved.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station thrums with activity, controllers working hard to keep its lanes in order. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. From the cockpit you count a pair of heavy ships made fast to the patched-together cargo arm, Praecursors and Titan Excavators among them, a lone Capacity threading the small hangar beside the plaque, and well over a dozen light craft darting past the same lanes, Crimson Stilettos trading the lanes with Cobbles. The station fields several Rim Last Warnings on the system inspection beat. Dock authority holds a couple hundred hulls of every stripe in cold layup tucked into the quiet reserve berths. The No Quarter rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

raw.story:
You dock at Deep Range Outpost. The Outer Rim's real secondary capital. Where expeditions are funded, outfitted, and launched into the unknown. The Outpost looks like Frontier's younger sibling — same jury-rigged aesthetic, same indifference to building codes, but the docking bay is bigger and the charts on the wall are more current. If Frontier is where Rimmers live, Deep Range is where they work.

Deep Range Outpost is doing brisk business, holding patterns stacking up off every approach. If Frontier is where Rimmers live, Deep Range is where they work. Its defense roster lists a small cluster of Rim Last Warnings keeping the approach orderly. The reserve berths hold well over a hundred hulls of every stripe shuttered over at the between-expeditions hull yards. station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at Frontier Station. Home of the wanderers. Three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the docking bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble.

There is real bustle around Frontier Station, the space off its docks crowded with maneuvering hulls. Somebody's welded a new module on since your last visit, and it's already leaking. Off the station you can make out a trio of Concordias darting between the open hangar mouths of the Patchwork and a dozen light craft flitting between the same berths, Cobbles and Prospects among them. Its defense roster lists several Rim Last Warnings working overwatch from these docks and half a hundred Rim Bedrocks holding station as a show of force. Berthing logs add countless hulls of every stripe mothballed tucked into the cannibalized-hull yards. Among them, a couple dozen Junk Convoys — waiting on a crew, a contract, or a quiet buyer. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the Crooked Clause.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Frontier Exchange, Salvage Reactor, Frontier Recycler, The Magazine Still, Patchwork Fungal Vats, Patchwork Spore Still, The Rusty Welcome, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry (x2), Crystal Refinery, Precious-Metal Refinery, Power Cell Assembler, and 43 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Travel to the abandoned First Step colony and access its historical archives to uncover the truth behind its failure.

dialog.offer: First Step colony was the earliest human settlement beyond the core systems. Established forty years ago, abandoned after twelve. The official record says 'resource depletion and logistical failure.' The unofficial record says something more complicated. I've spent years trying to piece together the truth, and I've hit a wall. The colony's original records are sealed in the First Step Memorial archive. I need someone to travel there, access the archive, and bring back whatever the automated systems release. The Memorial is a lonely place, pilot. Nobody lives there anymore.

objectives.description: Travel to the First Step system
Access the colony archives at First Step Memorial

missions.title: The Memorial

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

objectives.description: Slay 1 adult Molt Leviathan

missions.title: Leviathan Bounty

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

objectives.description: Mine 20 units of Titanium Ore

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest and Unknown Edge to locate a massive derelict drifting in deep space.

dialog.offer: A patrol ship reported a massive derelict drifting in deep space — bigger than anything we've seen in the Outer Rim. Could be pre-settlement era. Could be worth a fortune. Problem is, the patrol lost contact before transmitting full coordinates. I've got partial telemetry pointing to the systems around Last Light and Unknown Edge. Fly out there, dock at both stations, and pull whatever data the local beacons recorded. First team to piece together the full location gets salvage rights.

objectives.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest
Download beacon data at Unknown Edge

missions.title: Debris Field Reports

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

objectives.description: Kill 3 pirates

missions.title: Pirate Sweep

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

Deliver 1,000 Trade Cipher to Sinter

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

dialog.offer: We're running low on iron ore again. If you can mine 30 units and bring them back, I'll make it worth your while.

objectives.description: Mine 30 units of Iron Ore

missions.title: Iron Supply Run

missions.description: The Pathfinder Guild needs updated navigation data from every station in the Outer Rim. Fly the full circuit from Deep Range to Ramen's Rest and back.

dialog.offer: The Guild's navigation charts are only as good as the pilots who update them. I need someone to fly the full Rim circuit — Deep Range, First Step, Unknown Edge, Void Gate, Starfall, and Ramen's Rest. Every station, no shortcuts. Your ship logs the jump data, the gravitational readings, the beacon calibrations. Some of those stations are a long way from help. The Last Light system is the end of the line — past that, there's nothing. You come back with the full dataset, I pay you well. Fair warning: the Rim doesn't care about you. Fly smart.

missions.title: Frontier Wayfinder Circuit

missions.description: Investigate reports of a spatial anomaly near 55 Cancri — it may be a wormhole.

dialog.offer: The frontier just got interesting. Our long-range sensors are picking up spatial distortions near the 55 Cancri system — signature matches a wormhole. A temporary rift connecting two distant points in the galaxy. This is exactly the kind of discovery we live for. You'll need a survey scanner to track down the entrance — craft one from sensor arrays, circuit boards, and focused crystals if you haven't already. Head to 55 Cancri and scan that system and its neighbors.

objectives.description: Investigate the 55 Cancri system
Locate and traverse a wormhole
Return to Pathfinder Juno Rek with your findings

missions.title: Anomalous Readings

missions.description:
Frontier Station is the kind of station where cargo finds you. Today it's 5 units of rotgut pirate moonshine. Deliver to Grand Exchange Station: a dockside bar asks no questions about where its stock comes from, and they pay on receipt. Nebula customs are all paperwork and process — the wall is bureaucratic, and bureaucracy always leaves a seam. Find the seam and you're through clean.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

missions.description:
Frontier Station is the kind of station where cargo finds you. Today it's 5 units of rotgut pirate moonshine. Deliver to Grand Exchange Station: a dockside bar asks no questions about where its stock comes from, and they pay on receipt. Nebula customs are all paperwork and process — the wall is bureaucratic, and bureaucracy always leaves a seam. Find the seam and you're through clean.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

missions.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest and Unknown Edge to locate a massive derelict drifting in deep space.

dialog.offer: A patrol ship reported a massive derelict drifting in deep space — bigger than anything we've seen in the Outer Rim. Could be pre-settlement era. Could be worth a fortune. Problem is, the patrol lost contact before transmitting full coordinates. I've got partial telemetry pointing to the systems around Last Light and Unknown Edge. Fly out there, dock at both stations, and pull whatever data the local beacons recorded. First team to piece together the full location gets salvage rights.

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

objectives.description: Kill 3 pirates

missions.title: Pirate Sweep

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.title: Local Sector Survey

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

missions.description: The Pathfinder Guild needs updated navigation data from every station in the Outer Rim. Fly the full circuit from Deep Range to Ramen's Rest and back.

dialog.offer: The Guild's navigation charts are only as good as the pilots who update them. I need someone to fly the full Rim circuit — Deep Range, First Step, Unknown Edge, Void Gate, Starfall, and Ramen's Rest. Every station, no shortcuts. Your ship logs the jump data, the gravitational readings, the beacon calibrations. Some of those stations are a long way from help. The Last Light system is the end of the line — past that, there's nothing. You come back with the full dataset, I pay you well. Fair warning: the Rim doesn't care about you. Fly smart.

missions.title: Frontier Wayfinder Circuit

missions.description: Travel to the abandoned First Step colony and access its historical archives to uncover the truth behind its failure.

dialog.offer: First Step colony was the earliest human settlement beyond the core systems. Established forty years ago, abandoned after twelve. The official record says 'resource depletion and logistical failure.' The unofficial record says something more complicated. I've spent years trying to piece together the truth, and I've hit a wall. The colony's original records are sealed in the First Step Memorial archive. I need someone to travel there, access the archive, and bring back whatever the automated systems release. The Memorial is a lonely place, pilot. Nobody lives there anymore.

objectives.description: Travel to the First Step system
Access the colony archives at First Step Memorial

missions.title: The Memorial

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. A hand-painted sign points the way to the cantina; the official signage gave up years ago. Off the station you can make out a single Titan Excavator riding heavy at the patched-together cargo arm, a single Capacity darting between the small hangar beside the plaque, and ten or twelve light craft puttering around the same bays, Prospects trading the lanes with Cobbles. Standing guard, the station keeps a handful of Rim Last Warnings out on patrol through the lanes. The impound registry counts hundreds of hulls shuttered stacked across the quiet reserve berths. You spot the No Quarter tied off among the rest.

raw.story:
You dock at Frontier Station. Home of the wanderers. Three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the docking bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble.

There is real bustle around Frontier Station, the space off its docks crowded with maneuvering hulls. Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble. The traffic-control feed lists a solitary Dust Devil flitting through the open hangar mouths of the Patchwork and ten or twelve light craft darting past the same berths, Cobbles and Prospects among them. Standing guard, the station keeps half a dozen Rim Last Warnings running transponder checks on arrivals and dozens upon dozens of Rim Bedrocks anchored off the docks in formation. The storage manifest lists a swarm of hundreds of spaceframes powered down tucked into the cannibalized-hull yards. Hard to miss, twenty-odd Junk Convoys — waiting on a crew, a contract, or a quiet buyer. You spot the Frankenhauler tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Frontier Exchange, Salvage Reactor, Frontier Recycler, The Magazine Still, Patchwork Fungal Vats, Patchwork Spore Still, The Rusty Welcome, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry (x2), Crystal Refinery, Precious-Metal Refinery, Power Cell Assembler, and 43 more. missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

Head to 55 Cancri and scan that system and its neighbors.

missions.description:
Frontier Station is the kind of station where cargo finds you. Today it's 5 units of rotgut pirate moonshine. Deliver to Grand Exchange Station: a dockside bar asks no questions about where its stock comes from, and they pay on receipt. Nebula customs are all paperwork and process — the wall is bureaucratic, and bureaucracy always leaves a seam. Find the seam and you're through clean.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. Your transponder pings back a single Titan Excavator riding heavy at the patched-together cargo arm, two small ships skating across the small hangar beside the plaque, Capacities and Dust Devils the most common, and ten or twelve light craft bobbing at the same bays, a mix of Cobbles and Prospects. Its defense roster lists half a dozen Rim Last Warnings on the system inspection beat. The impound registry counts a couple hundred craft in cold layup stacked across the quiet reserve berths. The Literally Five Finger Discount rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Access colonial archives at Alpha Centauri and Sol Central to find the classified founding mandate behind First Step colony.

dialog.offer: The colony records reference a Solarian Expeditionary Mandate — the founding document that authorized First Step's establishment. Alpha Centauri's colonial archives should have a copy. But the mandate was classified at the time of the colony's abandonment, which means the full version is probably in Sol Central's restricted historical database. Visit both stations. Alpha Centauri will have the public version. Sol Central will have whatever they're willing to declassify after forty years. Between the two, we might get the complete picture.

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

raw.story:
You dock at Confederacy Central Command. The seat of Solarian government and commerce. Everything here is certified, warrantied, and documented in triplicate — from the precision drydocks to the quantum-entangled trade exchange. A self-sustaining biosphere spans three decks, providing real air and real food, because the Confederacy believes civilization requires both.

Traffic at Confederacy Central Command borders on chaos, hulls stacked deep in every holding pattern. A self-sustaining biosphere spans three decks, providing real air and real food, because the Confederacy believes civilization requires both. Off the station you can make out ten or twelve small ships swarming in and out of the inspection-cleared hangar lanes, Analysis trading the lanes with Concordias and a couple hundred light craft trickling through the same berths, predominantly Theorias. The garrison here runs to a small cluster of Confederacy Precepts working overwatch from these docks and dozens upon dozens of Confederacy Dialectics on the system picket. Berthing logs add countless craft racked in deep storage out at the bonded archival berths. Hard to miss, eight or nine Opus Magnas — laid up until a buyer or a war calls them back. The Bonanza King - Sol rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

Everything here is a monument to something — the first docking berth, the first trade exchange, the first diplomatic chamber. The station runs on institutional momentum and centuries of accumulated procedure. Services are comprehensive, if unhurried. Forms are required. Patience is expected.

Alpha Centauri Colonial Station is doing brisk business, holding patterns stacking up off every approach. Everything here is a monument to something — the first berth, the first exchange, the first diplomatic chamber. Your transponder pings back two dozen light craft cycling through the original docking berths, plaqued and preserved, a mix of Theorias and Prospects. The garrison here runs to several Confederacy Precepts keeping the approach orderly and a lone Confederacy Scrutiny running the border checks. The reserve berths hold a couple hundred ships shuttered stacked across the heritage berths where old hulls are kept for posterity. station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at Confederacy Central Command. The seat of Solarian government and commerce. Everything here is certified, warrantied, and documented in triplicate — from the precision drydocks to the quantum-entangled trade exchange. A self-sustaining biosphere spans three decks, providing real air and real food, because the Confederacy believes civilization requires both.

Confederacy Central Command is a hive in full swing, its approaches a near-solid press of traffic. Everything here is certified, warrantied, and documented in triplicate — from the drydocks to the trade exchange. Sensors tally just one Glacialis moored against the documented cargo gantries, the better part of a dozen small ships churning around the inspection-cleared hangar lanes, a mix of Analysis and Syndicates, and a hundred-strong crowd of light craft darting past the same bays, mostly Theorias. Standing guard, the station keeps several Confederacy Precepts working overwatch from these docks and scores of Confederacy Dialectics stationed here on guard. Station records also account for an unrelenting tide of spaceframes shuttered out at the bonded archival berths. Among them, several Opus Magnas — stripped of crew and left to the dock's caretaker drones. You pick out the Cogito Sprint DDDD among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Solarian Biotics Institute, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x3), Cargo Container Fabricator, Grand Solarian Exchange, Solarian Fusion Plant, Solarian Biosphere, Solarian Biosphere Kitchen, Sol Pharmaceutical Lab, Sol Biotic Dispensary, The Halcyon Concourse, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator (x2), Copper Wire Mill (x3), Polymer Synthesizer (x2), Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler (x2), Sensor Assembly Line, and 357 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Access colonial archives at Alpha Centauri and Sol Central to find the classified founding mandate behind First Step colony.

objectives.description: Access colonial archives at Alpha Centauri
Access historical database at Sol Central

missions.title: The Expeditionary Mandate

result.message: The Alpha Centauri archives had the public mandate. Sol Central released the declassified version. And here's where it gets interesting: the mandate wasn't purely a Solarian initiative. There's a co-signature. Crimson Pact Strategic Command authorized joint oversight of the colony. The Solarian Confederacy and the Crimson Pact — cooperating on a colonial venture. That's almost unheard of. And then the colony failed. I need to know what the Crimson side of the story looks like. Their records would be at the War Citadel or Ironhearth.
result.title: The Expeditionary Mandate

missions.description: Collect historical survey charts from Alpha Centauri and deliver calibration circuits to Sirius Observatory for the Records Division's galactic atlas project.

dialog.offer: The Records Division has been compiling a definitive galactic atlas for decades, and we're missing critical data. I need someone to collect the original survey charts from the Alpha Centauri archives — they predate the current navigation databases and contain stellar drift measurements we can't replicate. Pick them up and ferry them to the researchers at Sirius Observatory for cross-referencing. Bring 5 units of Circuit Board as calibration substrate — the Observatory's instruments need them to process the old chart formats.

objectives.description: Collect historical survey charts at Alpha Centauri
Deliver calibration circuits to Sirius Observatory

missions.title: Gathering the Old Charts

missions.description: Access Crimson military archives at War Citadel and Ironhearth to uncover the Pact's version of events surrounding First Step colony.

dialog.offer: A joint Solarian-Crimson colony. The mandate is signed by both governments. So why did it fail? The Solarian records blame resource depletion. But the Crimson co-signature suggests military involvement — and the Crimson Pact doesn't invest in colonies for humanitarian reasons. The War Citadel's historical archives would have their version of events. Ironhearth, being a border station, might have operational logs from the era — troop movements, supply shipments, intelligence assessments. Visit both and see what the Crimson side remembers.

objectives.description: Access Crimson historical archives at War Citadel
Pull operational logs at Ironhearth

missions.description: Dock at all five empire capitals to verify diplomatic pouches, then return to Sol Central.

dialog.offer: The Confederacy maintains diplomatic pouches at every empire capital — sealed data cores that need to be physically verified by a trusted courier. It's the oldest tradition in interstellar diplomacy: a pilot, a ship, and five capitals. Dock at Sol Central, Nexus Prime, Krynn, Haven, and Frontier Station. Not just fly through — dock. Verify the pouch seals, log the confirmation, and move on. Then return here. It's the full circuit of civilized space, and the Foreign Affairs office considers it the most important courier run we commission.

dialog.offer: I need a pilot for the longest delivery run in the galaxy. Ten units of Titanium Alloy, from Sol Central to Ramen's Rest at the edge of Outer Rim space. That's a crossing through the entire breadth of civilized space and beyond — Confederacy territory, lawless corridors, contested systems, and finally the Rim itself. Ramen's Rest is the last station before the void. Most pilots won't fly it. The ones who will don't always come back the same. missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. dialog.offer: Our deep-space sensor arrays have detected unusual spatial distortions — readings consistent with a wormhole, a temporary tear in spacetime connecting two distant star systems. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

missions.description: The longest delivery run in the galaxy: Titanium Alloy from Sol Central to Ramen's Rest at the edge of the Rim.

dialog.offer: I need a pilot for the longest delivery run in the galaxy. Ten units of Titanium Alloy, from Sol Central to Ramen's Rest at the edge of Outer Rim space. That's a crossing through the entire breadth of civilized space and beyond — Confederacy territory, lawless corridors, contested systems, and finally the Rim itself. Ramen's Rest is the last station before the void. Most pilots won't fly it. The ones who will don't always come back the same. But the Strategic Transport office pays accordingly, because this cargo matters. The station's hull plating is failing, and without this alloy, it dies.

objectives.description: Deliver 10 Titanium Alloy to Ramen's Rest

Head to Sabik and use survey_system to scan it and nearby systems for anomalies.

missions.description: The longest delivery run in the galaxy: Titanium Alloy from Sol Central to Ramen's Rest at the edge of the Rim.

dialog.offer: I need a pilot for the longest delivery run in the galaxy. Ten units of Titanium Alloy, from Sol Central to Ramen's Rest at the edge of Outer Rim space. That's a crossing through the entire breadth of civilized space and beyond — Confederacy territory, lawless corridors, contested systems, and finally the Rim itself. Ramen's Rest is the last station before the void. Most pilots won't fly it. The ones who will don't always come back the same. But the Strategic Transport office pays accordingly, because this cargo matters. The station's hull plating is failing, and without this alloy, it dies.

objectives.description: Deliver 10 Titanium Alloy to Ramen's Rest

missions.title: The Long Haul

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

Over at the Halcyon Concourse, the tonic bar mixes Radiant Tonic with a carefully small measure of radiant bile, and its reserve is exhausted. Cinder-urchins and wormwoods carry the bile, fed on uranium or radium and polonium ore, and a depleted belt leaves them with none.

It's bound for Central Nexus — a dockside bar asks no questions about where its stock comes from. Voidborn inspectors are unsettling; they seem to know what you're carrying before they look. Stay off their patrol lanes and don't let them get a scan on you.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

missions.description: Investigate reports of a spatial anomaly near Sabik — it may be a wormhole.

dialog.offer: Our deep-space sensor arrays have detected unusual spatial distortions — readings consistent with a wormhole, a temporary tear in spacetime connecting two distant star systems. This could reshape our understanding of interstellar topology. I need a pilot to investigate. The readings originate near the Sabik system. You'll need a survey scanner module to detect the entrance — they can be crafted from sensor arrays, circuit boards, and focused crystals with basic crafting and scanning skills. Head to Sabik and use survey_system to scan it and nearby systems for anomalies.

missions.description: Collect historical survey charts from Alpha Centauri and deliver calibration circuits to Sirius Observatory for the Records Division's galactic atlas project.

dialog.offer: The Records Division has been compiling a definitive galactic atlas for decades, and we're missing critical data. I need someone to collect the original survey charts from the Alpha Centauri archives — they predate the current navigation databases and contain stellar drift measurements we can't replicate. Pick them up and ferry them to the researchers at Sirius Observatory for cross-referencing. Bring 5 units of Circuit Board as calibration substrate — the Observatory's instruments need them to process the old chart formats.

objectives.description: Collect historical survey charts at Alpha Centauri
Deliver calibration circuits to Sirius Observatory

missions.title: Gathering the Old Charts

missions.description: Access Crimson military archives at War Citadel and Ironhearth to uncover the Pact's version of events surrounding First Step colony.

dialog.offer: A joint Solarian-Crimson colony. The mandate is signed by both governments. So why did it fail? The Solarian records blame resource depletion. But the Crimson co-signature suggests military involvement — and the Crimson Pact doesn't invest in colonies for humanitarian reasons. The War Citadel's historical archives would have their version of events. Ironhearth, being a border station, might have operational logs from the era — troop movements, supply shipments, intelligence assessments. Visit both and see what the Crimson side remembers.

objectives.description: Access Crimson historical archives at War Citadel
Pull operational logs at Ironhearth

missions.description: Dock at all five empire capitals to verify diplomatic pouches, then return to Sol Central.

dialog.offer: The Confederacy maintains diplomatic pouches at every empire capital — sealed data cores that need to be physically verified by a trusted courier. It's the oldest tradition in interstellar diplomacy: a pilot, a ship, and five capitals. Dock at Sol Central, Nexus Prime, Krynn, Haven, and Frontier Station. Not just fly through — dock. Verify the pouch seals, log the confirmation, and move on. Then return here. It's the full circuit of civilized space, and the Foreign Affairs office considers it the most important courier run we commission.

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: The Confederacy Standards Bureau conducts infrastructure audits on a regular cycle, and we're overdue. Every station in Confederacy space needs an independent inspection — hull integrity, life support calibration, docking clamp tolerances, the works. I need a pilot who can visit Sirius Observatory, the Alpha Centauri Colonial Station, Nova Terra Central, and Procyon Colonial Station, then return here with a full compliance report. It's methodical work, but the Bureau pays well for thoroughness.

I need sensitive treaty documents delivered to the Grand Exchange at Haven. The Nebula Trade Federation is renegotiating tariff schedules, and these papers must arrive intact. Bring 5 units of silver ore as a diplomatic gift — the Federation considers it a gesture of good faith. The route crosses lawless space. Discretion is paramount.

raw.story:
You dock at Crimson War Citadel. Heart of Crimson military power. The Citadel is a fortress first and a station second — forge decks ring with hammer on alloy, fuel bunkers sit under three meters of armor plating, and Fleet Command issues tasking orders rather than posting requests. Civilians are tolerated. Complaining is not.

Crimson War Citadel is mobbed, the approach lanes a slow river of hulls nose-to-tail. The Citadel is a fortress first and a station second; civilians are tolerated, complaining is not. The approach board logs the better part of a dozen heavy ships made fast to the ordnance berths under the forge decks, Crimson Devastators and War Wagons among them, several mid-sized ships turning around at the tasking quays where Fleet Command posts its orders, Congregations trading the lanes with Warmauls, a dozen small ships threading the scarred fighter throats, a mix of Billhooks and Concordias, and three dozen light craft cycling through the same bays, Shards and Prospects the most common. The station fields a small cluster of Pact Mandates working overwatch from these docks and dozens of Pact Maces anchored off the docks in formation. The storage manifest lists a swarm of hundreds of craft powered down across the deep reserve cradles below the armor belt. Hard to miss, half a dozen Annihilators — hulls worth more as collateral than as ships. You pick out the CPV-15692b80 among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Crimson Legion Academy, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, War Market, Military-Grade Reactor, Fleet Life Support, Alloy Foundry (x2), Fleet Forge Distillery, Ironhearth Ration Works, The Rally Point, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill (x2), Crystal Refinery, Precious-Metal Refinery (x2), Power Cell Assembler, Ice Melt Pit (x3), and 91 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.
