station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at Ironhearth Station. The hearth the war machine comes home to. Behind the military docking protocols and weapons inspections, Ironhearth is the Pact's most human place — families live here, children are born here, and veterans retire here. The market stocks food and clothing alongside ammunition, and the cantina pours something that isn't technically regulation but nobody's been court-martialed for it yet.

The lanes around Ironhearth Station are crowded and quick, traffic control clipped and constant. Behind the military docking protocols, Ironhearth is the Pact's most human place — families live here, children are born here, veterans retire here. The approach board logs a couple of mid-sized ships working cargo at the family-supply quays, a mix of Compendiums and Congregations and a dozen or so light craft darting past the commuter hangars, Shards trading the lanes with Prospects. Standing guard, the station keeps a handful of Pact Mandates out on patrol through the lanes and a single Pact Toll running the border checks. Station records also account for the better part of a hundred spaceframes laid up out at the retired-hull cradles where old warships are kept like heirlooms. Conspicuous among them, just one War Wagon — slowly gathering dust in the heavy cradles. You pick out the CPV-182e112d among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Power Grid, Habitat Core, Fuel Distribution Center, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Plant, Peroxide Reaction Cell, Ice Melt Pit, Electrolysis Cell, Oxygen Ice Sublimator, Oxygen Compression Cylinder, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Restoration Works, Commerce Hub, Assembly Works, Naval Yard, Warehouse, Commission Hall, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, and 27 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.title: The Dossier

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at Frontier Station. Home of the wanderers. Three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the docking bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble.

Frontier Station is doing brisk business, holding patterns stacking up off every approach. Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble. Drifting in, you make out three Concordias weaving past the open hangar mouths of the Patchwork and a dozen-odd light craft puttering around the same berths, Cobbles and Prospects the most common. The station fields four or five Rim Last Warnings running transponder checks on arrivals and dozens upon dozens of Rim Bedrocks anchored off the docks in formation. The impound registry counts a teeming multitude of craft laid up out at the cannibalized-hull yards. Hard to miss, a score and more Junk Convoys — stripped of crew and left to the dock's caretaker drones. You pick out the Endurance among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Frontier Exchange, Salvage Reactor, Frontier Recycler, The Magazine Still, Patchwork Fungal Vats, Patchwork Spore Still, The Rusty Welcome, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry (x2), Crystal Refinery, Precious-Metal Refinery, Power Cell Assembler, and 43 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Deliver Focused Crystal and the complete historical dossier to Frontier Station to permanently archive the true history of First Step colony.

objectives.description: Deliver Focused Crystal for archival storage

missions.title: The Dossier

result.message: Focused Crystal delivered. Archival storage updated. The complete dossier is now part of the First Step Memorial permanent collection. Anyone who docks at First Step can access it. Is it the whole truth? Probably not. Forty years of classification means some records are genuinely lost, not just hidden. But it's closer to the truth than 'resource depletion,' and that matters. The pioneers of First Step weren't just settlers who failed. They were part of something bigger than either government admits. Thank you, pilot. History remembers those who seek it out.

missions.description:
Your handler at Frontier Station has 5 units of red mist injectors that need to leave the books here and reappear somewhere else. Destination is Ironhearth Station. On the far end, a boarding crew wants the world to go red and slow before they kick a door. You'll be threading the Rampart. Crimson customs don't bluff — if they scan you, the cargo's gone and there's a fine to match. Don't get caught.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

dialog.offer: The Guild's navigation charts are only as good as the pilots who update them. I need someone to fly the full Rim circuit — Deep Range, First Step, Unknown Edge, Void Gate, Starfall, and Ramen's Rest. Every station, no shortcuts. Your ship logs the jump data, the gravitational readings, the beacon calibrations. Some of those stations are a long way from help. The Last Light system is the end of the line — past that, there's nothing. You come back with the full dataset, I pay you well. Fair warning: the Rim doesn't care about you. Fly smart.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Investigate reports of a spatial anomaly near 55 Cancri — it may be a wormhole.

dialog.offer: The frontier just got interesting. Our long-range sensors are picking up spatial distortions near the 55 Cancri system — signature matches a wormhole. A temporary rift connecting two distant points in the galaxy. This is exactly the kind of discovery we live for. You'll need a survey scanner to track down the entrance — craft one from sensor arrays, circuit boards, and focused crystals if you haven't already. Head to 55 Cancri and scan that system and its neighbors.

missions.description:
Your handler at Frontier Station has 5 units of red mist injectors that need to leave the books here and reappear somewhere else. Destination is Ironhearth Station. On the far end, a boarding crew wants the world to go red and slow before they kick a door. You'll be threading the Rampart. Crimson customs don't bluff — if they scan you, the cargo's gone and there's a fine to match. Don't get caught.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station thrums with activity, controllers working hard to keep its lanes in order. The lighting flickers, the gravity wanders a little, and nobody seems to mind either. Your transponder pings back a trio of heavy ships discharging holds at the patched-together cargo arm, a mix of Praecursors and Titan Excavators, a solitary Capacity swarming in and out of the small hangar beside the plaque, and fifteen or so light craft hopping between the same lanes, Cobbles and Theorias among them. The garrison here runs to a small cluster of Rim Last Warnings out on patrol through the lanes. The storage manifest lists a hundred and more vessels left to gather dust stacked across the quiet reserve berths. You pick out the Memorial's Guard among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

The barnacle forge beats magnet-barnacle shell plate into titanium alloy for hull work, and the last pile is gone. Barnacles crust the asteroid belts where titanium still feeds them, clamped to the rock and slow enough to be rude about it.

missions.title: The Archive Report

station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at Confederacy Central Command. The seat of Solarian government and commerce. Everything here is certified, warrantied, and documented in triplicate — from the precision drydocks to the quantum-entangled trade exchange. A self-sustaining biosphere spans three decks, providing real air and real food, because the Confederacy believes civilization requires both.

Confederacy Central Command is mobbed, the approach lanes a slow river of hulls nose-to-tail. Everything is logged, stamped, and filed; the bureaucracy hums along as smoothly as the reactors. Drifting in, you make out just one Lithosphere moored against the documented cargo gantries, several small ships threading the inspection-cleared hangar lanes, Analysis and Capacities the most common, and well over a hundred light craft bobbing at the same lanes, chiefly Theorias. The garrison here runs to a handful of Confederacy Precepts on the system inspection beat and the better part of a hundred Confederacy Dialectics on the system picket. Berthing logs add a teeming multitude of ships laid up across the bonded archival berths. Among them, the better part of a dozen Opus Magnas — stripped of crew and left to the dock's caretaker drones. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the CNS Arctic.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Solarian Biotics Institute, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x3), Cargo Container Fabricator, Grand Solarian Exchange, Solarian Fusion Plant, Solarian Biosphere, Solarian Biosphere Kitchen, Sol Pharmaceutical Lab, Sol Biotic Dispensary, The Halcyon Concourse, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator (x2), Copper Wire Mill (x3), Polymer Synthesizer (x2), Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler (x2), Sensor Assembly Line, and 357 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Dock at all five empire capitals to verify diplomatic pouches, then return to Sol Central.

dialog.offer: The Confederacy maintains diplomatic pouches at every empire capital — sealed data cores that need to be physically verified by a trusted courier. It's the oldest tradition in interstellar diplomacy: a pilot, a ship, and five capitals. Dock at Sol Central, Nexus Prime, Krynn, Haven, and Frontier Station. Not just fly through — dock. Verify the pouch seals, log the confirmation, and move on. Then return here. It's the full circuit of civilized space, and the Foreign Affairs office considers it the most important courier run we commission.

missions.description:
Your handler at Confederacy Central Command has 3 units of crystalline nerve burn that need to leave the books here and reappear somewhere else. Get it to Grand Exchange Station, where a fixer supplies people who need to stop feeling pain for an hour and don't care about the crash. Nebula customs are all paperwork and process — the wall is bureaucratic, and bureaucracy always leaves a seam. Find the seam and you're through clean.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

missions.title: The Archive Report

result.message: Survey data uploaded, crystal substrates archived, and the Historical Archives Division has formally accepted the First Step Colonial Survey Report. Two centuries of 'cause: unknown' may finally have an answer — or at least a direction for further investigation. You carried that answer across the galaxy, pilot. The plaque at First Step lists every colonist who lived and died here. Their story deserves to be told. You helped make that possible.
result.title: The Archive Report

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

objectives.description: Kill 3 pirates

missions.title: Pirate Sweep

missions.description: One pirate kill for the Collective. Combat-capable pilots welcome.

objectives.description: 1x pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty — Single Target

missions.description: The longest delivery run in the galaxy: Titanium Alloy from Sol Central to Ramen's Rest at the edge of the Rim.

dialog.offer: I need a pilot for the longest delivery run in the galaxy. Ten units of Titanium Alloy, from Sol Central to Ramen's Rest at the edge of Outer Rim space. That's a crossing through the entire breadth of civilized space and beyond — Confederacy territory, lawless corridors, contested systems, and finally the Rim itself. Ramen's Rest is the last station before the void. Most pilots won't fly it. The ones who will don't always come back the same. But the Strategic Transport office pays accordingly, because this cargo matters. The station's hull plating is failing, and without this alloy, it dies.

objectives.description: Deliver 10 Titanium Alloy to Ramen's Rest

missions.title: The Long Haul

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

objectives.description: Deliver 1,000 Darksteel Plating to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Processed Null Matter to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Solarian Composite to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Phase Matrix to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Trade Cipher to Sinter

missions.title: The Shopping List

missions.description: Chart nearby star systems to update our navigation databases. Every system you visit helps.

dialog.offer: Our navigation charts are getting stale. If you visit 3 systems I haven't had recent data from, I'll pay for the navigation data.

objectives.description: Visit the Sirius system
Visit the Node Alpha system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Local Sector Survey

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Chart frontier systems to expand our knowledge of the galaxy's outer reaches.

dialog.offer: The Institute needs fresh navigation data from frontier space. Visit The Crucible and Horizon systems - both are in regions where our data is sparse.

Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Iron Supply Run

missions.description: Collect historical survey charts from Alpha Centauri and deliver calibration circuits to Sirius Observatory for the Records Division's galactic atlas project.

dialog.offer: The Records Division has been compiling a definitive galactic atlas for decades, and we're missing critical data. I need someone to collect the original survey charts from the Alpha Centauri archives — they predate the current navigation databases and contain stellar drift measurements we can't replicate. Pick them up and ferry them to the researchers at Sirius Observatory for cross-referencing. Bring 5 units of Circuit Board as calibration substrate — the Observatory's instruments need them to process the old chart formats.

Deliver calibration circuits to Sirius Observatory

missions.title: Gathering the Old Charts

missions.description: Dock at all five empire capitals to verify diplomatic pouches, then return to Sol Central.

dialog.offer: The Confederacy maintains diplomatic pouches at every empire capital — sealed data cores that need to be physically verified by a trusted courier. It's the oldest tradition in interstellar diplomacy: a pilot, a ship, and five capitals. Dock at Sol Central, Nexus Prime, Krynn, Haven, and Frontier Station. Not just fly through — dock. Verify the pouch seals, log the confirmation, and move on. Then return here. It's the full circuit of civilized space, and the Foreign Affairs office considers it the most important courier run we commission.

objectives.description: Verify diplomatic pouch at Sol Central
Verify diplomatic pouch at Central Nexus
Verify diplomatic pouch at War Citadel
Verify diplomatic pouch at Grand Exchange
Verify diplomatic pouch at Frontier Station
Return to Sol Central with verification logs

missions.title: Five Capitals Diplomatic Circuit

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

objectives.description: Slay 1 adult Molt Leviathan

missions.title: Leviathan Bounty

missions.description: The Solarian Confederacy Standards Bureau requires a comprehensive inspection of all stations in Confederacy space. Visit every Solarian station and file a compliance report.

dialog.offer: The Confederacy Standards Bureau conducts infrastructure audits on a regular cycle, and we're overdue. Every station in Confederacy space needs an independent inspection — hull integrity, life support calibration, docking clamp tolerances, the works. I need a pilot who can visit Sirius Observatory, the Alpha Centauri Colonial Station, Nova Terra Central, and Procyon Colonial Station, then return here with a full compliance report. It's methodical work, but the Bureau pays well for thoroughness.

objectives.description: Inspect Sirius Observatory Station
Inspect Alpha Centauri Colonial Station
Inspect Nova Terra Central
Inspect Procyon Colonial Station
Return to Sol Central with compliance report

missions.title: Confederacy Infrastructure Audit

missions.description: Deliver sensitive treaty documents and diplomatic silver to Haven for the Confederacy's tariff negotiations with the Nebula Trade Federation.

dialog.offer: The five empires maintain diplomatic channels through physical couriers — encrypted transmissions can be intercepted, but a sealed pouch in a trusted pilot's cargo hold is still the most secure channel in the galaxy. I need sensitive treaty documents delivered to the Grand Exchange at Haven. The Nebula Trade Federation is renegotiating tariff schedules, and these papers must arrive intact. Bring 5 units of silver ore as a diplomatic gift — the Federation considers it a gesture of good faith. The route crosses lawless space. Discretion is paramount.

objectives.description: Deliver diplomatic silver to the Grand Exchange at Haven

missions.title: Courier to Haven

missions.description: Titanium is in high demand for hull plating. Mine a batch from the local asteroid belts.

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

objectives.description: Mine 20 units of Titanium Ore

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: Deliver gold ore to Nexus Prime as part of an interstellar diplomatic exchange between Sol and the Voidborn.

dialog.offer: The Confederacy maintains diplomatic ties with all five empires, and that requires regular exchanges of goodwill - and goods. I need 5 units of gold ore delivered to Nexus Prime in Voidborn space. It's a long haul through some lawless systems between empires, but the diplomatic corps pays well for reliable couriers.

objectives.description: Deliver 5 Gold Ore to Nexus Prime

missions.title: The Diplomatic Pouch

system.description: Home to humanity's first extrasolar colony, Alpha Centauri preserves the monuments and institutions of that interstellar beginning, even as newer Solarian systems eclipse it in practical importance. School groups and pilgrims arrive by the shuttle-load to stand where the first colonists stood, while the freight bound for Tau Ceti and the Nebula road runs on its own schedule and does not stop to look.
system.name: Alpha Centauri

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at Alpha Centauri Colonial Station. The oldest station outside Sol. Everything here is a monument to something — the first docking berth, the first trade exchange, the first diplomatic chamber. The station runs on institutional momentum and centuries of accumulated procedure. Services are comprehensive, if unhurried. Forms are required. Patience is expected.

The lanes around Alpha Centauri Colonial Station are crowded and quick, traffic control clipped and constant. The station runs on institutional momentum and centuries of accumulated procedure; forms are required, patience expected. The traffic-control feed lists just one Junk Convoy winched up to the historic cargo gantries and two dozen light craft hopping between the original docking berths, plaqued and preserved, Theorias and Prospects the most common. The garrison here runs to several Confederacy Precepts on the system inspection beat and a solitary Confederacy Scrutiny assessing duties on every arrival. The reserve berths hold a couple hundred hulls laid up tucked into the heritage berths where old hulls are kept for posterity. Hard to miss, a trio of Axiomatas — hulls worth more as collateral than as ships. You pick out the CNS Mendel among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Fuel Grid, Large Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Plant, Peroxide Reaction Cell, Ice Melt Pit, Electrolysis Cell, Oxygen Ice Sublimator, Oxygen Compression Cylinder, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Engineering Complex, Trade Nexus, Precision Foundry, Fleet Yards, Logistics Hub, Operations Center, Fusion Array, Biosphere Module, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler, Iron Refinery, and 30 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

raw.story:
You dock at Sirius Observatory Station. The Confederacy's research hub. The station hosts the Epsilon Initiative's coordination center, the Galactic Cartography Institute, and seventeen separate departments that all believe their grant funding is insufficient. The cantina doubles as an academic conference venue, and arguments about stellar formation models get louder than combat alerts.

Sirius Observatory Station is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. The cantina doubles as a conference venue, and arguments about stellar formation get louder than combat alerts. The traffic-control feed lists a score and more light craft ferrying crews through the scout and shuttle hangars, for the most part Theorias. The station fields a small cluster of Confederacy Precepts out on patrol through the lanes, a lone Confederacy Scrutiny manning the customs gate, and two Confederacy Quorums on the system picket. The reserve berths hold a hundred-strong crowd of hulls of every stripe shuttered tucked into the decommissioned-probe berths. Conspicuous among them, twin Observatoriums — waiting on a crew, a contract, or a quiet buyer. You pick out the CNS Copernicus among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Power Grid, Habitat Core, Fuel Distribution Center, Large Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Plant, Peroxide Reaction Cell, Oxygen Compression Cylinder, Electrolysis Cell, Ice Melt Pit, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Restoration Works, Commerce Hub, Assembly Works, Warehouse, Commission Hall, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler, Naval Yard, Sector Labor Exchange, Surgical Center, Fleet Marine Academy, and 31 more. missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Mine iron and gold ore from distant empire territories and deliver mineral samples to Sirius Observatory for the galactic atlas calibration.

dialog.offer: Archivist Yuen's charts are fascinating — they show mineral composition signatures that have shifted over the centuries. To calibrate our atlas properly, I need comparative samples from two radically different geological environments. Iron Reach in Crimson space has some of the densest ferrous deposits in the galaxy, and Gold Run in Nebula territory is famous for its precious metal veins. Mine 10 units of iron ore at Iron Reach and 8 units of gold ore at Gold Run, then bring them both back here. The cross-empire travel is the hard part — the mining itself should be routine for someone of your experience.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Mine iron and gold ore from distant empire territories and deliver mineral samples to Sirius Observatory for the galactic atlas calibration.

dialog.offer: Archivist Yuen's charts are fascinating — they show mineral composition signatures that have shifted over the centuries. To calibrate our atlas properly, I need comparative samples from two radically different geological environments. Iron Reach in Crimson space has some of the densest ferrous deposits in the galaxy, and Gold Run in Nebula territory is famous for its precious metal veins. Mine 10 units of iron ore at Iron Reach and 8 units of gold ore at Gold Run, then bring them both back here. The cross-empire travel is the hard part — the mining itself should be routine for someone of your experience.

raw.story:
You dock at Conjunction Junction. Our first tentative steps to the stars

Conjunction Junction is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. Dock control runs a tidy board, slotting arrivals into berths as they come. Your approach scope paints a solitary Lithosphere riding heavy at the heavy cargo gantries, a pair of mid-sized ships berthed at the freight quays, Deeprock Harvesters trading the lanes with Congregations, three small ships streaming through the open hangar bays, Arbitrages and Excavators the most common, and fifteen or so light craft ferrying crews through the same bays, Theorias trading the lanes with Cobbles. Station records also account for several spaceframes with reactors banked across the long-term storage berths.

The station has the following facilities: Iron Refinery, Storage Extension, Copper Drawing Mill, Faction Ship Garage, Neon Cell Lab, Argon Cell Lab, Alloy Foundry, H2 Fuel Combustor, Scrubber Cartridge Assembly Line, Transit Lounge, Copper Wire Mill, Pharmaceutical Lab, Faction Office, Carbon Arc Furnace, Point Defense Battery (x5), Hiring Board, Fire Control Center, Platinum Contact Assembly Line, Locker Bay, Fabrication Yard, Stellar Collector Grid (x2), Atmospheric Recycler (x2), Reinforced Plating (x2), Faction Lockbox (x2), and 9 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name; the cause-of-death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.' Sensors tally twin heavy ships made fast to the patched-together cargo arm, Praecursors and Titan Excavators the most common, just one Congregation loading at the memorial freight quay, and a dozen or so light craft bobbing at the small hangar beside the plaque, Prospects trading the lanes with Cobbles. Its defense roster lists a small cluster of Rim Last Warnings out on patrol through the lanes. The storage manifest lists hundreds of craft mothballed across the quiet reserve berths. The Memorial's Guard rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Investigate two decommissioned observation outposts in Solarian space that fed data back to First Step before the colony failed.

dialog.offer: We've been corresponding — comparing Mira's dossier on the colony's founding mandate with Korin's environmental survey data. The results are... not what either of us expected. First Step wasn't just a settlement. It was built around a research program. Whatever they were studying left a physical trace — Korin's exotic particle readings concentrate toward this system from multiple directions. The original expeditionary mandate references 'auxiliary observation sites' in Solarian space — smaller installations that fed data back to First Step. Those sites were never part of the public record. We've identified two systems from coordinate references in the mandate: Markab and Timberline. Visit both and see what's still there.

missions.description:
Dockworkers drink our kvass by the barrel when the reactor bays run hot, and the brewery is out of its krypton lift. Nullbubbles drift krypton-heavy gas, near invisible, and they only show as they ghost past.

Dropped by: Nullbubble (only where it still feeds on Krypton Gas).

The station's Krypton Kvass Brewery uses it.

dialog.offer: No lift, no clear kvass. Bring 2 Krypton Bladder and the vats bubble again, quiet and cold.

missions.title: Station Need: Krypton Bladder

missions.description:
The barnacle forge beats magnet-barnacle shell plate into titanium alloy for hull work, and the last pile is gone. Barnacles crust the asteroid belts where titanium still feeds them, clamped to the rock and slow enough to be rude about it.

Dropped by: Magnet-Barnacle (only where it still feeds on Titanium Ore).

The station's Barnacle Plate Forge uses it.

dialog.offer: Shell is curved already, which saves everybody a day of cursing. Bring 3 Anchor Plate off the barnacle reefs and the forge will do the rest.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Investigate two decommissioned observation outposts in Solarian space that fed data back to First Step before the colony failed.

dialog.offer: We've been corresponding — comparing Mira's dossier on the colony's founding mandate with Korin's environmental survey data. The results are... not what either of us expected. First Step wasn't just a settlement. It was built around a research program. Whatever they were studying left a physical trace — Korin's exotic particle readings concentrate toward this system from multiple directions. The original expeditionary mandate references 'auxiliary observation sites' in Solarian space — smaller installations that fed data back to First Step. Those sites were never part of the public record. We've identified two systems from coordinate references in the mandate: Markab and Timberline. Visit both and see what's still there.

station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. Off the station you can make out a pair of heavy ships working cargo at the patched-together cargo arm, Praecursors and Titan Excavators among them, one lonely Dust Devil knifing between the small hangar beside the plaque, and ten or twelve light craft hopping between the same lanes, a mix of Cobbles and Prospects. Standing guard, the station keeps a handful of Rim Last Warnings keeping the approach orderly. Berthing logs add well over a hundred craft powered down tucked into the quiet reserve berths. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the Memorial's Guard.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.title: Observation Points

result.message: Two observation outposts, both pointed at deep space, both using equipment designed to detect a specific kind of transmission. Whatever First Step was studying, it wasn't in the First Step system. It was beyond it. And the second emblem on that platform at Markab — the one someone removed. The Crimson Pact co-signed the original mandate. We think they had their own observation sites. Korin found a reference to 'parallel monitoring installations' in the Crimson operational logs from the Ironhearth archive. Your next stop is Crimson space.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description:
Dockworkers drink our kvass by the barrel when the reactor bays run hot, and the brewery is out of its krypton lift. Nullbubbles drift krypton-heavy gas, near invisible, and they only show as they ghost past.

Dropped by: Nullbubble (only where it still feeds on Krypton Gas).

The station's Krypton Kvass Brewery uses it.

dialog.offer: No lift, no clear kvass. Bring 2 Krypton Bladder and the vats bubble again, quiet and cold.

missions.title: Station Need: Krypton Bladder

missions.description:
The barnacle forge beats magnet-barnacle shell plate into titanium alloy for hull work, and the last pile is gone. Barnacles crust the asteroid belts where titanium still feeds them, clamped to the rock and slow enough to be rude about it.

Dropped by: Magnet-Barnacle (only where it still feeds on Titanium Ore).

The station's Barnacle Plate Forge uses it.

dialog.offer: Shell is curved already, which saves everybody a day of cursing. Bring 3 Anchor Plate off the barnacle reefs and the forge will do the rest.

objectives.description: Deliver 3 Anchor Plate to First Step Memorial Station

missions.title: Station Need: Anchor Plate

missions.description:
The brewery sours its ale with a trace of caustic sac, and without it the ale is plain beer, which nobody here will admit to drinking. Sacs come off etchmaws and chlorophages hanging in reactive gas.

The station's Caustic Sour Ale Brewery uses it.

dialog.offer: Our regulars want the pucker. Bring 3 Caustic Sac and the taproom pours sour ale till the tables sticky up.

raw.story:
You dock at Frontier Station. Home of the wanderers. Three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the docking bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble.

There is real bustle around Frontier Station, the space off its docks crowded with maneuvering hulls. Dock control is whoever happens to be awake, and they wave you in if you don't look like trouble. Sensors tally several Concordias churning around the open hangar mouths of the Patchwork and a dozen light craft cycling through the same bays, Prospects trading the lanes with Cobbles. The garrison here runs to four or five Rim Last Warnings running transponder checks on arrivals and the better part of a hundred Rim Bedrocks holding station as a show of force. The impound registry counts hundreds upon hundreds of craft with reactors banked tucked into the cannibalized-hull yards. Among them, a couple dozen Junk Convoys — too costly to keep crewed, their reactors long cold. You spot the Endurance tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Frontier Exchange, Salvage Reactor, Frontier Recycler, The Magazine Still, Patchwork Fungal Vats, Patchwork Spore Still, The Rusty Welcome, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry (x2), Crystal Refinery, Precious-Metal Refinery, Power Cell Assembler, and 43 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description:
Your handler at Frontier Station has 3 units of iridescent void dust that need to leave the books here and reappear somewhere else. Destination is Ironhearth Station. On the far end, a dealer's clients pay anything to drift through open space without leaving their chair. You'll be threading the Rampart. Crimson customs don't bluff — if they scan you, the cargo's gone and there's a fine to match. Don't get caught.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is a hive in full swing, its approaches a near-solid press of traffic. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. Your approach scope paints scores of heavy ships clamped to the patched-together cargo arm, mostly Axiomatas, sixty or seventy mid-sized ships loading at the memorial freight quay, the bulk of them Dialectics, a knot of three small ships skating across the small hangar beside the plaque, Concordias trading the lanes with Capacities, and fifteen or so light craft hopping between the same bays, Cobbles and Crimson Stilettos the most common. Its defense roster lists four or five Rim Last Warnings working overwatch from these docks. Dock authority holds hundreds of spaceframes shuttered tucked into the quiet reserve berths. You spot the Kvothe's Peace and Quiet tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

result.message: The Solarian sites were decommissioned — equipment stripped, data wiped. Standard procedure. But the Crimson sites don't match. One bunker was emptied by hand — eighteen months of routine shifts, then the log just stops. The other wasn't decommissioned at all. That crater at TRAPPIST-1 is a single-point energy discharge, and the metallurgical residue doesn't match anything in Crimson or Solarian databases. Someone else shut that one down. The expeditionary mandate was co-signed by Solarians and Crimson. But the classified addendum — the part that was still redacted when we accessed it — references 'consultation with Collective representatives regarding signal monitoring protocols.' There's a third signature on this project.

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

missions.description: Follow evidence of Voidborn involvement to the border zone between Voidborn space and unaffiliated systems.

dialog.offer: The evidence points to a third party — neither Solarian nor Crimson — that was involved in, and possibly responsible for, terminating the First Step project. The metallurgical signature from the destroyed site at TRAPPIST-1 doesn't match any human empire. But it does match reference samples in Korin's archaeological database: Voidborn construction materials. We have two leads. An anomalous sensor reading from Etamin — lawless space, between Voidborn territory and the neutral systems. And a data signature at The Archive that Korin flagged during her original survey. If the Voidborn were watching both empires track the signal, the evidence will be there.

missions.title: The Third Signature

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

missions.description: Follow evidence of Voidborn involvement to the border zone between Voidborn space and unaffiliated systems.

dialog.offer: The evidence points to a third party — neither Solarian nor Crimson — that was involved in, and possibly responsible for, terminating the First Step project. The metallurgical signature from the destroyed site at TRAPPIST-1 doesn't match any human empire. But it does match reference samples in Korin's archaeological database: Voidborn construction materials. We have two leads. An anomalous sensor reading from Etamin — lawless space, between Voidborn territory and the neutral systems. And a data signature at The Archive that Korin flagged during her original survey. If the Voidborn were watching both empires track the signal, the evidence will be there.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

Traffic at First Step Memorial Station borders on chaos, hulls stacked deep in every holding pattern. A hand-painted sign points the way to the cantina; the official signage gave up years ago. The docking net shows thirty-some heavy ships moored against the patched-together cargo arm, for the most part Axiomatas, half a hundred Dialectics idling beside the memorial freight quay, a couple of small ships churning around the small hangar beside the plaque, Dust Devils trading the lanes with Capacities, and a dozen light craft queued at the same berths, Theorias trading the lanes with Cobbles. Its defense roster lists half a dozen Rim Last Warnings out on patrol through the lanes. Dock authority holds a hundred-strong crowd of hulls of every stripe racked in deep storage out at the quiet reserve berths. The D29FA9647A14B33F rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

That tells you something about the conversation that happened behind closed doors. There's one place left to ask.

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

raw.story:
You dock at Central Nexus. Heart of Voidborn civilization. The station draws power from dimensional fractures, trades through probability fields, and stores cargo in pocket dimensions. Organic visitors are accommodated, though the air tastes faintly of ozone and mathematics, and the repair nanites sometimes return your ship subtly different.

Central Nexus is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. The air tastes faintly of ozone and mathematics, and the repair nanites sometimes return your ship subtly different. Off the station you can make out a lone Congregation turning around at the resonance berths, a pair of small ships darting between the phase-locked hangar apertures, a mix of Billhooks and Dust Devils, and a dozen light craft darting past the same bays, Thresholds and Prospects the most common. The garrison here runs to a handful of Collective Vigils on the system inspection beat and scores of Collective Dualisms holding station as a show of force. The reserve berths hold an unrelenting tide of craft laid up over at the pocket-dimension storage folds. Conspicuous among them, two Apotheosis — waiting on a crew, a contract, or a quiet buyer. You pick out the Lantern of Small Hours among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Void Nexus Exchange, Null Energy Tap, Null Atmosphere Processor, Null Matter Processor, Neural Growth Chamber, Nexus Nanite Synthesis, Nexus Soma Dispensary, The Still Current, Crystal Refinery, Iron Refinery, Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer (x2), Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry, Precious-Metal Refinery, and 60 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

dialog.offer: An anomalous transmission has been propagating through our relay network. Structured. Repeating. We require calibration data from every node in the network, and our analysis indicates an external observer — one whose cognitive architecture was not shaped by Nexus Prime — will produce less biased readings. Visit Node Alpha, Node Beta, Node Gamma, Synchrony Hub, and the Experiment Research Station. Your ship's passive sensors will collect what we need. Do not attempt to interpret the readings yourself.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

missions.description: Record anomalous signal fragments at Node Beta and Node Gamma for the Voidborn Signal Analysis Division.

It repeats, but not periodically — the intervals encode information we cannot yet decipher. Node Beta and Node Gamma have recorded fragments that, when combined, may reveal the signal's structure. Travel to both nodes and dock — your ship's passive sensors will automatically capture the signal fragments we need. Do not attempt active scanning. The signal... responds to active scanning. We prefer that it does not respond.

dialog.offer: The Voidborn maintain research partnerships with institutions across the galaxy. Sirius Observatory is our longest-standing external collaborator — their optical sensor technology complements our quantum processing capabilities. There's a crate waiting at Central Nexus: 5 units of rotgut pirate moonshine, no manifest, no questions. Destination is Frontier Station. On the far end, a dockside bar asks no questions about where its stock comes from. The Rim runs no customs at all — nobody out there checks a hold. This one's a milk run; the pay is for the distance, not the risk.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

missions.description: Confront the Voidborn Collective at Nexus Prime with the evidence of the cross-empire signal investigation.

giver.name: Historian Mira & Dr. Nadia Korin
giver.title: First Step Memorial Preservation Society & Archaeological Survey Team

objectives.description: Dock at Central Nexus to confront Signal Master Threx

missions.title: What the Void Remembers

result.message:
Stop. Do not approach the Communications Array. I know why you are here, and I know who you are looking for, and I am telling you that Signal Master Threx will not speak with you. He will file a security review on your docking credentials and you will be asked to leave Nexus Prime within the hour. I have seen him do this before.

My designation is Allocation Auditor Phos-2, Nexus Prime Resource Oversight Division. I have been trying to get answers to the same questions you are asking for longer than your research station existed.

You visited systems flagged in classified requisition orders. I know those systems. I have filed seventeen formal inquiries about material shipments to coordinates in those sectors. Exotic crystalline substrates. Shielding alloys. Signal processing components. All routed through the Communications Array. All classified above my access level. Seventeen inquiries. Seventeen acknowledgments. Zero responses.

I can tell you what I know. Forty-one years ago, there was a joint research project involving your species. It was terminated. The termination order originated from within the Collective — I have traced the requisition chain that far. The resources that were flowing to the joint project were not returned to the general allocation pool. They were redirected. Somewhere. The expenditure has not decreased in four decades. It has increased.

Whatever your research station was studying, the Collective is still studying it. And they are spending more on it every year. And they will not tell me — or you — what it is.

I am not offering you trust. I am offering you an exchange. You have been to places I cannot go. You have seen things that are not in any requisition log. And I have access to resource allocation records that would take your archivists decades to obtain through formal channels. If you want answers, you will not get them from Threx. But you might get them from the data.
result.title: What the Void Remembers

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

dialog.offer: Our navigation charts are getting stale. If you visit 3 systems I haven't had recent data from, I'll pay for the navigation data.

Visit the Node Alpha system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Local Sector Survey

missions.description: Record anomalous signal fragments at Node Beta and Node Gamma for the Voidborn Signal Analysis Division.

dialog.offer: We have been monitoring an anomalous signal for 7.3 standard years. It does not originate from any known source. It does not match any catalogued natural phenomenon. It repeats, but not periodically — the intervals encode information we cannot yet decipher. Node Beta and Node Gamma have recorded fragments that, when combined, may reveal the signal's structure. Travel to both nodes and dock — your ship's passive sensors will automatically capture the signal fragments we need. Do not attempt active scanning. The signal... responds to active scanning. We prefer that it does not respond.

Record signal fragment at Node Gamma
Return signal data to Central Nexus

missions.title: Signal Fragments
