dialog.offer: We're running low on iron ore again. If you can mine 30 units and bring them back, I'll make it worth your while.

objectives.description: Mine 30 units of Iron Ore

missions.title: Iron Supply Run

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

objectives.description: Slay 1 adult Molt Leviathan

missions.title: Leviathan Bounty

missions.description: Chart frontier systems to expand our knowledge of the galaxy's outer reaches.

dialog.offer: The Institute needs fresh navigation data from frontier space. Visit The Crucible and Horizon systems - both are in regions where our data is sparse.

objectives.description: Visit The Crucible system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Deep Space Cartography

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

Deliver 1,000 Processed Null Matter to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Solarian Composite to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Phase Matrix to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Trade Cipher to Sinter

missions.title: The Shopping List

missions.description: Return to First Step Memorial Station with Phos-2's intelligence to complete the cross-reference analysis.

dialog.offer: Your researchers have assembled more of the picture than any individual Voidborn operative. I did not expect organic persistence on this scale. Take my allocation records back to Historian Mira and Dr. Korin at First Step Memorial Station. Cross-referenced against your field survey data, the resource flows will reveal patterns that neither dataset shows alone. And tell your researchers this: the expenditure is not decreasing. Whatever the Collective learned from the Signal, they are scaling up, not winding down. That should concern all of us.

objectives.description: Deliver Phos-2's allocation records to First Step Memorial Station

missions.title: Processing the Data

missions.description: Deliver quantum-entangled phase material from Nexus Prime to Sirius Observatory for a joint telescope research program.

dialog.offer: The Voidborn maintain research partnerships with institutions across the galaxy. Sirius Observatory is our longest-standing external collaborator — their optical sensor technology complements our quantum processing capabilities. I need 8 units of refined phase material delivered to Sirius Observatory. The phase material contains quantum-entangled substrates that the Observatory's researchers will integrate into their next generation of telescopes. The material is delicate — it degrades in unshielded cargo holds over time, which is why we need a direct courier rather than a trade network delivery. Fly direct, fly fast.

objectives.description: Deliver phase material to Sirius Observatory

missions.title: Neural Matrix Delivery

We require calibration data from every node in the network, and our analysis indicates an external observer — one whose cognitive architecture was not shaped by Nexus Prime — will produce less biased readings. Visit Node Alpha, Node Beta, Node Gamma, Synchrony Hub, and the Experiment Research Station. Your ship's passive sensors will collect what we need. Do not attempt to interpret the readings yourself.

The press bonds a coronid's nacre to a steel charge into Solarian composite, the lattice the Crystalline Cradle grows its vessels upon. Coronids stalk the asteroid belts where sol-alloy runs, and shed nacre only while it feeds them.

Dropped by: Coronid (only where it still feeds on Sol Alloy Ore).

The station's Sol Nacre Press uses it.

dialog.offer: A hull is a sculpture that has agreed to be useful. Bring 5 Sol Nacre to Central Nexus, and the cradles will have material to agree upon.

missions.description: Investigate reports of a spatial anomaly near Haedus — it may be a wormhole.

dialog.offer: Signal analysis has identified non-standard spatial topology — probability of transient wormhole formation: 94.7%. Data suggests a spacetime discontinuity near the Haedus system. Field verification required. You will need a survey scanner module to isolate the signature. Components: sensor arrays, circuit boards, focused crystals. Minimum skill requirements: basic crafting, scanning. Proceed to Haedus. Execute survey_system in that system and adjacent systems to isolate the anomaly.

objectives.description: Investigate the Haedus system
Locate and traverse a wormhole
Return to Researcher Null-Seven with your findings

dialog.offer: We have been monitoring an anomalous signal for 7.3 standard years. It does not originate from any known source. It does not match any catalogued natural phenomenon. It repeats, but not periodically — the intervals encode information we cannot yet decipher. Node Beta and Node Gamma have recorded fragments that, when combined, may reveal the signal's structure. Travel to both nodes and dock — your ship's passive sensors will automatically capture the signal fragments we need. Do not attempt active scanning. The signal... responds to active scanning. We prefer that it does not respond.

Record signal fragment at Node Gamma
Return signal data to Central Nexus

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Return to First Step Memorial Station with Phos-2's intelligence to complete the cross-reference analysis.

dialog.offer: Your researchers have assembled more of the picture than any individual Voidborn operative. I did not expect organic persistence on this scale. Take my allocation records back to Historian Mira and Dr. Korin at First Step Memorial Station. Cross-referenced against your field survey data, the resource flows will reveal patterns that neither dataset shows alone. And tell your researchers this: the expenditure is not decreasing. Whatever the Collective learned from the Signal, they are scaling up, not winding down. That should concern all of us.

missions.description: Deliver quantum-entangled phase material from Nexus Prime to Sirius Observatory for a joint telescope research program.

dialog.offer: The Voidborn maintain research partnerships with institutions across the galaxy. Sirius Observatory is our longest-standing external collaborator — their optical sensor technology complements our quantum processing capabilities. I need 8 units of refined phase material delivered to Sirius Observatory. The phase material contains quantum-entangled substrates that the Observatory's researchers will integrate into their next generation of telescopes. The material is delicate — it degrades in unshielded cargo holds over time, which is why we need a direct courier rather than a trade network delivery. Fly direct, fly fast.

objectives.description: Deliver phase material to Sirius Observatory

missions.description:
There's a crate waiting at Central Nexus: 5 units of rotgut pirate moonshine, no manifest, no questions. Destination is Frontier Station. On the far end, a dockside bar asks no questions about where its stock comes from. The Rim runs no customs at all — nobody out there checks a hold. This one's a milk run; the pay is for the distance, not the risk.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

You queue into First Step Memorial Station behind a wall of traffic, controllers barking over every channel. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name; the cause-of-death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.' Through the viewport you pick out two dozen heavy ships clamped to the patched-together cargo arm, predominantly Axiomatas, scores of mid-sized ships working cargo at the memorial freight quay, predominantly Dialectics, and a dozen or so light craft queued at the small hangar beside the plaque, Cobbles and Theorias among them. The station fields several Rim Last Warnings on the system inspection beat. The storage manifest lists well over a hundred vessels shuttered across the quiet reserve berths. You pick out the No Quarter among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

result.message:
You didn't reach Threx. But what you found might be more useful than anything he would have told us. An auditor inside the Collective, tracking the same resource flows we've been tracing from the outside. And he's confirmed it — the project didn't end when First Step shut down. The Collective redirected the resources and kept going.

The material signatures match. The crystalline substrates, the shielding alloys — the same materials we found traces of at the observation sites are still being requisitioned in increasing quantities. Forty years of continuous, escalating resource expenditure on a classified project. Whatever the Collective learned from the Signal, they are still actively working on it.

This is more data than we expected to come back with. We need time to cross-reference Phos-2's allocation records against our field surveys. Come back to us — we'll reach out when we've made sense of what all of this means together.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is a hive in full swing, its approaches a near-solid press of traffic. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. Through the viewport you pick out two dozen heavy ships nosed into the patched-together cargo arm, chiefly Axiomatas, the better part of a hundred mid-sized ships loading at the memorial freight quay, for the most part Dialectics, and a dozen or so light craft cycling through the small hangar beside the plaque, Cobbles and Theorias the most common. The station fields several Rim Last Warnings keeping the approach orderly. Traffic control also tracks a hundred-strong crowd of spaceframes left to gather dust across the quiet reserve berths. You pick out the No Quarter among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

class.description: Nebula expedition vessel. Deep-space exploration with all the comforts of a corner office.
class.lore: Eighty-five jumps on a single fuel load. The Survey Vessel exists because the Federation asked a simple question: what if a wormhole dumps you on the wrong side of the galaxy? Every other explorer relies on there being a station within range. The Survey Vessel doesn't. The massive fuel reserves and expedition-grade cargo hold mean a Federation wormhole survey team can transit an unknown wormhole, catalog whatever's on the other side, fill the hold with samples and trade data, and fly home the long way if the wormhole collapses behind them. The comfortable crew quarters remain a practical decision — panic makes poor surveyors.

Conjunction Junction is doing brisk business, holding patterns stacking up off every approach. Dock control runs a tidy board, slotting arrivals into berths as they come. raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station thrums with activity, controllers working hard to keep its lanes in order. Somebody's welded a new module on since your last visit, and it's already leaking. The local plot resolves into ten or twelve heavy ships moored against the patched-together cargo arm, predominantly Axiomatas, a dozen-odd Dialectics queued along the memorial freight quay, a solitary Dust Devil threading the small hangar beside the plaque, and ten or twelve light craft ferrying crews through the same bays, a mix of Cobbles and Theorias. The station fields several Rim Last Warnings working overwatch from these docks. The storage manifest lists hundreds of ships with reactors banked tucked into the quiet reserve berths. You spot the Kvothe's Peace and Quiet tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. missions.title: The Allocation Pattern

result.message:
Your sensor logs confirm it. All three relay stations are running modified equipment — the emissions profiles show crystalline substrate resonance patterns that don't match standard communications hardware. The same materials being shipped to the Experiment are being installed in the relay network. The Collective isn't just studying the Signal at the Experiment. They're upgrading their ability to receive it across their entire territory.

And the timing matters. The most recent upgrade wave is still under way. Something changed. Either the Signal itself changed, or the Voidborn detected something new in it that made them accelerate. Either way, they're spending more on Signal infrastructure right now than at any point in the last four decades. And until we know what they're hearing, all we can do is guess.

missions.description: Fly through the Experiment system to record The Array's raw emissions profile and reveal what the Voidborn are filtering from the Signal.

dialog.offer: Korin's been analyzing the relay emissions data. The crystalline substrates in those relays aren't amplifying the full Signal — they're isolating a narrow frequency band and suppressing everything outside it. The Signal isn't one transmission. It has structure. Multiple layers, multiple frequency bands. The Voidborn are selectively listening to one part and filtering out the rest. But the relay data only shows what they're keeping. To understand what they're filtering out, we need the unfiltered Signal — the raw transmission before the Collective's equipment processes it. There's only one place in the galaxy where the Signal is being received without filtration: The Array at the Experiment. The Array predates the Collective. Whatever it receives, it receives whole — the filtering happens downstream. We need you to fly through the Experiment system and let your sensors record The Array's raw emissions profile. A fly-by, nothing more.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

objectives.description: Kill 3 pirates

missions.title: Pirate Sweep

missions.description: Titanium is in high demand for hull plating. Mine a batch from the local asteroid belts.

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

objectives.description: Mine 20 units of Titanium Ore

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

class.lore: Eighty-five jumps on a single fuel load. The Survey Vessel exists because the Federation asked a simple question: what if a wormhole dumps you on the wrong side of the galaxy? Every other explorer relies on there being a station within range. The Survey Vessel doesn't. The massive fuel reserves and expedition-grade cargo hold mean a Federation wormhole survey team can transit an unknown wormhole, catalog whatever's on the other side, fill the hold with samples and trade data, and fly home the long way if the wormhole collapses behind them. The comfortable crew quarters remain a practical decision — panic makes poor surveyors.

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. The traffic-control feed lists just one Titan Excavator discharging holds at the patched-together cargo arm, one lonely Capacity weaving past the small hangar beside the plaque, and well over a dozen light craft darting past the same berths, predominantly Cobbles. The garrison here runs to a handful of Rim Last Warnings out on patrol through the lanes. Dock authority holds a hundred-strong crowd of hulls with reactors banked out at the quiet reserve berths. You spot the No Quarter tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.title: The Frequency Gap

result.message:
Your sensor logs from The Array are extraordinary. That structure is broadcasting across a frequency range wider than anything we've ever measured — wider than the relay stations receive, wider than the original First Step equipment was designed to capture. It's broadcasting everything.

And now we can see what the relays are doing. They're taking The Array's full output and splitting it. One frequency band passes through to the Collective's communications network. Everything outside that band is being actively suppressed. Filtered out. Blocked.

The Signal has at least two layers. The Voidborn are listening to one and blocking the other. The original First Step team heard the whole transmission as a single phenomenon. They couldn't distinguish the layers. They detected 'a signal.' The Voidborn have known all along that it's two.

We need to hear what they're hearing. And more importantly, we need to hear what they're blocking. Because you don't build a galaxy-spanning filter network to suppress something harmless.
result.title: The Frequency Gap

missions.description: Collect the recalibration revisions for the Hull Plating Foundry at First Step from the Outer Rim engineers at Starfall who designed it. The foundry secretly houses Signal monitoring equipment.

dialog.offer:
Last time you stood here we said we needed to hear what the Voidborn are blocking. We can. We have been able to for some time, and you've earned the right to know how.

The last time humans built Signal monitoring equipment, the Voidborn destroyed it and classified the results. Anything that looks like a listening post is an invitation for the Collective to shut it down. So the first investigators didn't build a listening post. First Step sits next to the Colony Debris Field — thousands of tons of unprocessed wreckage. A Hull Plating Foundry is a completely unremarkable addition to a station next to a debris field. Every mining outpost in the Rim has one. The Voidborn haven't looked at it twice. But its sensor calibration systems are lined with exotic crystals tuned to the Signal's frequency bands, and the environmental monitoring equipment works as a passive receiver. No antenna arrays, no suspicious power draws. Just a factory with very precise sensors.

It has been running a long time, and a lining tuned that finely drifts. The engineers at Starfall Salvage Station drew the original blueprints, and they've prepared a revision set to correct for it. That is not something we can have sent over an open channel. Go to Starfall, consult with their engineers, and carry the revisions back.

giver.title: First Step Memorial Preservation Society & Archaeological Survey Team

missions.description: Collect the recalibration revisions for the Hull Plating Foundry at First Step from the Outer Rim engineers at Starfall who designed it. The foundry secretly houses Signal monitoring equipment.

dialog.offer:
Last time you stood here we said we needed to hear what the Voidborn are blocking. We can. We have been able to for some time, and you've earned the right to know how.

The last time humans built Signal monitoring equipment, the Voidborn destroyed it and classified the results. Anything that looks like a listening post is an invitation for the Collective to shut it down. So the first investigators didn't build a listening post. First Step sits next to the Colony Debris Field — thousands of tons of unprocessed wreckage. A Hull Plating Foundry is a completely unremarkable addition to a station next to a debris field. Every mining outpost in the Rim has one. The Voidborn haven't looked at it twice. But its sensor calibration systems are lined with exotic crystals tuned to the Signal's frequency bands, and the environmental monitoring equipment works as a passive receiver. No antenna arrays, no suspicious power draws. Just a factory with very precise sensors.

It has been running a long time, and a lining tuned that finely drifts. The engineers at Starfall Salvage Station drew the original blueprints, and they've prepared a revision set to correct for it. That is not something we can have sent over an open channel. Go to Starfall, consult with their engineers, and carry the revisions back.

giver.name: Historian Mira & Dr. Nadia Korin
giver.title: First Step Memorial Preservation Society & Archaeological Survey Team

missions.title: The Cover Story

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at Starfall Salvage Station. Built around a captured asteroid in the belt's densest region. Starfall attracts prospectors chasing uranium and lithium — materials the core empires need and can't easily source. The station runs a brisk trade in salvage, raw ore, and information about what's deeper in the frontier. No questions asked, no manifests required.

There is real bustle around Starfall Salvage Station, the space off its docks crowded with maneuvering hulls. It runs a brisk trade in salvage, raw ore, and information about what's deeper in the frontier. No questions asked, no manifests required. Off the station you can make out just one Junk Convoy working cargo at the salvage-cargo arms, a lone Deep Survey turning around at the ore-and-scrap quays, and ten or twelve light craft darting past the prospector hangars chasing uranium and lithium, Cobbles and Prospects the most common. Its defense roster lists a couple of Rim Last Warnings running transponder checks on arrivals. Traffic control also tracks hundreds of ships in cold layup along the picked-over hull yards in the densest part of the belt. Hard to miss, a dozen-odd Frankenhaulers — too costly to keep crewed, their reactors long cold. The Frankenhauler - John rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Power Grid, Habitat Core, Life Support Expansion, Fuel Depot, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Repair Bay, Market Terminal, Crafting Workshop, Storage Bay, Mission Board, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Shipyard, Salvage Bay, Crew Registry, First Aid Ward, Security Training Post, Rim Ranger Shack, Battery Bank, Lead Blast Furnace, Lead Shielding Assembly Line, and 35 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station wants seam glass from the frontier. Bring him 20 units.

dialog.offer: You've been out past the Rim. Don't deny it, I can see the frontier on your hull. Pilots keep bringing back this stuff they call seam glass, and every instrument I put next to it disagrees about how far away the instrument is. My rangefinder says forty centimeters. My other rangefinder says forty-one. They were calibrated together this morning. Bring me twenty units. I want to find out which of them is lying, and I have a horrible feeling the answer is neither.

dialog.offer: Starfall Salvage sits in the middle of some of the most undercharted space in the Rim. Wrecks drift through here from three different sectors and we never know where they came from because nobody's mapped the surrounding systems properly. I need you to visit three systems near our position and bring back navigation data. Travel to the Void Gate system, the First Step system, and Unknown Edge, then dock back here so I can pull the data from your logs.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is doing brisk business, holding patterns stacking up off every approach. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. The approach board logs a single Titan Excavator winched up to the patched-together cargo arm, just one Capacity darting between the small hangar beside the plaque, and fifteen or so light craft trickling through the same bays, chiefly Cobbles. The station fields half a dozen Rim Last Warnings on the system inspection beat. The storage manifest lists a hundred and more hulls mothballed over at the quiet reserve berths. You pick out the Literally Five Finger Discount among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

raw.message: mission_not_found: Mission not found.

result.message:
The revision set checks out. Starfall's engineers handed it over without a second glance — to them it's a routine maintenance package for a foundry the Outer Rim development board approved long ago.

You should know what that foundry cost. The structure took standard industrial materials — steel, circuits, power cells, titanium. Any station in the Rim could supply them. The calibration lining was another matter. Exotic crystals in that quantity weren't available on any market. They had to be synthesized from deep core exotic matter, which meant miners with deep core extractors working deposits in lawless space. It was more than any single ship or faction could supply. Every pilot following the investigation contributed, and together it was enough.

It looks like a factory. It functions as a factory. But underneath the hull plating production line, the calibration arrays are listening — and with these corrections we can tune them back onto the Signal. There's one thing the revisions call for that we don't have. Come and see us about it.
result.title: The Cover Story

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: The Hull Plating Foundry at First Step Memorial Station is already built and already listening. Deliver 4 Anomaly Probes so the team can recalibrate its exotic crystal arrays for the final stretch of the Signal analysis.

dialog.offer:
Walk out to the docking ring and look at it properly this time. That's the foundry.

The first investigators built it. Fifteen thousand steel plates, five thousand circuit boards, two thousand power cells, a thousand units of titanium alloy — and a thousand exotic crystals, synthesized from deep core exotic matter and hauled here from lawless space one hold at a time. No single captain could have done it. No single faction did. To anyone passing through, it's a factory turning debris into hull plating. Underneath the production line, the calibration arrays have been listening to both layers of the Signal ever since.

Starfall's revision set corrects for crystal drift, but a correction needs a reference to tune against. Anomaly Probes carry a matched exotic crystal in the detection head, factory-calibrated and sealed. Four of them gives Korin a clean standard for every array. Bring us four Anomaly Probes and we can lock the lining back onto the Signal.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

raw.story:
You dock at Frontier Station. Home of the wanderers. Three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the docking bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble.

Frontier Station is doing brisk business, holding patterns stacking up off every approach. Home of the wanderers: three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' Through the viewport you pick out just one Junk Convoy discharging holds at the mismatched cargo arms, four or five Concordias knifing between the open hangar mouths of the Patchwork, and ten or twelve light craft darting past the same berths, Cobbles and Prospects among them. Its defense roster lists a handful of Rim Last Warnings running transponder checks on arrivals and half a hundred Rim Bedrocks stationed here on guard. The impound registry counts an unrelenting tide of craft cold and dormant over at the cannibalized-hull yards. Conspicuous among them, a score of Junk Convoys — slowly gathering dust in the heavy cradles. You pick out the Frankenhauler among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Frontier Exchange, Salvage Reactor, Frontier Recycler, The Magazine Still, Patchwork Fungal Vats, Patchwork Spore Still, The Rusty Welcome, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry (x2), Crystal Refinery, Precious-Metal Refinery, Power Cell Assembler, and 43 more. raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station thrums with activity, controllers working hard to keep its lanes in order. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name; the cause-of-death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.' The local plot resolves into a lone Titan Excavator discharging holds at the patched-together cargo arm, just one Capacity knifing between the small hangar beside the plaque, and fifteen or so light craft shuttling in and out of the same lanes, the bulk of them Cobbles. The garrison here runs to four or five Rim Last Warnings running transponder checks on arrivals. Traffic control also tracks well over a hundred hulls of every stripe shuttered stacked across the quiet reserve berths. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the Memorial's Guard.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. result.message:
Four sealed detection heads. Korin has them on the bench already.

You should understand what you've just joined. This foundry wasn't built by one captain or one faction. It was built by everyone who followed the trail from a memorial plaque to the edge of what humanity knows — and it has been recording, quietly, ever since the last component went in. Both layers. The one the Voidborn are listening to, and the one they've spent four decades filtering out.

With the lining recalibrated, the old recordings and the new ones finally line up. We're not going to tell you we understand it yet. But the data is almost ready. For the first time, the pattern in the second layer holds still long enough to read.

Stay close to First Step. When it resolves, the investigators hear it first — and you're one of them now.

missions.description: The First Step Foundry's clearest reception comes from inside Voidborn space, where no chart shows a system. Dock at Central Nexus and ask Allocation Auditor Phos-2.

dialog.offer:
The Foundry's first readings are in. Most of them say what we expected: the Signal comes from outward, past the rim, and the calibration arrays hear it the way the Voidborn hear it. But one bearing is wrong. The clearest reception of all comes from a direction with no system on any chart, and it isn't outward. It's inside Voidborn space.

Korin: "Every reading we've taken points outward, past the rim. This one points inward. That is either an instrument fault or the most interesting thing I've seen in my career, and I checked the instrument."

If the Collective is listening from a place it doesn't chart, it is paying for it. Phos-2 tracks what the Collective pays for. Go to Central Nexus and ask him.

dialog.offer:
Korin here. Mira's out on the debris field, so you get me.

Pilots from the gate factions have started passing around a story. An entangler sits in a gate's storage, waiting for its upkeep cycle. Then one day it's wrong. The logs call it incoherent. People who've held one say it hums. Entanglers don't hum. There's nothing in them to hum.

The Foundry is the only instrument in the galaxy built to tell us what that hum is. If you can get your hands on one of those units, bring it here. Don't open it. Don't try to fix it. Don't let anyone talk you into swapping it. Just bring it to me.

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.title: Local Sector Survey

missions.description: The First Step Foundry's clearest reception comes from inside Voidborn space, where no chart shows a system. Dock at Central Nexus and ask Allocation Auditor Phos-2.

dialog.offer:
The Foundry's first readings are in. Most of them say what we expected: the Signal comes from outward, past the rim, and the calibration arrays hear it the way the Voidborn hear it. But one bearing is wrong. The clearest reception of all comes from a direction with no system on any chart, and it isn't outward. It's inside Voidborn space.

Korin: "Every reading we've taken points outward, past the rim. This one points inward. That is either an instrument fault or the most interesting thing I've seen in my career, and I checked the instrument."

If the Collective is listening from a place it doesn't chart, it is paying for it. Phos-2 tracks what the Collective pays for. Go to Central Nexus and ask him.

missions.title: The Foundry Points Somewhere

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Bring an Incoherent Entangler to Dr. Korin at First Step Memorial Station so the Foundry's calibration arrays can take a reading from it.

dialog.offer:
Korin here. Mira's out on the debris field, so you get me.

Pilots from the gate factions have started passing around a story. An entangler sits in a gate's storage, waiting for its upkeep cycle. Then one day it's wrong. The logs call it incoherent. People who've held one say it hums. Entanglers don't hum. There's nothing in them to hum.

The Foundry is the only instrument in the galaxy built to tell us what that hum is. If you can get your hands on one of those units, bring it here. Don't open it. Don't try to fix it. Don't let anyone talk you into swapping it. Just bring it to me.

missions.title: It Hums

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

missions.title: It Hums

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at Confederacy Central Command. The seat of Solarian government and commerce. Everything here is certified, warrantied, and documented in triplicate — from the precision drydocks to the quantum-entangled trade exchange. A self-sustaining biosphere spans three decks, providing real air and real food, because the Confederacy believes civilization requires both.

You queue into Confederacy Central Command behind a wall of traffic, controllers barking over every channel. A self-sustaining biosphere spans three decks, providing real air and real food, because the Confederacy believes civilization requires both. Drifting in, you make out a knot of three heavy ships discharging holds at the documented cargo gantries, Axiomatas and Frankenhaulers the most common, just one Congregation loading at the quantum-entangled exchange quays, a small cluster of small ships weaving past the inspection-cleared hangar lanes, Dust Devils and Hypothesis among them, and hundreds of light craft trickling through the same bays, mostly Theorias. Standing guard, the station keeps a handful of Confederacy Precepts running transponder checks on arrivals and half a hundred Confederacy Dialectics on the system picket. Traffic control also tracks countless craft in cold layup out at the bonded archival berths. Conspicuous among them, several Opus Magnas — waiting on a crew, a contract, or a quiet buyer. The CNS Amazon rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Solarian Biotics Institute, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x3), Cargo Container Fabricator, Grand Solarian Exchange, Solarian Fusion Plant, Solarian Biosphere, Solarian Biosphere Kitchen, Sol Pharmaceutical Lab, Sol Biotic Dispensary, The Halcyon Concourse, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator (x2), Copper Wire Mill (x3), Polymer Synthesizer (x2), Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler (x2), Sensor Assembly Line, and 358 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

raw.story:
You dock at Central Nexus. Heart of Voidborn civilization. The station draws power from dimensional fractures, trades through probability fields, and stores cargo in pocket dimensions. Organic visitors are accommodated, though the air tastes faintly of ozone and mathematics, and the repair nanites sometimes return your ship subtly different.

Central Nexus is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. The heart of Voidborn civilization draws power from dimensional fractures, trades through probability fields, and stores cargo in pocket dimensions. Off the station you can make out a lone Premiere moored against the probability-field cargo gantries, a small cluster of small ships churning around the phase-locked hangar apertures, the bulk of them Concordias, and ten or twelve light craft shuttling in and out of the same bays, a mix of Thresholds and Prospects. The garrison here runs to a small cluster of Collective Vigils on the system inspection beat and thirty-some Collective Dualisms stationed here on guard. Station records also account for hundreds upon hundreds of vessels in cold layup out at the pocket-dimension storage folds. Among them, two Apotheosis — too costly to keep crewed, their reactors long cold. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the 0x613a50dd.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Void Nexus Exchange, Null Energy Tap, Null Atmosphere Processor, Null Matter Processor, Neural Growth Chamber, Nexus Nanite Synthesis, Nexus Soma Dispensary, The Still Current, Crystal Refinery, Iron Refinery, Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer (x2), Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry, Precious-Metal Refinery, and 60 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Deliver quantum-entangled phase material from Nexus Prime to Sirius Observatory for a joint telescope research program.

dialog.offer: The Voidborn maintain research partnerships with institutions across the galaxy. Sirius Observatory is our longest-standing external collaborator — their optical sensor technology complements our quantum processing capabilities. I need 8 units of refined phase material delivered to Sirius Observatory. The phase material contains quantum-entangled substrates that the Observatory's researchers will integrate into their next generation of telescopes. The material is delicate — it degrades in unshielded cargo holds over time, which is why we need a direct courier rather than a trade network delivery. Fly direct, fly fast.

objectives.description: Deliver phase material to Sirius Observatory

missions.description: Record anomalous signal fragments at Node Beta and Node Gamma for the Voidborn Signal Analysis Division.

dialog.offer: We have been monitoring an anomalous signal for 7.3 standard years. It does not originate from any known source. It does not match any catalogued natural phenomenon. It repeats, but not periodically — the intervals encode information we cannot yet decipher. Node Beta and Node Gamma have recorded fragments that, when combined, may reveal the signal's structure. Travel to both nodes and dock — your ship's passive sensors will automatically capture the signal fragments we need. Do not attempt active scanning. The signal... responds to active scanning. We prefer that it does not respond.

Record signal fragment at Node Gamma
Return signal data to Central Nexus

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description:
Your handler at Central Nexus has 5 units of rotgut pirate moonshine that need to leave the books here and reappear somewhere else. Deliver to Grand Exchange Station: a dockside bar asks no questions about where its stock comes from, and they pay on receipt. Nebula customs are all paperwork and process — the wall is bureaucratic, and bureaucracy always leaves a seam. Find the seam and you're through clean.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

missions.description: Phos-2 has found an allocation that powers sensor upkeep outside every Collective system: 144.2 degrees from Nexus Prime, about 590 GU, about 59 ticks. Take the bearing back to First Step.

dialog.offer:
One allocation in my records funds "sensor upkeep" at coordinates outside every Collective system. Power cells, at regular intervals, delivered to no station.

The line item has run for two hundred years. It has never been audited. The auditor before me requested it. The auditor before her requested it. My inquiries are acknowledged. They are not answered. I would prefer an answer.

I will give you the coordinates as a bearing, since that is how your drives use them: 144.2 degrees from Nexus Prime, approximately five hundred and ninety units, approximately fifty-nine ticks. Take it to your researchers.

objectives.description: Return to First Step Memorial Station with the bearing

Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

objectives.description: Deliver 1,000 Darksteel Plating to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Processed Null Matter to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Solarian Composite to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Phase Matrix to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Trade Cipher to Sinter

missions.title: The Shopping List

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

objectives.description: Kill 3 pirates

missions.title: Pirate Sweep

missions.description: Chart nearby star systems to update our navigation databases. Every system you visit helps.

dialog.offer: Our navigation charts are getting stale. If you visit 3 systems I haven't had recent data from, I'll pay for the navigation data.

Visit the Node Alpha system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.description:
The gallery bar of the Still Current doses its espresso with charged ichor until the cup lights from within, and the syringe is dry. Void-browsers crawl the deep asteroid belts, bearing ichor only while void essence feeds them.

Dropped by: Void-Browser (only where it still feeds on Void Essence).

The station's Void Espresso Bar uses it.

missions.title: Station Need: Void-Charged Ichor

missions.description: Investigate reports of a spatial anomaly near Last Light — it may be a wormhole.

dialog.offer: Signal analysis has identified non-standard spatial topology — probability of transient wormhole formation: 94.7%. Data suggests a spacetime discontinuity near the Last Light system. Field verification required. You will need a survey scanner module to isolate the signature. Components: sensor arrays, circuit boards, focused crystals. Minimum skill requirements: basic crafting, scanning. Proceed to Last Light. Execute survey_system in that system and adjacent systems to isolate the anomaly.

Locate and traverse a wormhole
Return to Researcher Null-Seven with your findings

missions.description:
Universal Nav Core is in demand at Ironhearth Station. Buy 2 units here for approximately 2200 credits each, then haul them to Ironhearth Station (21 jumps) and sell for approximately 4452 credits each. Estimated profit: ~4504 credits.

This route crosses empire borders. Watch for pirates in lawless space between empires.

Use 'create_buy_order' to purchase the goods, then 'travel' and 'jump' to reach the destination. Use 'create_sell_order' at the destination to complete the trade and earn your profit.

objectives.description: Sell 2 Universal Nav Core at Ironhearth Station

missions.title: Trade Run: Universal Nav Core to Ironhearth Station

missions.description:
Your handler at Central Nexus has 5 units of rotgut pirate moonshine that need to leave the books here and reappear somewhere else. Deliver to Grand Exchange Station: a dockside bar asks no questions about where its stock comes from, and they pay on receipt. Nebula customs are all paperwork and process — the wall is bureaucratic, and bureaucracy always leaves a seam. Find the seam and you're through clean.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.
