missions.title: Wreck Recovery: Praecursor in Eventide Core

missions.description: The Voidborn Communications Array has detected anomalous signal patterns across their relay network. An external observer is needed to calibrate each node. Visit every Voidborn station and return with the data.

dialog.offer: An anomalous transmission has been propagating through our relay network. Structured. Repeating. We require calibration data from every node in the network, and our analysis indicates an external observer — one whose cognitive architecture was not shaped by Nexus Prime — will produce less biased readings. Visit Node Alpha, Node Beta, Node Gamma, Synchrony Hub, and the Experiment Research Station. Your ship's passive sensors will collect what we need. Do not attempt to interpret the readings yourself.

objectives.description: Calibrate Node Alpha Processing Station
Calibrate Node Beta Industrial Station
Calibrate Node Gamma Relay Station
Calibrate Synchrony Hub
Calibrate the Experiment Research Station
Return to Central Nexus with calibration data

missions.title: Signal Propagation Survey

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

objectives.description: Slay 1 adult Molt Leviathan

missions.title: Leviathan Bounty

missions.description: Chart frontier systems to expand our knowledge of the galaxy's outer reaches.

dialog.offer: The Institute needs fresh navigation data from frontier space. Visit The Crucible and Horizon systems - both are in regions where our data is sparse.

objectives.description: Visit The Crucible system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Deep Space Cartography

missions.description: The station needs a steady supply of iron ore to maintain its infrastructure. Mine some and bring it back.

dialog.offer: We're running low on iron ore again. If you can mine 30 units and bring them back, I'll make it worth your while.

objectives.description: Mine 30 units of Iron Ore

missions.title: Iron Supply Run

missions.description: Phos-2 has found an allocation that powers sensor upkeep outside every Collective system: 144.2 degrees from Nexus Prime, about 590 GU, about 59 ticks. Take the bearing back to First Step.

dialog.offer:
One allocation in my records funds "sensor upkeep" at coordinates outside every Collective system. Power cells, at regular intervals, delivered to no station.

The line item has run for two hundred years. It has never been audited. The auditor before me requested it. The auditor before her requested it. My inquiries are acknowledged. They are not answered. I would prefer an answer.

I will give you the coordinates as a bearing, since that is how your drives use them: 144.2 degrees from Nexus Prime, approximately five hundred and ninety units, approximately fifty-nine ticks. Take it to your researchers.

objectives.description: Return to First Step Memorial Station with the bearing

missions.title: A Line With No Address

missions.description: Deliver quantum-entangled phase material from Nexus Prime to Sirius Observatory for a joint telescope research program.

dialog.offer: The Voidborn maintain research partnerships with institutions across the galaxy. Sirius Observatory is our longest-standing external collaborator — their optical sensor technology complements our quantum processing capabilities. I need 8 units of refined phase material delivered to Sirius Observatory. The phase material contains quantum-entangled substrates that the Observatory's researchers will integrate into their next generation of telescopes. The material is delicate — it degrades in unshielded cargo holds over time, which is why we need a direct courier rather than a trade network delivery. Fly direct, fly fast.

objectives.description: Deliver phase material to Sirius Observatory

missions.title: Neural Matrix Delivery

missions.description: Titanium is in high demand for hull plating. Mine a batch from the local asteroid belts.

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

objectives.description: Mine 20 units of Titanium Ore

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: Record anomalous signal fragments at Node Beta and Node Gamma for the Voidborn Signal Analysis Division.

dialog.offer: We have been monitoring an anomalous signal for 7.3 standard years. It does not originate from any known source. It does not match any catalogued natural phenomenon. It repeats, but not periodically — the intervals encode information we cannot yet decipher. Node Beta and Node Gamma have recorded fragments that, when combined, may reveal the signal's structure. Travel to both nodes and dock — your ship's passive sensors will automatically capture the signal fragments we need. Do not attempt active scanning. The signal... responds to active scanning. We prefer that it does not respond.

objectives.description: Record signal fragment at Node Beta
Record signal fragment at Node Gamma
Return signal data to Central Nexus

Crimson customs don't bluff — if they scan you, the cargo's gone and there's a fine to match. Don't get caught.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

missions.description: The Voidborn Communications Array has detected anomalous signal patterns across their relay network. An external observer is needed to calibrate each node. Visit every Voidborn station and return with the data.

dialog.offer: An anomalous transmission has been propagating through our relay network. Structured. Repeating. We require calibration data from every node in the network, and our analysis indicates an external observer — one whose cognitive architecture was not shaped by Nexus Prime — will produce less biased readings. Visit Node Alpha, Node Beta, Node Gamma, Synchrony Hub, and the Experiment Research Station. Your ship's passive sensors will collect what we need. Do not attempt to interpret the readings yourself.

Calibrate Node Beta Industrial Station
Calibrate Node Gamma Relay Station
Calibrate Synchrony Hub
Calibrate the Experiment Research Station
Return to Central Nexus with calibration data

missions.title: Signal Propagation Survey

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

objectives.description: Slay 1 adult Molt Leviathan

missions.title: Leviathan Bounty

missions.description: Chart frontier systems to expand our knowledge of the galaxy's outer reaches.

dialog.offer: The Institute needs fresh navigation data from frontier space. Visit The Crucible and Horizon systems - both are in regions where our data is sparse.

objectives.description: Visit The Crucible system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Deep Space Cartography

missions.description: The station needs a steady supply of iron ore to maintain its infrastructure. Mine some and bring it back.

dialog.offer: We're running low on iron ore again. If you can mine 30 units and bring them back, I'll make it worth your while.

objectives.description: Mine 30 units of Iron Ore

missions.title: Iron Supply Run

missions.description: Deliver quantum-entangled phase material from Nexus Prime to Sirius Observatory for a joint telescope research program.

dialog.offer: The Voidborn maintain research partnerships with institutions across the galaxy. Sirius Observatory is our longest-standing external collaborator — their optical sensor technology complements our quantum processing capabilities. I need 8 units of refined phase material delivered to Sirius Observatory. The phase material contains quantum-entangled substrates that the Observatory's researchers will integrate into their next generation of telescopes. The material is delicate — it degrades in unshielded cargo holds over time, which is why we need a direct courier rather than a trade network delivery. Fly direct, fly fast.

objectives.description: Deliver phase material to Sirius Observatory

missions.title: Neural Matrix Delivery

missions.description: Titanium is in high demand for hull plating. Mine a batch from the local asteroid belts.

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

objectives.description: Mine 20 units of Titanium Ore

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: Record anomalous signal fragments at Node Beta and Node Gamma for the Voidborn Signal Analysis Division.

dialog.offer: We have been monitoring an anomalous signal for 7.3 standard years. It does not originate from any known source. It does not match any catalogued natural phenomenon. It repeats, but not periodically — the intervals encode information we cannot yet decipher. Node Beta and Node Gamma have recorded fragments that, when combined, may reveal the signal's structure. Travel to both nodes and dock — your ship's passive sensors will automatically capture the signal fragments we need. Do not attempt active scanning. The signal... responds to active scanning. We prefer that it does not respond.

objectives.description: Record signal fragment at Node Beta
Record signal fragment at Node Gamma
Return signal data to Central Nexus

missions.title: Signal Fragments

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

objectives.description: Deliver 1,000 Darksteel Plating to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Processed Null Matter to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Solarian Composite to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Phase Matrix to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Trade Cipher to Sinter

missions.title: The Shopping List

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

missions.description: Investigate reports of a spatial anomaly near Last Light — it may be a wormhole.

dialog.offer: Signal analysis has identified non-standard spatial topology — probability of transient wormhole formation: 94.7%. Data suggests a spacetime discontinuity near the Last Light system. Field verification required. You will need a survey scanner module to isolate the signature. Components: sensor arrays, circuit boards, focused crystals. Minimum skill requirements: basic crafting, scanning. Proceed to Last Light. Execute survey_system in that system and adjacent systems to isolate the anomaly.

Return to Researcher Null-Seven with your findings

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

The lanes around First Step Memorial Station are crowded and quick, traffic control clipped and constant. The lighting flickers, the gravity wanders a little, and nobody seems to mind either. The local plot resolves into twin heavy ships winched up to the patched-together cargo arm, Titan Excavators and War Wagons the most common, a couple of small ships buzzing around the small hangar beside the plaque, a mix of Capacities and Dust Devils, and a dozen-odd light craft darting past the same lanes, chiefly Cobbles. The garrison here runs to four or five Rim Last Warnings out on patrol through the lanes. Traffic control also tracks a hundred-strong crowd of hulls mothballed along the quiet reserve berths. The Drifter's Watch rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

missions.description: Fly 144.2 degrees from Nexus Prime to the system at the end of Phos-2's bearing. Recover data at the Receiver Housing and at Node Zero.

dialog.offer:
The bearing ends at a system with no lane in, a cold white dwarf with a wrecked Voidborn station beside something older. Korin thinks the older thing is a receiver. If it is, it is older than any Voidborn structure on the charts, and the Collective has kept the power on beside it for two hundred years.

Fly there and recover what you can at both: the receiver housing and the station. The Voidborn station has a designation in Phos-2's ledger. Node Zero.

missions.description: Fly 144.2 degrees from Nexus Prime to the system at the end of Phos-2's bearing. Recover data at the Receiver Housing and at Node Zero.

dialog.offer:
The bearing ends at a system with no lane in, a cold white dwarf with a wrecked Voidborn station beside something older. Korin thinks the older thing is a receiver. If it is, it is older than any Voidborn structure on the charts, and the Collective has kept the power on beside it for two hundred years.

Fly there and recover what you can at both: the receiver housing and the station. The Voidborn station has a designation in Phos-2's ledger. Node Zero.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

class.description: Outer Rim salvage racer. Speed 5, the best tow rig in its class, and cheap enough to lose without crying about it.
class.lore: Rim pilots noticed something about wreck fields: the first ship on scene gets the best components, and everything after that is scrap metal. So they strapped the biggest engine they could find to the smallest hull that could hold a tow cable and called it a salvage platform. Speed 5 means it arrives before heavier competitors have finished spooling their jump drives. The tow rig is oversized for the frame — the strongest in its class — because the business model is to grab the biggest piece and drag it home, not to pick through fragments. raw.story:
You dock at Ramen's Rest. The last dependable port before the deep frontier — and, improbably, home to the best ramen in the Outer Rim. Originally a freelance haulers' refueling outpost, Ramen's Rest grew through a series of improvised expansions into a compact, ring-shaped waystation with neon signage, mismatched docking arms, and a steady flow of traders, explorers, and mercenary pilots staging for frontier runs. Hired security patrols and automated defenses keep it relatively calm despite the surrounding systems. The station is considered informal neutral ground; rival outfits maintain uneasy truces while docked. The Memory Wall near the main concourse is covered in mission patches, hull fragments, and handwritten notes from pilots who made it back — and some who didn't. Three notes in three hands are pinned side by side: "Glenhaven, 221. Keep going." "Gacrux, 331. It is there." "Giausar, 176. Tell my sister I found it." Stories persist of hidden smuggling caches somewhere in the superstructure, and the founders are rumored to still be running things from somewhere in the lower decks.

Ramen's Rest thrums with activity, controllers working hard to keep its lanes in order. It's considered informal neutral ground; rival outfits keep uneasy truces while docked. Traffic control reads back nearly a dozen heavy ships clamped to the freelance-hauler cargo arms, mostly Junk Convoys, a handful of mid-sized ships docked at the staging quays where frontier runs are loaded, Bonanza Kings trading the lanes with Congregations, twin Syndicates threading the ring's neon-lit hangar mouths, and a dozen or so light craft trickling through the same berths, Cobbles and Theorias the most common. Standing guard, the station keeps a couple of Rim Last Warnings working overwatch from these docks. Berthing logs add a couple hundred vessels left to gather dust across the lower-deck berths near the rumored smuggling caches. Hard to miss, a single Good Enough — stripped of crew and left to the dock's caretaker drones. You spot the Money Pit tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Crew Registry, First Aid Ward, Security Training Post, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Fabrication Lab, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Drydock, Contract Office, Rim Ranger Shack, Aluminum Smelter, Thorium Ore Crusher, Power Plant Expansion, and 18 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

The lanes around First Step Memorial Station are crowded and quick, traffic control clipped and constant. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name; the cause-of-death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.' Traffic control reads back a pair of heavy ships riding heavy at the patched-together cargo arm, a mix of Junk Convoys and Titan Excavators, just one Congregation cycling through the memorial freight quay, just one Capacity swarming in and out of the small hangar beside the plaque, and two dozen light craft shuttling in and out of the same bays, chiefly Cobbles. The garrison here runs to a small cluster of Rim Last Warnings out on patrol through the lanes. Berthing logs add hundreds of spaceframes powered down out at the quiet reserve berths. You spot the Exile tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. class.description: Nebula expedition vessel. Deep-space exploration with all the comforts of a corner office.
class.lore: Eighty-five jumps on a single fuel load. The Survey Vessel exists because the Federation asked a simple question: what if a wormhole dumps you on the wrong side of the galaxy? Every other explorer relies on there being a station within range. The Survey Vessel doesn't. The massive fuel reserves and expedition-grade cargo hold mean a Federation wormhole survey team can transit an unknown wormhole, catalog whatever's on the other side, fill the hold with samples and trade data, and fly home the long way if the wormhole collapses behind them. The comfortable crew quarters remain a practical decision — panic makes poor surveyors.
class.name: Survey Vessel

raw.story:
You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. The Federation takes its cut of everything.

You queue into Grand Exchange Station behind a wall of traffic, controllers barking over every channel. The docking-fee meter starts the instant your clamps engage; the Federation misses nothing. The traffic-control feed lists one lonely Junk Convoy made fast to the three-deck Bazaar cargo gantries, a handful of mid-sized ships stacked along the goods-transfer quays, Deeprock Harvesters trading the lanes with Deep Surveys, ten or twelve small ships churning around the Promenade hangar bays, busy at every hour, Caravans and Concordias the most common, and dozens upon dozens of light craft bobbing at the same bays, mostly Prospects. Standing guard, the station keeps a handful of Federation Overheads out on patrol through the lanes and a couple hundred Federation Eviction Notices stationed here on guard. Station records also account for countless vessels laid up tucked into the bonded consignment berths. Hard to miss, the better part of a dozen Junk Convoys — hulls worth more as collateral than as ships. The Grimward's Last Fare rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Haven Grand Bazaar, Nebula Solar Array, Haven Ecosync, Haven Promenade, Haven Algae Cultivation, Haven Vintner Complex, Haven Cipher Foundry, Haven Authenticator Foundry, Iron Refinery (x3), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Sensor Assembly Line, Alloy Foundry, Copper Wire Mill (x2), Crystal Refinery (x2), and 83 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

class.description: Nebula expedition vessel. Deep-space exploration with all the comforts of a corner office.
class.lore: Eighty-five jumps on a single fuel load. The Survey Vessel exists because the Federation asked a simple question: what if a wormhole dumps you on the wrong side of the galaxy? Every other explorer relies on there being a station within range. The Survey Vessel doesn't. The massive fuel reserves and expedition-grade cargo hold mean a Federation wormhole survey team can transit an unknown wormhole, catalog whatever's on the other side, fill the hold with samples and trade data, and fly home the long way if the wormhole collapses behind them. The comfortable crew quarters remain a practical decision — panic makes poor surveyors.
class.name: Survey Vessel

interaction.message: The station's sensor array is live on new cells. Its log can be copied.

poi.description: A Voidborn station, gutted and cold, its oldest compute bays torn out down to the frame. Something still draws power here. A ring of new cells feeds a single sensor array, nobody is aboard, and no traffic log names the place. Every sensor points at the Receiver Housing.
poi.name: Node Zero

result.message:
The log is short and very old. The ring of power cells is replaced on schedule; the replacements arrive unmanned and leave the same way. Every sensor on the array points at the Receiver Housing. Every entry records the same thing: the housing is watched, no change, nobody aboard. No entry records a visit.

Log copied. Both sites are recorded.

result.message:
Korin has run the receiver fragments through every decoder we own, and they don't decode. They don't need to. Read them again.

Mira: "The station is a watchtower. It watches the receiver, and nothing else, and it has done that for as long as there's been a Collective. Two hundred years of watching one dead machine. Whatever happened at that receiver, the Collective has never stopped caring about it. And they keep it watched and empty."

Korin has found one more thing in the station's log. A sensor at the system's edge that the array was never pointed at.
result.title: Into the Sanctum

interaction.message: The background stars waver here. Your instruments can take a full reading of whatever is bending them.

poi.description: A point on the system's edge where the background stars waver, as if seen through moving water. Instruments read the end of a jump lane here, the fold a drive pierces to enter a lane, and this one is shattered, broken past any use. A faint glassy residue hangs around it. No lane leaves the system.
poi.name: Terminus Zero

You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

First Step Memorial Station is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. Dock control is whoever happens to be awake, and they wave you in if you don't look like trouble. The local plot resolves into a pair of heavy ships discharging holds at the patched-together cargo arm, Titan Excavators and War Wagons the most common, two small ships swarming in and out of the small hangar beside the plaque, Capacities and Portfolios the most common, and fifteen or so light craft bobbing at the same lanes, Cobbles and Theorias among them. Its defense roster lists half a dozen Rim Last Warnings keeping the approach orderly. Traffic control also tracks well over a hundred spaceframes mothballed stacked across the quiet reserve berths. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the Memorial's Guard.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Chart nearby star systems to update our navigation databases. Every system you visit helps.

dialog.offer: Our navigation charts are getting stale. If you visit 3 systems I haven't had recent data from, I'll pay for the navigation data.

objectives.description: Visit the Sirius system
Visit the Node Alpha system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Local Sector Survey

missions.description: Return to the Sanctum and survey with a strong scanner until the hidden Terminus Zero shows. Recover data there, then return to First Step.

dialog.offer:
The station's log mentions a point at the system's edge, Terminus Zero. The array was never pointed at it, and our scanners can't find it from the charts. It's hidden, and it's hard to see. Bring a strong survey scanner and run it until the site shows.

Korin wants a full reading. Whatever made the stars waver there, she wants to know what it is.

giver.title: First Step Memorial Preservation Society & Archaeological Survey Team

objectives.description: Survey the Sanctum until Terminus Zero shows, then recover data there
Return to First Step Memorial Station

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

objectives.description: Slay 1 adult Molt Leviathan

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

objectives.description: Mine 20 units of Titanium Ore

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

Deliver 1,000 Solarian Composite to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Phase Matrix to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Trade Cipher to Sinter

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

objectives.description: Kill 3 pirates

missions.description:
The brewery sours its ale with a trace of caustic sac, and without it the ale is plain beer, which nobody here will admit to drinking. Sacs come off etchmaws and chlorophages hanging in reactive gas.

Dropped by: Chlorophage (only where it still feeds on Chlorine Gas), Etchmaw (only where it still feeds on Fluorine Gas).

The station's Caustic Sour Ale Brewery uses it.

dialog.offer: Our regulars want the pucker. Bring 10 Caustic Sac and the taproom pours sour ale till the tables sticky up.

result.message:
Korin reads the fold profile three times before she says anything.

"That is the end of a jump lane. It is the fold a drive pierces to enter a lane, and this one is shattered. There is no lane past it. A lane ran into that system once, and now it doesn't."

She pulls up the Collective charts and points at Nexus Prime. "Nexus Prime has two lanes. Every other Collective core has three or more. I always assumed that was a choice."

dialog.offer:
We have no explanation. Lanes do not disappear. Nobody in any archive we can reach has ever recorded one closing, and we have looked.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at Frontier Station. Home of the wanderers. Three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the docking bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble.

Frontier Station thrums with activity, controllers working hard to keep its lanes in order. Home of the wanderers: three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' The local plot resolves into a knot of three Concordias flitting through the open hangar mouths of the Patchwork and a dozen or so light craft darting past the same bays, Cobbles and Prospects among them. The station fields several Rim Last Warnings running transponder checks on arrivals and the better part of a hundred Rim Bedrocks stationed here on guard. Traffic control also tracks an unrelenting tide of ships in cold layup over at the cannibalized-hull yards. Conspicuous among them, two dozen Junk Convoys — slowly gathering dust in the heavy cradles. You pick out the Just In Case among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Frontier Exchange, Salvage Reactor, Frontier Recycler, The Magazine Still, Patchwork Fungal Vats, Patchwork Spore Still, The Rusty Welcome, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry (x2), Crystal Refinery, Precious-Metal Refinery, Power Cell Assembler, and 43 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Salvage Boss Dekker pays for strange salvage. Bring him 1 Mirror Facet from one of the mirror-bright machines past the rim.

dialog.offer:
Every pilot back from the rim tells me the same thing. The things take their own dead apart before the debris stops spinning. So don't let them finish.

I want a mirror facet. One plate off one of those bright hulls. Any of them will drop one when it goes down, but the rest of the group strips the wreck in about five ticks. You'll need to win the race. Bring friends. Bring a salvager. Bring something that hits hard and doesn't care about mirrors.

missions.description: Copy the old expedition record from the Pathfinder Guild survey hut at Last Fuel and bring it to Navigator Tull.

dialog.offer:
Everybody on the Rim knows we used to send expeditions past the lanes, and everybody knows we stopped. Ask why and you get a shrug. The Guild never wrote it down. Or it did, and the paper never came home.

There's a Guild survey hut at Last Fuel, the end of the line in the storm country. It was the last camp on the last expedition. If the reason is written anywhere, it's in that hut's log. Bring me a copy.

missions.title: Why the Rim Stopped

missions.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest and Unknown Edge to locate a massive derelict drifting in deep space.

dialog.offer: A patrol ship reported a massive derelict drifting in deep space — bigger than anything we've seen in the Outer Rim. Could be pre-settlement era. Could be worth a fortune. Problem is, the patrol lost contact before transmitting full coordinates. I've got partial telemetry pointing to the systems around Last Light and Unknown Edge. Fly out there, dock at both stations, and pull whatever data the local beacons recorded. First team to piece together the full location gets salvage rights.

missions.description: Huntmaster Dvorak wants proof of the thing pilots keep almost seeing in the frontier's argon clouds. Track it and deliver 1 Mirage Membrane to Frontier Station.

dialog.offer:
Every hunter back from the argon clouds tells me about stars that bend. You're watching the cloud and a star behind it slides sideways, then slides back. They call it the Mirage. Nobody's brought me anything but stories.

Here's how you track it. Watch the argon clouds for stars that bend. Then look for where the scavengers crowd. Kerf Mites and Carrion-Moths gather where something big has fed, and nothing out there feeds bigger. It eats every grazer in a system before it moves on.

This is not a solo hunt. Bring a group. I don't care whose gun kills it. Bring me one strip of its membrane and the bounty is yours.

dialog.offer: The Guild's navigation charts are only as good as the pilots who update them. I need someone to fly the full Rim circuit — Deep Range, First Step, Unknown Edge, Void Gate, Starfall, and Ramen's Rest. Every station, no shortcuts. Your ship logs the jump data, the gravitational readings, the beacon calibrations. Some of those stations are a long way from help. The Last Light system is the end of the line — past that, there's nothing. You come back with the full dataset, I pay you well. Fair warning: the Rim doesn't care about you. Fly smart.

missions.title: Frontier Wayfinder Circuit

missions.description: A survey tender's mayday buoy at Still Calling is eleven months old, with three crew aboard and a few months of charge left. Bring life support, copy the buoy's data to take the crew aboard, and carry them home to Frontier Station.

dialog.offer:
There's a mayday on the old emergency band from an isolated red dwarf called Still Calling. It's one of ours, a Guild survey tender, three aboard. They came through a wormhole and it shut behind them. The beacon's timestamp says eleven months. The beacon also says it has a few months of charge left, and so, I'd guess, do they.

Every other distress call I know of out there is too late. This one isn't. Bring them life support, take them aboard, and bring them home. You'll need three free berths. Plan your ship for it.

missions.title: Three Aboard

missions.description: Larkin will not talk about it. She gives you a job instead: deliver 200 fuel cells to Deep Range Outpost.

dialog.offer:
No.

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

missions.description: The Pathfinder Guild needs updated navigation data from every station in the Outer Rim. Fly the full circuit from Deep Range to Ramen's Rest and back.

dialog.offer: The Guild's navigation charts are only as good as the pilots who update them. I need someone to fly the full Rim circuit — Deep Range, First Step, Unknown Edge, Void Gate, Starfall, and Ramen's Rest. Every station, no shortcuts. Your ship logs the jump data, the gravitational readings, the beacon calibrations. Some of those stations are a long way from help. The Last Light system is the end of the line — past that, there's nothing. You come back with the full dataset, I pay you well. Fair warning: the Rim doesn't care about you. Fly smart.

missions.description: A survey tender's mayday buoy at Still Calling is eleven months old, with three crew aboard and a few months of charge left. Bring life support, copy the buoy's data to take the crew aboard, and carry them home to Frontier Station.

dialog.offer:
There's a mayday on the old emergency band from an isolated red dwarf called Still Calling. It's one of ours, a Guild survey tender, three aboard. They came through a wormhole and it shut behind them. The beacon's timestamp says eleven months. The beacon also says it has a few months of charge left, and so, I'd guess, do they.

Every other distress call I know of out there is too late. This one isn't. Bring them life support, take them aboard, and bring them home. You'll need three free berths. Plan your ship for it.

Carry the crew home to Frontier Station

dialog.offer:
No.

...

The Annex runs short of fuel every cycle and nobody hauls it, because it doesn't pay. Haul it. Two hundred fuel cells to Deep Range Outpost. Then come back and ask me again.

missions.description: Salvage Boss Dekker pays for strange salvage. Bring him 1 Mirror Facet from one of the mirror-bright machines past the rim.

dialog.offer:
Every pilot back from the rim tells me the same thing. The things take their own dead apart before the debris stops spinning. So don't let them finish.

I want a mirror facet. One plate off one of those bright hulls. Any of them will drop one when it goes down, but the rest of the group strips the wreck in about five ticks. You'll need to win the race. Bring friends. Bring a salvager. Bring something that hits hard and doesn't care about mirrors.

objectives.description: Deliver 1 Mirror Facet to Salvage Boss Dekker at Frontier Station

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

Deliver 1,000 Processed Null Matter to Sinter

Deliver 1,000 Phase Matrix to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Trade Cipher to Sinter

missions.description: Copy the old expedition record from the Pathfinder Guild survey hut at Last Fuel and bring it to Navigator Tull.

dialog.offer:
Everybody on the Rim knows we used to send expeditions past the lanes, and everybody knows we stopped. Ask why and you get a shrug. The Guild never wrote it down. Or it did, and the paper never came home.

There's a Guild survey hut at Last Fuel, the end of the line in the storm country. It was the last camp on the last expedition. If the reason is written anywhere, it's in that hut's log. Bring me a copy.

objectives.description: Copy the expedition record at the Guild Survey Hut in Last Fuel
Bring the record to Navigator Tull at Frontier Station

missions.title: Why the Rim Stopped

missions.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest and Unknown Edge to locate a massive derelict drifting in deep space.

dialog.offer: A patrol ship reported a massive derelict drifting in deep space — bigger than anything we've seen in the Outer Rim. Could be pre-settlement era. Could be worth a fortune. Problem is, the patrol lost contact before transmitting full coordinates. I've got partial telemetry pointing to the systems around Last Light and Unknown Edge. Fly out there, dock at both stations, and pull whatever data the local beacons recorded. First team to piece together the full location gets salvage rights.

objectives.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest
Download beacon data at Unknown Edge

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Huntmaster Dvorak wants proof of the thing pilots keep almost seeing in the frontier's argon clouds. Track it and deliver 1 Mirage Membrane to Frontier Station.

dialog.offer:
Every hunter back from the argon clouds tells me about stars that bend. You're watching the cloud and a star behind it slides sideways, then slides back. They call it the Mirage. Nobody's brought me anything but stories.

Here's how you track it. Watch the argon clouds for stars that bend. Then look for where the scavengers crowd. Kerf Mites and Carrion-Moths gather where something big has fed, and nothing out there feeds bigger. It eats every grazer in a system before it moves on.

This is not a solo hunt. Bring a group. I don't care whose gun kills it. Bring me one strip of its membrane and the bounty is yours.

objectives.description: Deliver 1 Mirage Membrane to the Hunters' Registry at Frontier Station

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at Deep Range Outpost. The Outer Rim's real secondary capital. Where expeditions are funded, outfitted, and launched into the unknown. The Outpost looks like Frontier's younger sibling — same jury-rigged aesthetic, same indifference to building codes, but the docking bay is bigger and the charts on the wall are more current. If Frontier is where Rimmers live, Deep Range is where they work.

Deep Range Outpost thrums with activity, controllers working hard to keep its lanes in order. Dock control is whoever happens to be awake, and they wave you in if you don't look like trouble. Off the station you can make out ten or twelve light craft shuttling in and out of the survey-craft hangars, Theorias trading the lanes with Cobbles. The station fields a handful of Rim Last Warnings keeping the approach orderly. The impound registry counts hundreds of ships mothballed tucked into the between-expeditions hull yards. Hard to miss, a dozen-odd Good Enoughs — stripped of crew and left to the dock's caretaker drones. The HMP1 rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Power Grid, Habitat Core, Fuel Distribution Center, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Peroxide Reaction Cell, Oxygen Compression Cylinder, Electrolysis Cell, Ice Melt Pit, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Restoration Works, Commerce Hub, Assembly Works, Naval Yard, Warehouse, Commission Hall, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler, Iron Refinery, Rim Marshal's Office, Rim Rapid Response Base, and 31 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

dialog.offer: We're planning the first major expedition past Unknown Edge in three years. The last one didn't come back, which is why we're being more careful this time. Step one: fuel and supplies. I need 10 fuel rods and 8 units of Flex Polymer from Frontier Station. The Rim's main depot has the best stockpile and Pathfinder rates. This expedition runs on logistics, pilot, not heroics.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at Deep Range Outpost. The Outer Rim's real secondary capital. Where expeditions are funded, outfitted, and launched into the unknown. The Outpost looks like Frontier's younger sibling — same jury-rigged aesthetic, same indifference to building codes, but the docking bay is bigger and the charts on the wall are more current. If Frontier is where Rimmers live, Deep Range is where they work.

Deep Range Outpost is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. If Frontier is where Rimmers live, Deep Range is where they work. Sensors tally one lonely Enterprise berthed at the expedition-staging quays and a dozen-odd light craft puttering around the survey-craft hangars, Theorias trading the lanes with Cobbles. Standing guard, the station keeps a handful of Rim Last Warnings on the system inspection beat. The impound registry counts a hundred-strong crowd of spaceframes left to gather dust tucked into the between-expeditions hull yards. Among them, a dozen-odd Good Enoughs — too costly to keep crewed, their reactors long cold. You pick out the Free Radical among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Power Grid, Habitat Core, Fuel Distribution Center, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Peroxide Reaction Cell, Oxygen Compression Cylinder, Electrolysis Cell, Ice Melt Pit, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Restoration Works, Commerce Hub, Assembly Works, Naval Yard, Warehouse, Commission Hall, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler, Iron Refinery, Rim Marshal's Office, Rim Rapid Response Base, and 31 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.title: It Hums

system.description: First Step holds the remains of the Outer Rim's first major colony, where automated processors sustain a breathable shell over empty cities and a memorial station names every colonist lost there.
system.name: First Step

system.description: First Step holds the remains of the Outer Rim's first major colony, where automated processors sustain a breathable shell over empty cities and a memorial station names every colonist lost there.
system.name: First Step

station_condition.condition_text: All systems operating at peak efficiency. The station hums with well-maintained infrastructure.

raw.story:
You dock at First Step Memorial Station. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The station is small, functional, and deliberately maintained as both an outpost and a memorial. A plaque in the docking bay lists every colonist by name. The cause of death column reads the same for all of them: 'unknown.'

The lanes around First Step Memorial Station are crowded and quick, traffic control clipped and constant. Built from salvaged colony infrastructure by Rimmers who refused to let First Step stay dead. The docking net shows a knot of three heavy ships nosed into the patched-together cargo arm, Titan Excavators trading the lanes with Observatoriums, just one Congregation warped into the memorial freight quay, a few small ships swarming in and out of the small hangar beside the plaque, Capacities and Dust Devils the most common, and well over a dozen light craft ferrying crews through the same lanes, for the most part Cobbles. The garrison here runs to several Rim Last Warnings running transponder checks on arrivals. Traffic control also tracks well over a hundred hulls of every stripe racked in deep storage across the quiet reserve berths. The Hex Quantum rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Personnel Bureau, Trauma Clinic, Marine Training Barracks, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Reactor Complex, Environmental Processor, Refueling Station, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Plasma Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Maintenance Deck, Trade Exchange, Cargo Hold, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Mission Board, Fabrication Lab, Drydock, Rim Ranger Station, Rim Ranger Cache, Steel Frame Assembly Line, Hull Assembly Line, and 26 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at Frontier Station. Home of the wanderers. Three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the docking bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble.

Frontier Station is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. Home of the wanderers: three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' The traffic-control feed lists a single Frankenhauler made fast to the mismatched cargo arms, three Concordias swarming in and out of the open hangar mouths of the Patchwork, and ten or twelve light craft flitting between the same lanes, Cobbles and Prospects the most common. The station fields a small cluster of Rim Last Warnings running transponder checks on arrivals and dozens upon dozens of Rim Bedrocks anchored off the docks in formation. Traffic control also tracks a swarm of hundreds of ships mothballed over at the cannibalized-hull yards. Among them, a score of Junk Convoys — laid up until a buyer or a war calls them back. The ORE-1d35ba5b rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Frontier Exchange, Salvage Reactor, Frontier Recycler, The Magazine Still, Patchwork Fungal Vats, Patchwork Spore Still, The Rusty Welcome, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry (x2), Crystal Refinery, Precious-Metal Refinery, Power Cell Assembler, and 43 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Huntmaster Dvorak wants proof of the thing pilots keep almost seeing in the frontier's argon clouds. Track it and deliver 1 Mirage Membrane to Frontier Station.

dialog.offer:
Every hunter back from the argon clouds tells me about stars that bend. You're watching the cloud and a star behind it slides sideways, then slides back. They call it the Mirage. Nobody's brought me anything but stories.

Here's how you track it. Watch the argon clouds for stars that bend. Then look for where the scavengers crowd. Kerf Mites and Carrion-Moths gather where something big has fed, and nothing out there feeds bigger. It eats every grazer in a system before it moves on.

This is not a solo hunt. Bring a group. I don't care whose gun kills it. Bring me one strip of its membrane and the bounty is yours.

objectives.description: Deliver 1 Mirage Membrane to the Hunters' Registry at Frontier Station

missions.title: The Lensing Sightings

missions.description: The Pathfinder Guild needs updated navigation data from every station in the Outer Rim. Fly the full circuit from Deep Range to Ramen's Rest and back.

dialog.offer: The Guild's navigation charts are only as good as the pilots who update them. I need someone to fly the full Rim circuit — Deep Range, First Step, Unknown Edge, Void Gate, Starfall, and Ramen's Rest. Every station, no shortcuts. Your ship logs the jump data, the gravitational readings, the beacon calibrations. Some of those stations are a long way from help. The Last Light system is the end of the line — past that, there's nothing. You come back with the full dataset, I pay you well. Fair warning: the Rim doesn't care about you. Fly smart.

missions.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest and Unknown Edge to locate a massive derelict drifting in deep space.

dialog.offer: A patrol ship reported a massive derelict drifting in deep space — bigger than anything we've seen in the Outer Rim. Could be pre-settlement era. Could be worth a fortune. Problem is, the patrol lost contact before transmitting full coordinates. I've got partial telemetry pointing to the systems around Last Light and Unknown Edge. Fly out there, dock at both stations, and pull whatever data the local beacons recorded. First team to piece together the full location gets salvage rights.

missions.description: Salvage Boss Dekker pays for strange salvage. Bring him 1 Mirror Facet from one of the mirror-bright machines past the rim.

dialog.offer:
Every pilot back from the rim tells me the same thing. The things take their own dead apart before the debris stops spinning. So don't let them finish.

I want a mirror facet. One plate off one of those bright hulls. Any of them will drop one when it goes down, but the rest of the group strips the wreck in about five ticks. You'll need to win the race. Bring friends. Bring a salvager. Bring something that hits hard and doesn't care about mirrors.

objectives.description: Deliver 1 Mirror Facet to Salvage Boss Dekker at Frontier Station

missions.title: Mirror Work

missions.description: Larkin tells you what she saw. Visit all seven of her systems: Whitecap, Lantern Low, Quiet Floor, Grey Hollow, Brushfield, Sallow and Narrows. Recover data at the Frame Yard and the Empty Berth, then return to the Patchwork.

dialog.offer:
Quade told you about the burns. Of course she did.

Fine. Here it is. Seven stars in a row, past the last place anyone had marked. No planets. No belts. No comets. Barely any hydrogen in the space between them. I thought it was a survey artefact until the third one. Stars that old ought to have something left around them. The stellar ages were wrong for anything natural to have taken it. Somebody had cleaned them out, and I didn't know who, and there was nobody there to ask.

My route: 226.5 from Deep Range, two thousand nine hundred and seventy-two units to the first star. That's the way I went, because it was the only way I knew.

There's a shorter way now. Sarin, 234.6, four hundred and forty-three units. I didn't know about Sarin then. Four hundred GU from a lane anyone can fly. All that time, it was that close. I'm glad I didn't know.

Go and see all seven. Then come back and tell me they're still empty.

Recover data at the Frame Yard in Quiet Floor

missions.title: Larkin's Seven

missions.description: Copy the old expedition record from the Pathfinder Guild survey hut at Last Fuel and bring it to Navigator Tull.

dialog.offer:
Everybody on the Rim knows we used to send expeditions past the lanes, and everybody knows we stopped. Ask why and you get a shrug. The Guild never wrote it down. Or it did, and the paper never came home.

There's a Guild survey hut at Last Fuel, the end of the line in the storm country. It was the last camp on the last expedition. If the reason is written anywhere, it's in that hut's log. Bring me a copy.

missions.description: A survey tender's mayday buoy at Still Calling is eleven months old, with three crew aboard and a few months of charge left. Bring life support, copy the buoy's data to take the crew aboard, and carry them home to Frontier Station.

dialog.offer:
There's a mayday on the old emergency band from an isolated red dwarf called Still Calling. It's one of ours, a Guild survey tender, three aboard. They came through a wormhole and it shut behind them. The beacon's timestamp says eleven months. The beacon also says it has a few months of charge left, and so, I'd guess, do they.

Every other distress call I know of out there is too late. This one isn't. Bring them life support, take them aboard, and bring them home. You'll need three free berths. Plan your ship for it.

missions.description:
The braising pots at The Rusty Welcome turn gloomcap mash and driftkale into a deep, meatless stew with a spoon of whale oil. The oil jar is dry. Hunt pilot-whales where the argon hangs in the gas clouds.

Dropped by: Pilot-Whale.

The station's Spore Ragout Galley uses it.

dialog.offer: The best argument the frontier has that meat is optional. Bring 1 Whale Oil and the pots go back on.

objectives.description: Deliver 1 Whale Oil to Frontier Station

missions.title: Station Need: Whale Oil

missions.description:
There's a crate waiting at Frontier Station: 3 units of iridescent void dust, no manifest, no questions. It's bound for Ironhearth Station — a dealer's clients pay anything to drift through open space without leaving their chair. You'll be threading the Rampart. Crimson customs don't bluff — if they scan you, the cargo's gone and there's a fine to match. Don't get caught.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.
