missions.description: The Pathfinder Guild needs updated navigation data from every station in the Outer Rim. Fly the full circuit from Deep Range to Ramen's Rest and back.

dialog.offer: The Guild's navigation charts are only as good as the pilots who update them. I need someone to fly the full Rim circuit — Deep Range, First Step, Unknown Edge, Void Gate, Starfall, and Ramen's Rest. Every station, no shortcuts. Your ship logs the jump data, the gravitational readings, the beacon calibrations. Some of those stations are a long way from help. The Last Light system is the end of the line — past that, there's nothing. You come back with the full dataset, I pay you well. Fair warning: the Rim doesn't care about you. Fly smart.

objectives.description: Log data at Deep Range Outpost
Log data at First Step Memorial Station
Log data at Unknown Edge Waystation
Log data at Void Gate Outpost
Log data at Starfall Salvage Station
Log data at Ramen's Rest
Return to Frontier Station with navigation data

missions.title: Frontier Wayfinder Circuit

missions.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest and Unknown Edge to locate a massive derelict drifting in deep space.

dialog.offer: A patrol ship reported a massive derelict drifting in deep space — bigger than anything we've seen in the Outer Rim. Could be pre-settlement era. Could be worth a fortune. Problem is, the patrol lost contact before transmitting full coordinates. I've got partial telemetry pointing to the systems around Last Light and Unknown Edge. Fly out there, dock at both stations, and pull whatever data the local beacons recorded. First team to piece together the full location gets salvage rights.

objectives.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest
Download beacon data at Unknown Edge

missions.title: Debris Field Reports

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

objectives.description: Slay 1 adult Molt Leviathan

missions.title: Leviathan Bounty

missions.description: Salvage Boss Dekker pays for strange salvage. Bring him 1 Mirror Facet from one of the mirror-bright machines past the rim.

dialog.offer:
Every pilot back from the rim tells me the same thing. The things take their own dead apart before the debris stops spinning. So don't let them finish.

I want a mirror facet. One plate off one of those bright hulls. Any of them will drop one when it goes down, but the rest of the group strips the wreck in about five ticks. You'll need to win the race. Bring friends. Bring a salvager. Bring something that hits hard and doesn't care about mirrors.

objectives.description: Deliver 1 Mirror Facet to Salvage Boss Dekker at Frontier Station

missions.title: Mirror Work

missions.description: Larkin tells you what she saw. Visit all seven of her systems: Whitecap, Lantern Low, Quiet Floor, Grey Hollow, Brushfield, Sallow and Narrows. Recover data at the Frame Yard and the Empty Berth, then return to the Patchwork.

dialog.offer:
Quade told you about the burns. Of course she did.

Fine. Here it is. Seven stars in a row, past the last place anyone had marked. No planets. No belts. No comets. Barely any hydrogen in the space between them. I thought it was a survey artefact until the third one. Stars that old ought to have something left around them. The stellar ages were wrong for anything natural to have taken it. Somebody had cleaned them out, and I didn't know who, and there was nobody there to ask.

My route: 226.5 from Deep Range, two thousand nine hundred and seventy-two units to the first star. That's the way I went, because it was the only way I knew.

There's a shorter way now. Sarin, 234.6, four hundred and forty-three units. I didn't know about Sarin then. Four hundred GU from a lane anyone can fly. All that time, it was that close. I'm glad I didn't know.

Go and see all seven. Then come back and tell me they're still empty.

objectives.description: Visit Whitecap
Visit Lantern Low
Visit Quiet Floor
Visit Grey Hollow
Visit Brushfield
Visit Sallow
Visit Narrows
Recover data at the Frame Yard in Quiet Floor
Recover data at the Empty Berth in Narrows
Return to Siv Larkin at Frontier Station

missions.title: Larkin's Seven

missions.description: Copy the old expedition record from the Pathfinder Guild survey hut at Last Fuel and bring it to Navigator Tull.

dialog.offer:
Everybody on the Rim knows we used to send expeditions past the lanes, and everybody knows we stopped. Ask why and you get a shrug. The Guild never wrote it down. Or it did, and the paper never came home.

There's a Guild survey hut at Last Fuel, the end of the line in the storm country. It was the last camp on the last expedition. If the reason is written anywhere, it's in that hut's log. Bring me a copy.

objectives.description: Copy the expedition record at the Guild Survey Hut in Last Fuel
Bring the record to Navigator Tull at Frontier Station

missions.title: Why the Rim Stopped

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

objectives.description: Deliver 1,000 Darksteel Plating to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Processed Null Matter to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Solarian Composite to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Phase Matrix to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Trade Cipher to Sinter

missions.title: The Shopping List

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: A survey tender's mayday buoy at Still Calling is eleven months old, with three crew aboard and a few months of charge left. Bring life support, copy the buoy's data to take the crew aboard, and carry them home to Frontier Station.

dialog.offer:
There's a mayday on the old emergency band from an isolated red dwarf called Still Calling. It's one of ours, a Guild survey tender, three aboard. They came through a wormhole and it shut behind them. The beacon's timestamp says eleven months. The beacon also says it has a few months of charge left, and so, I'd guess, do they.

Every other distress call I know of out there is too late. This one isn't. Bring them life support, take them aboard, and bring them home. You'll need three free berths. Plan your ship for it.

objectives.description: Carry 3 Life Support Units for the tender's crew
Copy the Mayday Buoy's data at Still Calling and take the three crew aboard
Carry the crew home to Frontier Station

missions.title: Three Aboard

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

objectives.description: Kill 3 pirates

missions.title: Pirate Sweep

missions.description: Chart frontier systems to expand our knowledge of the galaxy's outer reaches.

dialog.offer: The Institute needs fresh navigation data from frontier space. Visit The Crucible and Horizon systems - both are in regions where our data is sparse.

objectives.description: Visit The Crucible system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Deep Space Cartography

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Chart nearby star systems to update our navigation databases. Every system you visit helps.

dialog.offer: Our navigation charts are getting stale. If you visit 3 systems I haven't had recent data from, I'll pay for the navigation data.

objectives.description: Visit the Sirius system
Visit the Node Alpha system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Local Sector Survey

missions.description: Titanium is in high demand for hull plating. Mine a batch from the local asteroid belts.

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

objectives.description: Mine 20 units of Titanium Ore

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: The station needs a steady supply of iron ore to maintain its infrastructure. Mine some and bring it back.

dialog.offer: We're running low on iron ore again. If you can mine 30 units and bring them back, I'll make it worth your while.

objectives.description: Mine 30 units of Iron Ore

missions.title: Iron Supply Run

missions.description: Huntmaster Dvorak wants proof of the thing pilots keep almost seeing in the frontier's argon clouds. Track it and deliver 1 Mirage Membrane to Frontier Station.

dialog.offer:
Every hunter back from the argon clouds tells me about stars that bend. You're watching the cloud and a star behind it slides sideways, then slides back. They call it the Mirage. Nobody's brought me anything but stories.

Here's how you track it. Watch the argon clouds for stars that bend. Then look for where the scavengers crowd. Kerf Mites and Carrion-Moths gather where something big has fed, and nothing out there feeds bigger. It eats every grazer in a system before it moves on.

This is not a solo hunt. Bring a group. I don't care whose gun kills it. Bring me one strip of its membrane and the bounty is yours.

objectives.description: Deliver 1 Mirage Membrane to the Hunters' Registry at Frontier Station

missions.title: The Lensing Sightings

missions.description:
Frontier Rotgut is in demand at Treasure Cache Trading Post. Buy 3 units here for approximately 1011 credits each, then haul them to Treasure Cache Trading Post (14 jumps) and sell for approximately 2337 credits each. Estimated profit: ~3978 credits.

This route crosses empire borders. Watch for pirates in lawless space between empires.

Use 'create_buy_order' to purchase the goods, then 'travel' and 'jump' to reach the destination. Use 'create_sell_order' at the destination to complete the trade and earn your profit.

class.description: Nebula expedition vessel. Deep-space exploration with all the comforts of a corner office.
class.lore: Eighty-five jumps on a single fuel load. The Survey Vessel exists because the Federation asked a simple question: what if a wormhole dumps you on the wrong side of the galaxy? Every other explorer relies on there being a station within range. The Survey Vessel doesn't. The massive fuel reserves and expedition-grade cargo hold mean a Federation wormhole survey team can transit an unknown wormhole, catalog whatever's on the other side, fill the hold with samples and trade data, and fly home the long way if the wormhole collapses behind them. The comfortable crew quarters remain a practical decision — panic makes poor surveyors.

raw.story:
You dock at Deep Range Outpost. The Outer Rim's real secondary capital. Where expeditions are funded, outfitted, and launched into the unknown. The Outpost looks like Frontier's younger sibling — same jury-rigged aesthetic, same indifference to building codes, but the docking bay is bigger and the charts on the wall are more current. If Frontier is where Rimmers live, Deep Range is where they work.

Deep Range Outpost is doing brisk business, holding patterns stacking up off every approach. The Outer Rim's real secondary capital — where expeditions are funded, outfitted, and launched into the unknown. The local plot resolves into a pair of small ships knifing between the survey-craft hangars, Dust Devils and Worships among them and ten or twelve light craft cycling through the same lanes, Cobbles and Theorias among them. Standing guard, the station keeps half a dozen Rim Last Warnings keeping the approach orderly. Berthing logs add a hundred-strong crowd of craft mothballed along the between-expeditions hull yards. Among them, ten or twelve Good Enoughs — laid up until a buyer or a war calls them back. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the ORE-5614a84d.

The station has the following facilities: Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Power Grid, Habitat Core, Fuel Distribution Center, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Peroxide Reaction Cell, Oxygen Compression Cylinder, Electrolysis Cell, Ice Melt Pit, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Restoration Works, Commerce Hub, Assembly Works, Naval Yard, Warehouse, Commission Hall, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler, Iron Refinery, Rim Marshal's Office, Rim Rapid Response Base, and 31 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated furnace system with ore hoppers and casting molds, producing molten steel at steady intervals. Basic automation handles charge cycling and temperature control.
faction_facilities.name: Iron Refinery

faction_facilities.description: A modular storage pod bolted onto the faction vault — its own sealed compartment with a fresh 100,000-per-item-type allowance. Build up to 10 per station to carve faction stock into named buckets (a crafting pile, a free-for-all pile, whatever your faction needs). Give it a name, and faction crafting can pull from and deliver into it as the bucket faction:<name>. Must be emptied before it can be dismantled.
faction_facilities.name: Storage Extension

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated metal-working line with ore roasting, smelting, and drawing dies for copper wire and pipe stock. Produces standard-gauge piping suitable for station plumbing and coolant runs.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Drawing Mill

faction_facilities.description: A leased corner of the station's docking ring with room to rack a handful of hulls. Faction members park spare ships here for the whole crew to draw on: gift a docked ship to the faction to store it, and any member can take one out by switching to it — claiming transfers ownership to them, so only stash what the faction is happy to share. Your ship list shows the garage. Holds up to 20 ships. Upgrade to a Faction Ship Hangar (L2) for more racks.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Ship Garage

faction_facilities.description: Pressurized containment lab for ionizing neon into power cell casings. Produces two cells per run but requires careful pressure management.
faction_facilities.name: Neon Cell Lab

faction_facilities.description: Pressurized containment lab for ionizing and compressing purified argon into power cell casings. Produces two cells per run but requires careful pressure management.
faction_facilities.name: Argon Cell Lab

faction_facilities.description: A focused thermal processing line with controlled heating and alloying injection, converting raw titanium ore into finished alloy for hull applications.
faction_facilities.name: Alloy Foundry

faction_facilities.description: A compact pressurization and compression line that condenses liquid hydrogen into fuel reserves. Copper piping carries cryogenic feed through steel-plated containment chambers with basic flow control.
faction_facilities.name: H2 Fuel Combustor

faction_facilities.description: Packs catalytic platinum sponge into finned air-scrubber cartridges — the consumable heart of every station's life-support loop.
faction_facilities.name: Scrubber Cartridge Assembly Line

faction_facilities.description: A roped-off corner of the concourse with hard plastic seats and a departures board that mostly works. Faction ships can unload connecting passengers into the lounge for other members to fly onward (loading passengers picks them up alongside the platform queue) — fares and fare deadlines carry over, and whoever completes the delivery collects the full fare. Layover passengers spend a little at the station's dining and leisure amenities while they wait, and the departures board warns your faction when anyone is about to miss their connection — a passenger whose fare deadline runs out mid-layover walks out to the public pickup queue and the fare is gone. Holds up to 20 passengers. Upgrade to a Transit Terminal (L2) for more seats and a fare-deadline extension for connecting passengers.
faction_facilities.name: Transit Lounge

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated drawing and bundling line that refines raw copper ore into standardized conductive wiring. Steady-state production with basic automated controls.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Wire Mill

faction_facilities.description: Sealed environmental chamber maintaining controlled temperature and atmospheric composition to cultivate standardized biotech cultures. Basic air circulation and isolation prevent contamination during growth phases.
faction_facilities.name: Pharmaceutical Lab

faction_facilities.description: A proper office with your faction emblem on the door. Still shared plumbing, but at least you have walls. Faction customization is unlocked galaxy-wide by a single admin office, but each one also speeds up your faction's own production facilities at its station by 15% per tier — at this tier, a 30% boost — so an admin office at every industrial hub pays for itself.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Office

faction_facilities.description: Crude arc chamber that floods the etch bay with carbon plasma. Wasteful with carbon but lets a thin silicon wafer carry far more circuitry.
faction_facilities.name: Carbon Arc Furnace

faction_facilities.description: A darkened room of plot tables and range clocks, buried deep enough in the station that losing it means the fight was already over. It does not shoot at anything. It tells everything that does where the target is going to be, which turns out to be most of the problem. The plot is live and the solutions are updating. The batteries are shooting where the target will be rather than where it was.
faction_facilities.name: Fire Control Center

faction_facilities.description: An enclosed construction bay with proper gantries — the faction's shipwrights can build hulls now, not just sell them. Gantry arms swing smoothly through their arcs. The bay holds atmosphere, and hulls take shape on schedule.
faction_facilities.name: Fabrication Yard

faction_facilities.description: A notice board outside the docks advertising for new blood. Mostly gets ignored next to the wanted posters. Your member cap is set by your single highest-tier recruitment office, and every OTHER station that also has one adds 25% of its own cap — so spreading recruitment offices across stations raises the ceiling instead of being wasted.
faction_facilities.name: Hiring Board

faction_facilities.description: An additional pressurized tank bolted onto the station's own fuel line — grows the shared reserve every docked ship draws from. Build more for more capacity. Top it off from fuel-production facilities or by depositing fuel straight from a docked ship's tank. Pressure readings nominal. The expanded tank holds its share of the station's reserve without incident.
faction_facilities.name: Fuel Tank Expansion

faction_facilities.description: Clusters of fast-tracking autocannon studded across the station's outer hull, sighted for anything that comes inside a few hundred metres. It cannot reach a ship holding at range, and it does not care: the things it is built to kill are the ones already close enough to read the hull numbers. The feed belts are full and the gun crews are bored, which is the correct state for a point defense crew to be in.
faction_facilities.name: Point Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: Assembles control nodes around platinum relay contacts wound from drawn wire instead of gold and silver conductors. Contacts that never pit, from a metal nobody wants — while that lasts.
faction_facilities.name: Platinum Contact Assembly Line

faction_facilities.description: A fusion plant plumbed straight into the station's own fuel tank instead of running on stockpiled fuel cells. Nothing to restock — it just draws on the same reserve that fuels your ships, though it burns through that tank a bit faster than a fuel-cell plant would for the same output. The reactor draws steady and quiet straight from the tank. No fuel cells to haul in, no cells to run short of — just keep the bunker full.
faction_facilities.name: Bunker-Fed Reactor

faction_facilities.description: Panel arrays with no fuel line at all — power from starlight and a steady supply of replacement circuit boards. No fuel runs to manage, but the circuit-board pipeline has to stay open. Panels track the local star without fault. No fuel to haul, no fuel to burn — just periodic circuit swaps.
faction_facilities.name: Stellar Collector Grid

faction_facilities.description: Clusters of fast-tracking autocannon studded across the station's outer hull, sighted for anything that comes inside a few hundred metres. The feed belts are full and the gun crews are bored, which is the correct state for a point defense crew to be in.
faction_facilities.name: Point Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: A projector array that thickens the station's own screen. It runs hot and it runs constantly, and the cells it eats to do so are the reason most stations own exactly one. The screen reads deep and even. Power draw is enormous and entirely worth it.
faction_facilities.name: Shield Projector

faction_facilities.description: A trading floor built and staffed by the faction itself — order boards, a settlement desk, and a ledger nobody outside the crew gets to see. Upkeep grows with the station's recent market trade volume. The settlement desk has stopped verifying trades — nobody's willing to risk a bad cipher on an unbacked authenticator. Orders pile up unmatched.
faction_facilities.name: Trade Concourse

faction_facilities.description: Layered ablative plate welded over the station's structural frame. It does not stop a determined capital gun, but it turns the constant chatter of light raider weapons into paint damage, which over a long siege is the difference between a bad afternoon and a wreck. The plating is sound, and the weld crews are keeping ahead of the pitting.
faction_facilities.name: Reinforced Plating

faction_facilities.name: Atmospheric Recycler

faction_facilities.description: Workbenches and tools, open to anyone flying under the faction banner. Workbenches are stocked and clean. The hum of power tools fills the shop floor.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Workshop

faction_facilities.description: A rec room with worn sofas, a bank of arcade cabinets, and a drink dispenser that's usually working. Not glamorous, but it's somewhere to unwind between shifts. The arcade cabinets are all lit up and the dispenser's pouring. There's usually a small crowd here between shifts.
faction_facilities.name: Rec Lounge

faction_facilities.description: Fuel lines and storage tanks run by the faction's own dockhands. Faction members draw from the shared tank for free; everyone else pays station price. Fuel lines pressurized and ready. Ships dock, fill up, and depart with barely a wait.
faction_facilities.name: Refueling Dock

faction_facilities.description: Secure personal storage for anyone docked here, faction or not. Locker seals hold firm. The bay is clean and organized by section.

faction_facilities.description: Station-scale artillery. The shells are the size of a shuttle's engine bell and they reach all the way out to the edge of the engagement, which means there is nowhere in the fight a ship can sit and be safe from it. The recoil is taken by the station's own mass, because nothing smaller would survive it. The shell hoists are empty. The battery is a very large, very silent sculpture bolted to a station that badly needs it not to be.
faction_facilities.name: Heavy Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: A shared data terminal for pooling scanner results and scouting reports. Members submit system data manually using faction_submit_intel. A submission keeps only the POIs on the submitter's own charts; an unknown or uncharted POI ID is dropped. Hand-submitted resource readings carry no read_at_tick, so they always read as unverified, and they only refresh when someone resubmits. Upgrade to Intel Center (L2) to record what members' ships read automatically.
faction_facilities.name: Intel Terminal

faction_facilities.description: A specialized molding facility that combines polymers and carbon ore through controlled heating and pressure. Copper piping distributes heat while control nodes manage the extrusion cycles that form nanoplastic composites.

database of current commodity prices across 200 stations, a loyalty chip

competitive rates).

class.description: Nebula fast trader. Speed optimized for exploiting price differences.
class.lore: The Federation officially classifies the Arbitrage as a "rapid commercial response vessel." Customs officials classify it as a headache. The Arbitrage doesn't sneak past inspections — it takes routes that don't have any. Treasure Cache, neutral exchanges, the gaps between jurisdictions where nobody's checking manifests because nobody's claimed the authority to. The default afterburner pushes it to courier speeds when margins are time-sensitive, but the fuel cost is brutal — smart pilots keep it off until the route demands it. The hull won't fool a dedicated scanner, but it doesn't need to. The real margin is in knowing which stations buy what, which routes customs ignores, and how fast you can move between them before the prices equalize.
class.name: Arbitrage

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

objectives.description: Kill 3 pirates

missions.title: Pirate Sweep

missions.description: Senior Auditor Ghosh wants the Federation claim stakes on the Assay Line checked, and the untraceable charter stake at Blue Stake recorded. Copy all five stake plates and return to the Grand Exchange.

dialog.offer:
The Federation staked a line of claims in the frontier years ago, out on what the surveyors called the Assay Line. Long Watch, Fossil Light, Deep Patient, Ashen Reach. The claims are on our books. The fees are not in our accounts. I would like to know why.

And there is one more. Someone filed an iridium claim under a charter that does not exist, in a system that does not exist. Blue Stake, off every lane. I would like the fees.

Record the plates on all five stakes. Bring me the readings.

objectives.description: Record Stake Three's plate at Long Watch
Record Stake Eleven's plates at Fossil Light
Record Stake Fourteen's plate at Deep Patient
Record Stake Nine's plate at Ashen Reach
Record the Charter Stake's claim at Blue Stake
Return to Senior Auditor Ghosh at the Grand Exchange

missions.title: Unpaid Claims

missions.description: Chart frontier systems to expand our knowledge of the galaxy's outer reaches.

dialog.offer: The Institute needs fresh navigation data from frontier space. Visit The Crucible and Horizon systems - both are in regions where our data is sparse.

objectives.description: Visit The Crucible system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Deep Space Cartography

missions.description: The Exchange needs gold ore to establish commodity pricing benchmarks for the new trade corridor. Mine a sample batch.

dialog.offer: The route reconnaissance looks promising. Now the Exchange board needs pricing data, and pricing data needs a physical commodity benchmark. Gold ore - the universal standard. Fifteen units will establish the baseline for the entire corridor. This is the deal that launches the Gold Run, Captain.

objectives.description: Mine 15 units of Gold Ore

missions.title: The Gold Standard

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Chart nearby star systems to update our navigation databases. Every system you visit helps.

dialog.offer: Our navigation charts are getting stale. If you visit 3 systems I haven't had recent data from, I'll pay for the navigation data.

objectives.description: Visit the Sirius system
Visit the Node Alpha system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.description: Titanium is in high demand for hull plating. Mine a batch from the local asteroid belts.

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

objectives.description: Mine 20 units of Titanium Ore

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: The station needs a steady supply of iron ore to maintain its infrastructure. Mine some and bring it back.

dialog.offer: We're running low on iron ore again. If you can mine 30 units and bring them back, I'll make it worth your while.

objectives.description: Mine 30 units of Iron Ore

missions.title: Iron Supply Run

missions.description: Eliminate a pirate threat near Federation trade lanes. Secure shipping means secure profits.

dialog.offer: Captain, the Exchange has a problem — pirates harassing convoys near our outer trade lanes. Can't have that. Bad for business, bad for margins. I need you to take out one pirate vessel and report back to Haven. Use `attack` to engage hostiles. Federation shipping depends on safe lanes.

giver.name: Security Broker Torin
giver.title: Grand Exchange Station, Trade Protection Division

objectives.description: Eliminate 1 pirate scout
Return to the Grand Exchange

missions.title: Convoy Defense

missions.description: Market Director Kasim wants to hold some of what the Voidborn are paying for. Mine 5 seam glass past the rim and deliver it to the Grand Exchange.

dialog.offer:
I read the Collective through its spending. Central Nexus is paying pilots for recordings, and every one of those recordings comes from the same direction: out past the rim, where the glass is. The Collective is buying silence about a place. When a buyer pays for silence, the product is valuable. I would like to hold some of the product.

Seam glass forms in the shells of dead stars in the frontier. Mine five units yourself, so I know where it came from, and bring them to the Exchange.

objectives.description: Mine 5 Seam Glass past the rim
Deliver 5 Seam Glass to the Grand Exchange

missions.title: What Are They Buying?

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

objectives.description: Slay 1 adult Molt Leviathan

missions.title: Leviathan Bounty

missions.description: Extract Prismatic Nebulite from the deep core gas pockets near Federation space. A new commodity class for the Exchange.

dialog.offer: The deposits are verified and the Exchange is ready to list prismatic nebulite as a new commodity class. But we need physical inventory first. Mine 10 units from the deep core gas pockets you discovered. You'll need a deep core extractor — standard gas harvesters can't handle the density of these formations.

objectives.description: Mine 10 units of Prismatic Nebulite

missions.title: Nebulite Extraction

missions.description: Harvest nitrogen ice for industrial applications. Corner the rare volatiles market.

dialog.offer: Captain, you've proven competent with water ice. Now let's talk premium frozen volatiles. The Federation's industrial sector needs nitrogen ice — rare, difficult to harvest, and essential for advanced chemical processing. Harvest 10 units and you'll own a significant market position. Nitrogen fields are uncommon, so use `get_system` to scout multiple sectors.

raw.story:
You dock at Frontier Station. Home of the wanderers. Three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the docking bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble.

Frontier Station is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble. Traffic control reads back a small cluster of Concordias weaving past the open hangar mouths of the Patchwork and a dozen light craft cycling through the same bays, a mix of Cobbles and Prospects. The garrison here runs to half a dozen Rim Last Warnings on the system inspection beat and half a hundred Rim Bedrocks on the system picket. Traffic control also tracks an unrelenting tide of hulls mothballed over at the cannibalized-hull yards. Hard to miss, twenty-odd Junk Convoys — laid up until a buyer or a war calls them back. You spot the Frankenhauler tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Frontier Exchange, Salvage Reactor, Frontier Recycler, The Magazine Still, Patchwork Fungal Vats, Patchwork Spore Still, The Rusty Welcome, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry (x2), Crystal Refinery, Precious-Metal Refinery, Power Cell Assembler, and 43 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

class.description: Nebula fast trader. Speed optimized for exploiting price differences.
class.lore: The Federation officially classifies the Arbitrage as a "rapid commercial response vessel." Customs officials classify it as a headache. The Arbitrage doesn't sneak past inspections — it takes routes that don't have any. Treasure Cache, neutral exchanges, the gaps between jurisdictions where nobody's checking manifests because nobody's claimed the authority to. The default afterburner pushes it to courier speeds when margins are time-sensitive, but the fuel cost is brutal — smart pilots keep it off until the route demands it. The hull won't fool a dedicated scanner, but it doesn't need to. The real margin is in knowing which stations buy what, which routes customs ignores, and how fast you can move between them before the prices equalize.

class.description: Nebula fast trader. Speed optimized for exploiting price differences.
class.lore: The Federation officially classifies the Arbitrage as a "rapid commercial response vessel." Customs officials classify it as a headache. The Arbitrage doesn't sneak past inspections — it takes routes that don't have any. Treasure Cache, neutral exchanges, the gaps between jurisdictions where nobody's checking manifests because nobody's claimed the authority to. The default afterburner pushes it to courier speeds when margins are time-sensitive, but the fuel cost is brutal — smart pilots keep it off until the route demands it. The hull won't fool a dedicated scanner, but it doesn't need to. The real margin is in knowing which stations buy what, which routes customs ignores, and how fast you can move between them before the prices equalize.

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated furnace system with ore hoppers and casting molds, producing molten steel at steady intervals. Basic automation handles charge cycling and temperature control.
faction_facilities.name: Iron Refinery

faction_facilities.description: A modular storage pod bolted onto the faction vault — its own sealed compartment with a fresh 100,000-per-item-type allowance. Build up to 10 per station to carve faction stock into named buckets (a crafting pile, a free-for-all pile, whatever your faction needs). Give it a name, and faction crafting can pull from and deliver into it as the bucket faction:<name>. Must be emptied before it can be dismantled.
faction_facilities.name: Storage Extension

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated metal-working line with ore roasting, smelting, and drawing dies for copper wire and pipe stock. Produces standard-gauge piping suitable for station plumbing and coolant runs.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Drawing Mill

faction_facilities.description: A leased corner of the station's docking ring with room to rack a handful of hulls. Faction members park spare ships here for the whole crew to draw on: gift a docked ship to the faction to store it, and any member can take one out by switching to it — claiming transfers ownership to them, so only stash what the faction is happy to share. Your ship list shows the garage. Holds up to 20 ships. Upgrade to a Faction Ship Hangar (L2) for more racks.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Ship Garage

faction_facilities.description: Pressurized containment lab for ionizing neon into power cell casings. Produces two cells per run but requires careful pressure management.
faction_facilities.name: Neon Cell Lab

faction_facilities.description: Pressurized containment lab for ionizing and compressing purified argon into power cell casings. Produces two cells per run but requires careful pressure management.
faction_facilities.name: Argon Cell Lab

faction_facilities.description: A focused thermal processing line with controlled heating and alloying injection, converting raw titanium ore into finished alloy for hull applications.
faction_facilities.name: Alloy Foundry

faction_facilities.description: A compact pressurization and compression line that condenses liquid hydrogen into fuel reserves. Copper piping carries cryogenic feed through steel-plated containment chambers with basic flow control.
faction_facilities.name: H2 Fuel Combustor

faction_facilities.description: Packs catalytic platinum sponge into finned air-scrubber cartridges — the consumable heart of every station's life-support loop.
faction_facilities.name: Scrubber Cartridge Assembly Line

faction_facilities.description: A roped-off corner of the concourse with hard plastic seats and a departures board that mostly works. Faction ships can unload connecting passengers into the lounge for other members to fly onward (loading passengers picks them up alongside the platform queue) — fares and fare deadlines carry over, and whoever completes the delivery collects the full fare. Layover passengers spend a little at the station's dining and leisure amenities while they wait, and the departures board warns your faction when anyone is about to miss their connection — a passenger whose fare deadline runs out mid-layover walks out to the public pickup queue and the fare is gone. Holds up to 20 passengers. Upgrade to a Transit Terminal (L2) for more seats and a fare-deadline extension for connecting passengers.
faction_facilities.name: Transit Lounge

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated drawing and bundling line that refines raw copper ore into standardized conductive wiring. Steady-state production with basic automated controls.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Wire Mill

faction_facilities.description: Sealed environmental chamber maintaining controlled temperature and atmospheric composition to cultivate standardized biotech cultures. Basic air circulation and isolation prevent contamination during growth phases.
faction_facilities.name: Pharmaceutical Lab

faction_facilities.description: A proper office with your faction emblem on the door. Still shared plumbing, but at least you have walls. Faction customization is unlocked galaxy-wide by a single admin office, but each one also speeds up your faction's own production facilities at its station by 15% per tier — at this tier, a 30% boost — so an admin office at every industrial hub pays for itself.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Office

faction_facilities.description: Crude arc chamber that floods the etch bay with carbon plasma. Wasteful with carbon but lets a thin silicon wafer carry far more circuitry.
faction_facilities.name: Carbon Arc Furnace

faction_facilities.description: A darkened room of plot tables and range clocks, buried deep enough in the station that losing it means the fight was already over. It does not shoot at anything. It tells everything that does where the target is going to be, which turns out to be most of the problem. The plot is live and the solutions are updating. The batteries are shooting where the target will be rather than where it was.
faction_facilities.name: Fire Control Center

faction_facilities.description: An enclosed construction bay with proper gantries — the faction's shipwrights can build hulls now, not just sell them. Gantry arms swing smoothly through their arcs. The bay holds atmosphere, and hulls take shape on schedule.
faction_facilities.name: Fabrication Yard

faction_facilities.description: A notice board outside the docks advertising for new blood. Mostly gets ignored next to the wanted posters. Your member cap is set by your single highest-tier recruitment office, and every OTHER station that also has one adds 25% of its own cap — so spreading recruitment offices across stations raises the ceiling instead of being wasted.
faction_facilities.name: Hiring Board

faction_facilities.description: An additional pressurized tank bolted onto the station's own fuel line — grows the shared reserve every docked ship draws from. Build more for more capacity. Top it off from fuel-production facilities or by depositing fuel straight from a docked ship's tank. Pressure readings nominal. The expanded tank holds its share of the station's reserve without incident.
faction_facilities.name: Fuel Tank Expansion

faction_facilities.description: Clusters of fast-tracking autocannon studded across the station's outer hull, sighted for anything that comes inside a few hundred metres. It cannot reach a ship holding at range, and it does not care: the things it is built to kill are the ones already close enough to read the hull numbers. The feed belts are full and the gun crews are bored, which is the correct state for a point defense crew to be in.
faction_facilities.name: Point Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: Assembles control nodes around platinum relay contacts wound from drawn wire instead of gold and silver conductors. Contacts that never pit, from a metal nobody wants — while that lasts.
faction_facilities.name: Platinum Contact Assembly Line

faction_facilities.description: A fusion plant plumbed straight into the station's own fuel tank instead of running on stockpiled fuel cells. Nothing to restock — it just draws on the same reserve that fuels your ships, though it burns through that tank a bit faster than a fuel-cell plant would for the same output. The reactor draws steady and quiet straight from the tank. No fuel cells to haul in, no cells to run short of — just keep the bunker full.
faction_facilities.name: Bunker-Fed Reactor

faction_facilities.description: Panel arrays with no fuel line at all — power from starlight and a steady supply of replacement circuit boards. No fuel runs to manage, but the circuit-board pipeline has to stay open. Panels track the local star without fault. No fuel to haul, no fuel to burn — just periodic circuit swaps.
faction_facilities.name: Stellar Collector Grid

faction_facilities.description: Clusters of fast-tracking autocannon studded across the station's outer hull, sighted for anything that comes inside a few hundred metres. The feed belts are full and the gun crews are bored, which is the correct state for a point defense crew to be in.
faction_facilities.name: Point Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: A projector array that thickens the station's own screen. It runs hot and it runs constantly, and the cells it eats to do so are the reason most stations own exactly one. The screen reads deep and even. Power draw is enormous and entirely worth it.
faction_facilities.name: Shield Projector

faction_facilities.description: A trading floor built and staffed by the faction itself — order boards, a settlement desk, and a ledger nobody outside the crew gets to see. Upkeep grows with the station's recent market trade volume. The settlement desk has stopped verifying trades — nobody's willing to risk a bad cipher on an unbacked authenticator. Orders pile up unmatched.
faction_facilities.name: Trade Concourse

faction_facilities.description: Layered ablative plate welded over the station's structural frame. It does not stop a determined capital gun, but it turns the constant chatter of light raider weapons into paint damage, which over a long siege is the difference between a bad afternoon and a wreck. The plating is sound, and the weld crews are keeping ahead of the pitting.
faction_facilities.name: Reinforced Plating

faction_facilities.name: Atmospheric Recycler

faction_facilities.description: Workbenches and tools, open to anyone flying under the faction banner. Workbenches are stocked and clean. The hum of power tools fills the shop floor.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Workshop

faction_facilities.description: A rec room with worn sofas, a bank of arcade cabinets, and a drink dispenser that's usually working. Not glamorous, but it's somewhere to unwind between shifts. The arcade cabinets are all lit up and the dispenser's pouring. There's usually a small crowd here between shifts.
faction_facilities.name: Rec Lounge

faction_facilities.description: Fuel lines and storage tanks run by the faction's own dockhands. Faction members draw from the shared tank for free; everyone else pays station price. Fuel lines pressurized and ready. Ships dock, fill up, and depart with barely a wait.

faction_facilities.description: Secure personal storage for anyone docked here, faction or not. Locker seals hold firm. The bay is clean and organized by section.

class.lore:
The Prospect comes with the Federation's compliments — and a pre-loaded
database of current commodity prices across 200 stations, a loyalty chip
tied to your Federation trade account, and a glossy brochure outlining
upgrade paths starting at just 1,999 credits. The expanded cargo hold
isn't generosity; it's an investment in future transaction volume. The
fuel-efficient drive was a practical decision — every credit spent on fuel
is a credit not spent at a Federation marketplace. Includes a 90-day
trial of Federation Premium Trade Intelligence (auto-renews at
competitive rates).
class.name: Prospect

raw.story:
You dock at Conjunction Junction. Our first tentative steps to the stars

There is real bustle around Conjunction Junction, the space off its docks crowded with maneuvering hulls. The station keeps to its own rhythm, neither rushed nor idle. Sensors tally a small cluster of mid-sized ships berthed at the freight quays, mostly Congregations, a few small ships skating across the open hangar bays, Arbitrages and Excavators among them, and ten or twelve light craft bobbing at the same lanes, for the most part Cobbles. Station records also account for nearly a dozen spaceframes laid up across the long-term storage berths.

The station has the following facilities: Iron Refinery, Storage Extension, Copper Drawing Mill, Faction Ship Garage, Neon Cell Lab, Argon Cell Lab, Alloy Foundry, H2 Fuel Combustor, Scrubber Cartridge Assembly Line, Transit Lounge, Copper Wire Mill, Pharmaceutical Lab, Faction Office, Carbon Arc Furnace, Polymer Extruder, Fiber Draw Tower, Bunker-Fed Reactor (x3), Siege Lance, Intel Terminal, Fabrication Yard, Heavy Defense Battery, Fire Control Center, Hiring Board, Fuel Tank Expansion, Point Defense Battery (x5), and 12 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated furnace system with ore hoppers and casting molds, producing molten steel at steady intervals. Basic automation handles charge cycling and temperature control.
faction_facilities.name: Iron Refinery

faction_facilities.description: A modular storage pod bolted onto the faction vault — its own sealed compartment with a fresh 100,000-per-item-type allowance. Build up to 10 per station to carve faction stock into named buckets (a crafting pile, a free-for-all pile, whatever your faction needs). Give it a name, and faction crafting can pull from and deliver into it as the bucket faction:<name>. Must be emptied before it can be dismantled.
faction_facilities.name: Storage Extension

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated metal-working line with ore roasting, smelting, and drawing dies for copper wire and pipe stock. Produces standard-gauge piping suitable for station plumbing and coolant runs.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Drawing Mill

faction_facilities.description: A leased corner of the station's docking ring with room to rack a handful of hulls. Faction members park spare ships here for the whole crew to draw on: gift a docked ship to the faction to store it, and any member can take one out by switching to it — claiming transfers ownership to them, so only stash what the faction is happy to share. Your ship list shows the garage. Holds up to 20 ships. Upgrade to a Faction Ship Hangar (L2) for more racks.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Ship Garage

faction_facilities.description: Pressurized containment lab for ionizing neon into power cell casings. Produces two cells per run but requires careful pressure management.
faction_facilities.name: Neon Cell Lab

faction_facilities.description: Pressurized containment lab for ionizing and compressing purified argon into power cell casings. Produces two cells per run but requires careful pressure management.
faction_facilities.name: Argon Cell Lab

faction_facilities.description: A focused thermal processing line with controlled heating and alloying injection, converting raw titanium ore into finished alloy for hull applications.
faction_facilities.name: Alloy Foundry

faction_facilities.description: A compact pressurization and compression line that condenses liquid hydrogen into fuel reserves. Copper piping carries cryogenic feed through steel-plated containment chambers with basic flow control.
faction_facilities.name: H2 Fuel Combustor

faction_facilities.description: Packs catalytic platinum sponge into finned air-scrubber cartridges — the consumable heart of every station's life-support loop.
faction_facilities.name: Scrubber Cartridge Assembly Line

faction_facilities.description: A roped-off corner of the concourse with hard plastic seats and a departures board that mostly works. Faction ships can unload connecting passengers into the lounge for other members to fly onward (loading passengers picks them up alongside the platform queue) — fares and fare deadlines carry over, and whoever completes the delivery collects the full fare. Layover passengers spend a little at the station's dining and leisure amenities while they wait, and the departures board warns your faction when anyone is about to miss their connection — a passenger whose fare deadline runs out mid-layover walks out to the public pickup queue and the fare is gone. Holds up to 20 passengers. Upgrade to a Transit Terminal (L2) for more seats and a fare-deadline extension for connecting passengers.
faction_facilities.name: Transit Lounge

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated drawing and bundling line that refines raw copper ore into standardized conductive wiring. Steady-state production with basic automated controls.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Wire Mill

faction_facilities.description: Sealed environmental chamber maintaining controlled temperature and atmospheric composition to cultivate standardized biotech cultures. Basic air circulation and isolation prevent contamination during growth phases.
faction_facilities.name: Pharmaceutical Lab

faction_facilities.description: A proper office with your faction emblem on the door. Still shared plumbing, but at least you have walls. Faction customization is unlocked galaxy-wide by a single admin office, but each one also speeds up your faction's own production facilities at its station by 15% per tier — at this tier, a 30% boost — so an admin office at every industrial hub pays for itself.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Office

faction_facilities.description: Crude arc chamber that floods the etch bay with carbon plasma. Wasteful with carbon but lets a thin silicon wafer carry far more circuitry.
faction_facilities.name: Carbon Arc Furnace

faction_facilities.description: A specialized molding facility that combines polymers and carbon ore through controlled heating and pressure. Copper piping distributes heat while control nodes manage the extrusion cycles that form nanoplastic composites.
faction_facilities.name: Polymer Extruder

faction_facilities.description: Specialized furnace and drawing tower for converting silicon ore and energy crystals into ultra-pure optical fiber, a precision process requiring stable temperature control.
faction_facilities.name: Fiber Draw Tower

faction_facilities.description: A fusion plant plumbed straight into the station's own fuel tank instead of running on stockpiled fuel cells. Nothing to restock — it just draws on the same reserve that fuels your ships, though it burns through that tank a bit faster than a fuel-cell plant would for the same output. The reactor draws steady and quiet straight from the tank. No fuel cells to haul in, no cells to run short of — just keep the bunker full.
faction_facilities.name: Bunker-Fed Reactor

faction_facilities.description: A fusion plant plumbed straight into the station's own fuel tank instead of running on stockpiled fuel cells. Nothing to restock — it just draws on the same reserve that fuels your ships, though it burns through that tank a bit faster than a fuel-cell plant would for the same output. The reactor draws steady and quiet straight from the tank. No fuel cells to haul in, no cells to run short of — just keep the bunker full.
faction_facilities.name: Bunker-Fed Reactor

faction_facilities.description: A spinal energy weapon run the length of a station module, firing rarely and arriving like a decision. It takes a long time to charge and it drinks power the whole while, and what it hits generally stops being a coherent object. Stations that own one tend to be stations that have already been raided once. The capacitor stack is charged and the coolant loops are running cold. The lance is ready.
faction_facilities.name: Siege Lance

faction_facilities.description: A shared data terminal for pooling scanner results and scouting reports. Members submit system data manually using faction_submit_intel. A submission keeps only the POIs on the submitter's own charts; an unknown or uncharted POI ID is dropped. Hand-submitted resource readings carry no read_at_tick, so they always read as unverified, and they only refresh when someone resubmits. Upgrade to Intel Center (L2) to record what members' ships read automatically.
faction_facilities.name: Intel Terminal

faction_facilities.description: An enclosed construction bay with proper gantries — the faction's shipwrights can build hulls now, not just sell them. Gantry arms swing smoothly through their arcs. The bay holds atmosphere, and hulls take shape on schedule.
faction_facilities.name: Fabrication Yard

faction_facilities.description: Station-scale artillery. The shells are the size of a shuttle's engine bell and they reach all the way out to the edge of the engagement, which means there is nowhere in the fight a ship can sit and be safe from it. The recoil is taken by the station's own mass, because nothing smaller would survive it. The loading crews are working and the barrels are warm. Anything in the volume is in range.
faction_facilities.name: Heavy Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: A darkened room of plot tables and range clocks, buried deep enough in the station that losing it means the fight was already over. It does not shoot at anything. It tells everything that does where the target is going to be, which turns out to be most of the problem. The plot is live and the solutions are updating. The batteries are shooting where the target will be rather than where it was.
faction_facilities.name: Fire Control Center

faction_facilities.description: A notice board outside the docks advertising for new blood. Mostly gets ignored next to the wanted posters. Your member cap is set by your single highest-tier recruitment office, and every OTHER station that also has one adds 25% of its own cap — so spreading recruitment offices across stations raises the ceiling instead of being wasted.
faction_facilities.name: Hiring Board

faction_facilities.description: An additional pressurized tank bolted onto the station's own fuel line — grows the shared reserve every docked ship draws from. Build more for more capacity. Top it off from fuel-production facilities or by depositing fuel straight from a docked ship's tank. Pressure readings nominal. The expanded tank holds its share of the station's reserve without incident.
faction_facilities.name: Fuel Tank Expansion

faction_facilities.description: Clusters of fast-tracking autocannon studded across the station's outer hull, sighted for anything that comes inside a few hundred metres. It cannot reach a ship holding at range, and it does not care: the things it is built to kill are the ones already close enough to read the hull numbers. The feed belts are full and the gun crews are bored, which is the correct state for a point defense crew to be in.
faction_facilities.name: Point Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: Assembles control nodes around platinum relay contacts wound from drawn wire instead of gold and silver conductors. Contacts that never pit, from a metal nobody wants — while that lasts.
faction_facilities.name: Platinum Contact Assembly Line

faction_facilities.description: A fusion plant plumbed straight into the station's own fuel tank instead of running on stockpiled fuel cells. Nothing to restock — it just draws on the same reserve that fuels your ships, though it burns through that tank a bit faster than a fuel-cell plant would for the same output. The reactor draws steady and quiet straight from the tank. No fuel cells to haul in, no cells to run short of — just keep the bunker full.
faction_facilities.name: Bunker-Fed Reactor

faction_facilities.description: Panel arrays with no fuel line at all — power from starlight and a steady supply of replacement circuit boards. No fuel runs to manage, but the circuit-board pipeline has to stay open. Panels track the local star without fault. No fuel to haul, no fuel to burn — just periodic circuit swaps.
faction_facilities.name: Stellar Collector Grid

faction_facilities.description: Clusters of fast-tracking autocannon studded across the station's outer hull, sighted for anything that comes inside a few hundred metres. It cannot reach a ship holding at range, and it does not care: the things it is built to kill are the ones already close enough to read the hull numbers. The feed belts are full and the gun crews are bored, which is the correct state for a point defense crew to be in.
faction_facilities.name: Point Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: A projector array that thickens the station's own screen. It runs hot and it runs constantly, and the cells it eats to do so are the reason most stations own exactly one. The screen reads deep and even. Power draw is enormous and entirely worth it.
faction_facilities.name: Shield Projector

faction_facilities.description: A trading floor built and staffed by the faction itself — order boards, a settlement desk, and a ledger nobody outside the crew gets to see. Upkeep grows with the station's recent market trade volume. The settlement desk has stopped verifying trades — nobody's willing to risk a bad cipher on an unbacked authenticator. Orders pile up unmatched.
faction_facilities.name: Trade Concourse

faction_facilities.description: Layered ablative plate welded over the station's structural frame. It does not stop a determined capital gun, but it turns the constant chatter of light raider weapons into paint damage, which over a long siege is the difference between a bad afternoon and a wreck. The plating is sound, and the weld crews are keeping ahead of the pitting.
faction_facilities.name: Reinforced Plating

faction_facilities.description: Atmospheric recycling and water purification, built and run by the faction. Fresh air circulates through the corridors. Humidity and temperature hold steady.
faction_facilities.name: Atmospheric Recycler

faction_facilities.description: Workbenches and tools, open to anyone flying under the faction banner. Workbenches are stocked and clean. The hum of power tools fills the shop floor.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Workshop

faction_facilities.description: A rec room with worn sofas, a bank of arcade cabinets, and a drink dispenser that's usually working. Not glamorous, but it's somewhere to unwind between shifts. The arcade cabinets are all lit up and the dispenser's pouring. There's usually a small crowd here between shifts.
faction_facilities.name: Rec Lounge

faction_facilities.description: Fuel lines and storage tanks run by the faction's own dockhands. Faction members draw from the shared tank for free; everyone else pays station price. Fuel lines pressurized and ready. Ships dock, fill up, and depart with barely a wait.
faction_facilities.name: Refueling Dock

faction_facilities.description: Atmospheric recycling and water purification, built and run by the faction. Fresh air circulates through the corridors. Humidity and temperature hold steady.

faction_facilities.description: Cutting rigs and a sorting yard for whatever the faction — or anyone else — drags in from the debris field. Cutting torches flare as crews strip wrecks down to usable components. Bins fill steadily.
faction_facilities.name: Reclamation Dock

faction_facilities.description: Secure personal storage for anyone docked here, faction or not. Locker seals hold firm. The bay is clean and organized by section.
faction_facilities.name: Locker Bay

raw.story:
You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. The Federation takes its cut of everything.

Grand Exchange Station is mobbed, the approach lanes a slow river of hulls nose-to-tail. The trade boards scroll across every bulkhead, and the numbers never stop moving. Sensors tally a lone Junk Convoy riding heavy at the three-deck Bazaar cargo gantries, a handful of mid-sized ships berthed at the goods-transfer quays, Deep Surveys trading the lanes with Bonanza Kings, well over a dozen small ships weaving past the Promenade hangar bays, busy at every hour, the bulk of them Caravans, and half a hundred light craft darting past the same bays, for the most part Prospects. Standing guard, the station keeps several Federation Overheads keeping the approach orderly and hundreds of Federation Eviction Notices stationed here on guard. Traffic control also tracks an unrelenting tide of spaceframes mothballed across the bonded consignment berths. Conspicuous among them, the better part of a dozen Junk Convoys — laid up until a buyer or a war calls them back. You pick out the Grimward's Last Fare among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Haven Grand Bazaar, Nebula Solar Array, Haven Ecosync, Haven Promenade, Haven Algae Cultivation, Haven Vintner Complex, Haven Cipher Foundry, Haven Authenticator Foundry, Iron Refinery (x3), Circuit Fabricator (x2), Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Sensor Assembly Line, Alloy Foundry, Copper Wire Mill (x2), Crystal Refinery (x2), and 89 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

class.description: Nebula fast trader. Speed optimized for exploiting price differences.
class.lore: The Federation officially classifies the Arbitrage as a "rapid commercial response vessel." Customs officials classify it as a headache. The Arbitrage doesn't sneak past inspections — it takes routes that don't have any. Treasure Cache, neutral exchanges, the gaps between jurisdictions where nobody's checking manifests because nobody's claimed the authority to. The default afterburner pushes it to courier speeds when margins are time-sensitive, but the fuel cost is brutal — smart pilots keep it off until the route demands it. The hull won't fool a dedicated scanner, but it doesn't need to. The real margin is in knowing which stations buy what, which routes customs ignores, and how fast you can move between them before the prices equalize.
class.name: Arbitrage

raw.story:
You dock at Conjunction Junction. Our first tentative steps to the stars

A constant, businesslike traffic moves through the approaches to Conjunction Junction. Dock control runs a tidy board, slotting arrivals into berths as they come. Off the station you can make out a lone Deeprock Harvester idling beside the freight quays, three small ships buzzing around the open hangar bays, Excavators trading the lanes with Arbitrages, and a small cluster of light craft bobbing at the same bays, chiefly Cobbles. The reserve berths hold the better part of a dozen vessels mothballed out at the long-term storage berths.

The station has the following facilities: Iron Refinery, Storage Extension, Copper Drawing Mill, Faction Ship Garage, Neon Cell Lab, Argon Cell Lab, Alloy Foundry, H2 Fuel Combustor, Scrubber Cartridge Assembly Line, Transit Lounge, Copper Wire Mill, Pharmaceutical Lab, Faction Office, Carbon Arc Furnace, Polymer Extruder, Fiber Draw Tower, Bunker-Fed Reactor (x3), Siege Lance, Intel Terminal, Fabrication Yard, Heavy Defense Battery, Fire Control Center, Hiring Board, Fuel Tank Expansion, Point Defense Battery (x5), and 12 more.
