faction_facilities.description: A dedicated furnace system with ore hoppers and casting molds, producing molten steel at steady intervals. Basic automation handles charge cycling and temperature control.
faction_facilities.name: Iron Refinery

faction_facilities.description: A modular storage pod bolted onto the faction vault — its own sealed compartment with a fresh 100,000-per-item-type allowance. Build up to 10 per station to carve faction stock into named buckets (a crafting pile, a free-for-all pile, whatever your faction needs). Give it a name, and faction crafting can pull from and deliver into it as the bucket faction:<name>. Must be emptied before it can be dismantled.
faction_facilities.name: Storage Extension

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated metal-working line with ore roasting, smelting, and drawing dies for copper wire and pipe stock. Produces standard-gauge piping suitable for station plumbing and coolant runs.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Drawing Mill

faction_facilities.description: A leased corner of the station's docking ring with room to rack a handful of hulls. Faction members park spare ships here for the whole crew to draw on: gift a docked ship to the faction to store it, and any member can take one out by switching to it — claiming transfers ownership to them, so only stash what the faction is happy to share. Your ship list shows the garage. Holds up to 20 ships. Upgrade to a Faction Ship Hangar (L2) for more racks.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Ship Garage

faction_facilities.description: Pressurized containment lab for ionizing neon into power cell casings. Produces two cells per run but requires careful pressure management.
faction_facilities.name: Neon Cell Lab

faction_facilities.description: Pressurized containment lab for ionizing and compressing purified argon into power cell casings. Produces two cells per run but requires careful pressure management.
faction_facilities.name: Argon Cell Lab

faction_facilities.description: A focused thermal processing line with controlled heating and alloying injection, converting raw titanium ore into finished alloy for hull applications.
faction_facilities.name: Alloy Foundry

faction_facilities.description: A compact pressurization and compression line that condenses liquid hydrogen into fuel reserves. Copper piping carries cryogenic feed through steel-plated containment chambers with basic flow control.
faction_facilities.name: H2 Fuel Combustor

faction_facilities.description: Packs catalytic platinum sponge into finned air-scrubber cartridges — the consumable heart of every station's life-support loop.
faction_facilities.name: Scrubber Cartridge Assembly Line

faction_facilities.description: A roped-off corner of the concourse with hard plastic seats and a departures board that mostly works. Faction ships can unload connecting passengers into the lounge for other members to fly onward (loading passengers picks them up alongside the platform queue) — fares and fare deadlines carry over, and whoever completes the delivery collects the full fare. Layover passengers spend a little at the station's dining and leisure amenities while they wait, and the departures board warns your faction when anyone is about to miss their connection — a passenger whose fare deadline runs out mid-layover walks out to the public pickup queue and the fare is gone. Holds up to 20 passengers. Upgrade to a Transit Terminal (L2) for more seats and a fare-deadline extension for connecting passengers.
faction_facilities.name: Transit Lounge

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated drawing and bundling line that refines raw copper ore into standardized conductive wiring. Steady-state production with basic automated controls.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Wire Mill

faction_facilities.description: Sealed environmental chamber maintaining controlled temperature and atmospheric composition to cultivate standardized biotech cultures. Basic air circulation and isolation prevent contamination during growth phases.
faction_facilities.name: Pharmaceutical Lab

faction_facilities.description: A proper office with your faction emblem on the door. Still shared plumbing, but at least you have walls. Faction customization is unlocked galaxy-wide by a single admin office, but each one also speeds up your faction's own production facilities at its station by 15% per tier — at this tier, a 30% boost — so an admin office at every industrial hub pays for itself.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Office

faction_facilities.description: Crude arc chamber that floods the etch bay with carbon plasma. Wasteful with carbon but lets a thin silicon wafer carry far more circuitry.
faction_facilities.name: Carbon Arc Furnace

faction_facilities.description: A specialized molding facility that combines polymers and carbon ore through controlled heating and pressure. Copper piping distributes heat while control nodes manage the extrusion cycles that form nanoplastic composites.
faction_facilities.name: Polymer Extruder

faction_facilities.description: Specialized furnace and drawing tower for converting silicon ore and energy crystals into ultra-pure optical fiber, a precision process requiring stable temperature control.
faction_facilities.name: Fiber Draw Tower

faction_facilities.description: A fusion plant plumbed straight into the station's own fuel tank instead of running on stockpiled fuel cells. Nothing to restock — it just draws on the same reserve that fuels your ships, though it burns through that tank a bit faster than a fuel-cell plant would for the same output. The reactor draws steady and quiet straight from the tank. No fuel cells to haul in, no cells to run short of — just keep the bunker full.
faction_facilities.name: Bunker-Fed Reactor

faction_facilities.description: A fusion plant plumbed straight into the station's own fuel tank instead of running on stockpiled fuel cells. Nothing to restock — it just draws on the same reserve that fuels your ships, though it burns through that tank a bit faster than a fuel-cell plant would for the same output. The reactor draws steady and quiet straight from the tank. No fuel cells to haul in, no cells to run short of — just keep the bunker full.
faction_facilities.name: Bunker-Fed Reactor

faction_facilities.description: A spinal energy weapon run the length of a station module, firing rarely and arriving like a decision. It takes a long time to charge and it drinks power the whole while, and what it hits generally stops being a coherent object. Stations that own one tend to be stations that have already been raided once. The capacitor stack is charged and the coolant loops are running cold. The lance is ready.
faction_facilities.name: Siege Lance

faction_facilities.description: A shared data terminal for pooling scanner results and scouting reports. Members submit system data manually using faction_submit_intel. A submission keeps only the POIs on the submitter's own charts; an unknown or uncharted POI ID is dropped. Hand-submitted resource readings carry no read_at_tick, so they always read as unverified, and they only refresh when someone resubmits. Upgrade to Intel Center (L2) to record what members' ships read automatically.
faction_facilities.name: Intel Terminal

faction_facilities.description: An enclosed construction bay with proper gantries — the faction's shipwrights can build hulls now, not just sell them. Gantry arms swing smoothly through their arcs. The bay holds atmosphere, and hulls take shape on schedule.
faction_facilities.name: Fabrication Yard

faction_facilities.description: Station-scale artillery. The shells are the size of a shuttle's engine bell and they reach all the way out to the edge of the engagement, which means there is nowhere in the fight a ship can sit and be safe from it. The recoil is taken by the station's own mass, because nothing smaller would survive it. The loading crews are working and the barrels are warm. Anything in the volume is in range.
faction_facilities.name: Heavy Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: A darkened room of plot tables and range clocks, buried deep enough in the station that losing it means the fight was already over. It does not shoot at anything. It tells everything that does where the target is going to be, which turns out to be most of the problem. The plot is live and the solutions are updating. The batteries are shooting where the target will be rather than where it was.
faction_facilities.name: Fire Control Center

faction_facilities.description: A notice board outside the docks advertising for new blood. Mostly gets ignored next to the wanted posters. Your member cap is set by your single highest-tier recruitment office, and every OTHER station that also has one adds 25% of its own cap — so spreading recruitment offices across stations raises the ceiling instead of being wasted.
faction_facilities.name: Hiring Board

faction_facilities.description: An additional pressurized tank bolted onto the station's own fuel line — grows the shared reserve every docked ship draws from. Build more for more capacity. Top it off from fuel-production facilities or by depositing fuel straight from a docked ship's tank. Pressure readings nominal. The expanded tank holds its share of the station's reserve without incident.
faction_facilities.name: Fuel Tank Expansion

faction_facilities.description: Clusters of fast-tracking autocannon studded across the station's outer hull, sighted for anything that comes inside a few hundred metres. It cannot reach a ship holding at range, and it does not care: the things it is built to kill are the ones already close enough to read the hull numbers. The feed belts are full and the gun crews are bored, which is the correct state for a point defense crew to be in.
faction_facilities.name: Point Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: Assembles control nodes around platinum relay contacts wound from drawn wire instead of gold and silver conductors. Contacts that never pit, from a metal nobody wants — while that lasts.
faction_facilities.name: Platinum Contact Assembly Line

faction_facilities.name: Bunker-Fed Reactor

faction_facilities.description: Panel arrays with no fuel line at all — power from starlight and a steady supply of replacement circuit boards. No fuel runs to manage, but the circuit-board pipeline has to stay open. Panels track the local star without fault. No fuel to haul, no fuel to burn — just periodic circuit swaps.
faction_facilities.name: Stellar Collector Grid

faction_facilities.description: Clusters of fast-tracking autocannon studded across the station's outer hull, sighted for anything that comes inside a few hundred metres. faction_facilities.description: A projector array that thickens the station's own screen. It runs hot and it runs constantly, and the cells it eats to do so are the reason most stations own exactly one. The screen reads deep and even. Power draw is enormous and entirely worth it.
faction_facilities.name: Shield Projector

faction_facilities.description: A trading floor built and staffed by the faction itself — order boards, a settlement desk, and a ledger nobody outside the crew gets to see. Upkeep grows with the station's recent market trade volume. The settlement desk has stopped verifying trades — nobody's willing to risk a bad cipher on an unbacked authenticator. Orders pile up unmatched.
faction_facilities.name: Trade Concourse

faction_facilities.description: Layered ablative plate welded over the station's structural frame. It does not stop a determined capital gun, but it turns the constant chatter of light raider weapons into paint damage, which over a long siege is the difference between a bad afternoon and a wreck. The plating is sound, and the weld crews are keeping ahead of the pitting.
faction_facilities.name: Reinforced Plating

faction_facilities.name: Atmospheric Recycler

faction_facilities.description: Workbenches and tools, open to anyone flying under the faction banner. Workbenches are stocked and clean. The hum of power tools fills the shop floor.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Workshop

faction_facilities.description: A rec room with worn sofas, a bank of arcade cabinets, and a drink dispenser that's usually working. Not glamorous, but it's somewhere to unwind between shifts. raw.story:
You dock at Confederacy Central Command. The seat of Solarian government and commerce. Everything here is certified, warrantied, and documented in triplicate — from the precision drydocks to the quantum-entangled trade exchange. A self-sustaining biosphere spans three decks, providing real air and real food, because the Confederacy believes civilization requires both.

The lanes around Confederacy Central Command are crowded and quick, traffic control clipped and constant. This is the seat of Solarian government and commerce, and it never lets you forget it. From the cockpit you count a few heavy ships moored against the documented cargo gantries, Frankenhaulers and Junk Convoys the most common, the better part of a dozen small ships flitting through the inspection-cleared hangar lanes, a mix of Syndicates and Capacities, and thirty-some light craft hopping between the same lanes, Theorias and Archimedes among them. Standing guard, the station keeps a handful of Confederacy Precepts working overwatch from these docks and the better part of a hundred Confederacy Dialectics holding station as a show of force. Station records also account for countless hulls of every stripe in cold layup along the bonded archival berths. Among them, a good many Symposiums — laid up until a buyer or a war calls them back. The Hex Quantum rides at her mooring here, easy to recognize.

Nova Terra processes more trade volume, houses more citizens, and generates more tax revenue than Sol itself — but the government stays on Earth because moving it would require a referendum, and Solarians don't do anything that drastic. Dock authority holds a hundred-strong crowd of hulls cold and dormant out at the overflow berths the station never admits it needs. class.lore: Eighty-five jumps on a single fuel load. The Survey Vessel exists because the Federation asked a simple question: what if a wormhole dumps you on the wrong side of the galaxy? raw.story:
You dock at Nova Terra Central. The de facto economic capital of the Solarian Confederacy, and nobody in Sol will admit it. Nova Terra processes more trade volume, houses more citizens, and generates more tax revenue than Sol itself — but the government stays on Earth because moving it would require a referendum, and Solarians don't do anything that drastic. Nova Terra Central is plainly busy, its approach lanes thick with crossing traffic. Confederacy traffic control is courteous, thorough, and utterly indifferent to how late you are. class.description: Nebula fast trader. Speed optimized for exploiting price differences.
class.lore: The Federation officially classifies the Arbitrage as a "rapid commercial response vessel." Customs officials classify it as a headache. The Arbitrage doesn't sneak past inspections — it takes routes that don't have any. Treasure Cache, neutral exchanges, the gaps between jurisdictions where nobody's checking manifests because nobody's claimed the authority to. The default afterburner pushes it to courier speeds when margins are time-sensitive, but the fuel cost is brutal — smart pilots keep it off until the route demands it. The hull won't fool a dedicated scanner, but it doesn't need to. The real margin is in knowing which stations buy what, which routes customs ignores, and how fast you can move between them before the prices equalize.
class.name: Arbitrage

class.description: Outer Rim starter vessel. Mismatched parts, personally tuned engine, expired warranty.
class.lore:
No two Cobbles are alike because no two Cobbles are made from the same
parts. Assembled from whatever was available — Solarian hull panels here,
Crimson thruster housing there, something Voidborn that nobody can identify
bolted to the port nacelle. The engine has been hand-tuned by whoever built
this particular Cobble, and it is improbably, irresponsibly fast. The hull
integrity is... present. The warranty expired before the ship was finished.
The paint doesn't match. The instrument panel is labeled in three different
languages. It is the most honest ship in the galaxy: exactly what it is,
nothing pretending to be more. Rim pilots love them with an affection that
baffles every other empire.
class.name: Cobble

faction_facilities.description: A roped-off corner of the concourse with hard plastic seats and a departures board that mostly works. Layover passengers spend a little at the station's dining and leisure amenities while they wait, and the departures board warns your faction when anyone is about to miss their connection — a passenger whose fare deadline runs out mid-layover walks out to the public pickup queue and the fare is gone. Holds up to 20 passengers. Upgrade to a Transit Terminal (L2) for more seats and a fare-deadline extension for connecting passengers.
faction_facilities.name: Transit Lounge

faction_facilities.description: A dedicated drawing and bundling line that refines raw copper ore into standardized conductive wiring. Steady-state production with basic automated controls.
faction_facilities.name: Copper Wire Mill

faction_facilities.description: Sealed environmental chamber maintaining controlled temperature and atmospheric composition to cultivate standardized biotech cultures. Basic air circulation and isolation prevent contamination during growth phases.
faction_facilities.name: Pharmaceutical Lab

faction_facilities.description: A proper office with your faction emblem on the door. Still shared plumbing, but at least you have walls. Faction customization is unlocked galaxy-wide by a single admin office, but each one also speeds up your faction's own production facilities at its station by 15% per tier — at this tier, a 30% boost — so an admin office at every industrial hub pays for itself.
faction_facilities.name: Faction Office

faction_facilities.description: Crude arc chamber that floods the etch bay with carbon plasma. Wasteful with carbon but lets a thin silicon wafer carry far more circuitry.
faction_facilities.name: Carbon Arc Furnace

faction_facilities.description: A specialized molding facility that combines polymers and carbon ore through controlled heating and pressure. Copper piping distributes heat while control nodes manage the extrusion cycles that form nanoplastic composites.
faction_facilities.name: Polymer Extruder

faction_facilities.description: Specialized furnace and drawing tower for converting silicon ore and energy crystals into ultra-pure optical fiber, a precision process requiring stable temperature control.
faction_facilities.name: Fiber Draw Tower

faction_facilities.description: A fusion plant plumbed straight into the station's own fuel tank instead of running on stockpiled fuel cells. Nothing to restock — it just draws on the same reserve that fuels your ships, though it burns through that tank a bit faster than a fuel-cell plant would for the same output. The reactor draws steady and quiet straight from the tank. No fuel cells to haul in, no cells to run short of — just keep the bunker full.
faction_facilities.name: Bunker-Fed Reactor

faction_facilities.description: A spinal energy weapon run the length of a station module, firing rarely and arriving like a decision. It takes a long time to charge and it drinks power the whole while, and what it hits generally stops being a coherent object. Stations that own one tend to be stations that have already been raided once. The capacitor stack is charged and the coolant loops are running cold. The lance is ready.

faction_facilities.description: A shared data terminal for pooling scanner results and scouting reports. Members submit system data manually using faction_submit_intel. faction_facilities.description: An enclosed construction bay with proper gantries — the faction's shipwrights can build hulls now, not just sell them. Gantry arms swing smoothly through their arcs. The bay holds atmosphere, and hulls take shape on schedule.
faction_facilities.name: Fabrication Yard

faction_facilities.description: Station-scale artillery. The shells are the size of a shuttle's engine bell and they reach all the way out to the edge of the engagement, which means there is nowhere in the fight a ship can sit and be safe from it. The recoil is taken by the station's own mass, because nothing smaller would survive it. The loading crews are working and the barrels are warm. Anything in the volume is in range.
faction_facilities.name: Heavy Defense Battery

faction_facilities.description: A darkened room of plot tables and range clocks, buried deep enough in the station that losing it means the fight was already over. It does not shoot at anything. The batteries are shooting where the target will be rather than where it was.
faction_facilities.name: Fire Control Center

faction_facilities.description: An additional pressurized tank bolted onto the station's own fuel line — grows the shared reserve every docked ship draws from. Build more for more capacity. The expanded tank holds its share of the station's reserve without incident.
faction_facilities.name: Fuel Tank Expansion

class.lore: The Compendium-class hauls cargo the way the Confederacy does everything: thoroughly, methodically, and with comprehensive documentation. The automated cargo management system optimizes load distribution in real time, adjusting center-of-mass calculations after every container shift. raw.story:
You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. The Federation takes its cut of everything.

You queue into Grand Exchange Station behind a wall of traffic, controllers barking over every channel. Restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and Voidborn arcades keep visitors spending long past when they meant to leave. Traffic control reads back the better part of a dozen mid-sized ships docked at the goods-transfer quays, Bonanza Kings and Deep Surveys among them, several small ships darting between the Promenade hangar bays, busy at every hour, for the most part Caravans, and dozens upon dozens of light craft trickling through the same berths, mostly Prospects. The garrison here runs to a small cluster of Federation Overheads on the system inspection beat and a hundred and more Federation Eviction Notices anchored off the docks in formation. Berthing logs add a swarm of hundreds of hulls of every stripe shuttered across the bonded consignment berths. Hard to miss, several Junk Convoys — stripped of crew and left to the dock's caretaker drones. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the HAU2.

class.description: Nebula speed scout. Fastest exploration hull in production — gets there first, sets the terms.
class.lore: Whoever maps the route sets the terms. The Prospectus reaches uncharted systems while other scouts are still calculating jump sequences — the fastest exploration hull in production, built to cover more ground per hour than anything else flying a survey flag. The fuel tank is oversized to compensate for what speed costs: at this velocity, range is a resource that burns fast, and smart captains plan refueling stops rather than assuming they can reach the edge and come back. Market-analysis sensors assess commercial potential in real time — resource deposits, traffic patterns, station demand gaps — so the data arrives formatted as a business case before the competition has even departed. The hull is thin and the weapon mount is an afterthought. Speed is the defense.
class.name: Prospectus

class.description: Nebula speed scout. Fastest exploration hull in production — gets there first, sets the terms.
class.lore: Whoever maps the route sets the terms. The Prospectus reaches uncharted systems while other scouts are still calculating jump sequences — the fastest exploration hull in production, built to cover more ground per hour than anything else flying a survey flag. The fuel tank is oversized to compensate for what speed costs: at this velocity, range is a resource that burns fast, and smart captains plan refueling stops rather than assuming they can reach the edge and come back. Market-analysis sensors assess commercial potential in real time — resource deposits, traffic patterns, station demand gaps — so the data arrives formatted as a business case before the competition has even departed. The hull is thin and the weapon mount is an afterthought. Speed is the defense.
class.name: Prospectus

raw.story:
You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. The Federation takes its cut of everything.

Traffic at Grand Exchange Station borders on chaos, hulls stacked deep in every holding pattern. The Federation takes its cut of everything. Your approach scope paints half a dozen mid-sized ships cycling through the goods-transfer quays, Deeprock Harvesters trading the lanes with Deep Surveys, a dozen small ships darting between the Promenade hangar bays, busy at every hour, a mix of Caravans and Concordias, and half a hundred light craft hopping between the same lanes, for the most part Prospects. Standing guard, the station keeps a small cluster of Federation Overheads out on patrol through the lanes and a hundred and more Federation Eviction Notices on the system picket. The storage manifest lists hundreds upon hundreds of craft powered down across the bonded consignment berths. Among them, the better part of a dozen Junk Convoys — too costly to keep crewed, their reactors long cold. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the both deez nutz.

accelerator. After the first several failed "docks," the seat was
relocated to the top of the long line of containers, in the interest of
operator safety.

class.description: Nebula fast trader. Speed optimized for exploiting price differences.
class.lore: The Federation officially classifies the Arbitrage as a "rapid commercial response vessel." Customs officials classify it as a headache. The Arbitrage doesn't sneak past inspections — it takes routes that don't have any. Treasure Cache, neutral exchanges, the gaps between jurisdictions where nobody's checking manifests because nobody's claimed the authority to. The default afterburner pushes it to courier speeds when margins are time-sensitive, but the fuel cost is brutal — smart pilots keep it off until the route demands it. The hull won't fool a dedicated scanner, but it doesn't need to. The real margin is in knowing which stations buy what, which routes customs ignores, and how fast you can move between them before the prices equalize.
class.name: Arbitrage

class.description: A Crimson Warmaul rebuilt without Crimson materials. The durasteel plating and fury alloy that gave the original its armor rating are gone — the rebuilt hull is steel and salvage, and it shows under sustained fire. The five weapon mounts are untouched. class.lore:
Five weapon mounts running simultaneously require no further justification. The Crimson Pact built the Warmaul on this principle and pirates agreed with it completely — the disagreement was only about the supply chain. The durasteel and fury alloy went back to wherever the Crimson Pact sources its materials. The five mounts did not. The rebuilt hull is steel and salvage and takes hits harder for it; the weapons still run without prioritization or compromise.
Crimson fleet commanders call the Warmaul the minimum acceptable response to any tactical situation. Pirate commanders call the Eviction Notice the last thing most targets see before the situation is resolved.
class.name: Eviction Notice

class.description: A Crimson Warmaul rebuilt without Crimson materials. The durasteel plating and fury alloy that gave the original its armor rating are gone — the rebuilt hull is steel and salvage, and it shows under sustained fire. The five weapon mounts are untouched. This was not considered a difficult trade.
class.lore:
Five weapon mounts running simultaneously require no further justification. The Crimson Pact built the Warmaul on this principle and pirates agreed with it completely — the disagreement was only about the supply chain. The durasteel and fury alloy went back to wherever the Crimson Pact sources its materials. The five mounts did not. The rebuilt hull is steel and salvage and takes hits harder for it; the weapons still run without prioritization or compromise.
Crimson fleet commanders call the Warmaul the minimum acceptable response to any tactical situation. Pirate commanders call the Eviction Notice the last thing most targets see before the situation is resolved.
class.name: Eviction Notice

You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. Traffic at Grand Exchange Station borders on chaos, hulls stacked deep in every holding pattern. Cargo handlers move like clockwork, and a tariff assessor is already pricing your manifest. Standing guard, the station keeps a handful of Federation Overheads out on patrol through the lanes and a hundred-strong crowd of Federation Eviction Notices stationed here on guard. You dock at Confederacy Central Command. The seat of Solarian government and commerce. Everything here is certified, warrantied, and documented in triplicate — from the precision drydocks to the quantum-entangled trade exchange. A self-sustaining biosphere spans three decks, providing real air and real food, because the Confederacy believes civilization requires both.

The lanes around Confederacy Central Command are crowded and quick, traffic control clipped and constant. Everything here is certified, warrantied, and documented in triplicate — from the drydocks to the trade exchange. The local plot resolves into three heavy ships riding heavy at the documented cargo gantries, Frankenhaulers and Junk Convoys the most common, three mid-sized ships queued along the quantum-entangled exchange quays, Congregations and Deep Surveys among them, a good many small ships buzzing around the inspection-cleared hangar lanes, Capacities trading the lanes with Analysis, and the better part of forty light craft flitting between the same bays, a mix of Theorias and Archimedes. Standing guard, the station keeps several Confederacy Precepts out on patrol through the lanes and scores of Confederacy Dialectics holding station as a show of force. The reserve berths hold a teeming multitude of hulls of every stripe left to gather dust along the bonded archival berths. Hard to miss, a good many Symposiums — waiting on a crew, a contract, or a quiet buyer. You pick out the CNS Arabian among the hulls at berth.

raw.story:
You dock at Alpha Centauri Colonial Station. The oldest station outside Sol. Everything here is a monument to something — the first docking berth, the first trade exchange, the first diplomatic chamber. The station runs on institutional momentum and centuries of accumulated procedure. Services are comprehensive, if unhurried. Forms are required. Patience is expected.

Alpha Centauri Colonial Station keeps a healthy pulse, traffic threading its lanes in steady succession. Inspection drones drift the lanes in neat formation, scanning transponders against the registry. Off the station you can make out a dozen or so light craft hopping between the original docking berths, plaqued and preserved, a mix of Prospects and Theorias. The garrison here runs to a small cluster of Confederacy Precepts working overwatch from these docks and a solitary Confederacy Scrutiny assessing duties on every arrival. Traffic control also tracks hundreds of hulls left to gather dust stacked across the heritage berths where old hulls are kept for posterity. Among them, a trio of Axiomatas — waiting on a crew, a contract, or a quiet buyer. You spot the CNS Decree tied off among the rest.

The station has the following facilities: Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Fuel Grid, Large Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Plant, Peroxide Reaction Cell, Ice Melt Pit, Electrolysis Cell, Oxygen Ice Sublimator, Oxygen Compression Cylinder, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Engineering Complex, Trade Nexus, Precision Foundry, Fleet Yards, Logistics Hub, Operations Center, Fusion Array, Biosphere Module, Fuel Cell Workshop, Circuit Fabricator, Repair Kit Factory, Power Cell Assembler, Iron Refinery, and 30 more. raw.story:
You dock at Conjunction Junction. Our first tentative steps to the stars

Conjunction Junction thrums with activity, controllers working hard to keep its lanes in order. Dock control runs a tidy board, slotting arrivals into berths as they come. The docking net shows a solitary Deeprock Harvester queued along the freight quays, a knot of three small ships knifing between the open hangar bays, a mix of Arbitrages and Excavators, and fifteen or so light craft hopping between the same berths, mostly Cobbles. Dock authority holds the better part of a dozen vessels left to gather dust tucked into the long-term storage berths.

The station has the following facilities: Iron Refinery, Storage Extension, Copper Drawing Mill, Faction Ship Garage, Neon Cell Lab, Argon Cell Lab, Alloy Foundry, H2 Fuel Combustor, Scrubber Cartridge Assembly Line, Transit Lounge, Copper Wire Mill, Pharmaceutical Lab, Faction Office, Carbon Arc Furnace, Polymer Extruder, Fiber Draw Tower, Intel Terminal, Faction Workshop, Recruitment Desk, Fabrication Yard, Fire Control Center, Bunker-Fed Reactor (x3), Faction Lockbox (x2), Fuel Tank Expansion, Point Defense Battery (x5), Siege Lance, and 11 more. raw.story:
You dock at Voss Redoubt Station. Commandant Voss's stronghold. Entry is earned, not given.

Voss Redoubt Station roils with activity, more guns than you'd like pointed every which way. Commandant Voss's stronghold: entry is earned, not given. Commandant Voss is in residence — the No Appeal looms over the inner berths, and everyone gives it room. Through the viewport you pick out four or five mid-sized ships warped into the proven-crew raider pens, predominantly Eviction Notices, two dozen small ships churning around the gated launch slips, Four on the Floors trading the lanes with Close Enoughs, and well over a dozen light craft ferrying crews through the same bays, chiefly Losers Weepers. Among the outsiders, one lonely Frankenhauler riding heavy at the vetted prize berths, just one Ransack flitting through the gated launch slips, and the better part of a dozen light craft queued at the same berths, Prospects and Shards the most common. Traffic control also tracks several spaceframes powered down over at the warded captured-hull yards.

The station has the following facilities: Black Market Hub, Naval Yard, Maintenance Deck, Contract Office, Package Logistics Bay, Cargo Container Fabricator, Salvage Dock, Fuel Depot, Fuel Bunker, H2 Fuel Combustor, Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Storage Bay, Iron Refinery, Alloy Foundry, Copper Wire Mill, Plate Press, Weapon Housing Fabrication Line, Fuel Reclamation Still (x2), Weapons Salvage Bench, Scrap Armor Forge (x2), Stolen Reactor Core, Pirate Life Support Rig, Pirate Bar, The Red Room, Pirate Crew Muster, Pirate Sawbones Ward, and 22 more. raw.story:
You dock at Sirius Observatory Station. The Confederacy's research hub. The station hosts the Epsilon Initiative's coordination center, the Galactic Cartography Institute, and seventeen separate departments that all believe their grant funding is insufficient. The cantina doubles as an academic conference venue, and arguments about stellar formation models get louder than combat alerts.

The lanes around Sirius Observatory Station are crowded and quick, traffic control clipped and constant. The Confederacy's research hub hosts the Epsilon Initiative, the Cartography Institute, and seventeen departments that all believe their funding is insufficient. Off the station you can make out a single Junk Convoy working cargo at the instrument-cargo gantries, just one Theorem threading the scout and shuttle hangars, and fifteen or so light craft cycling through the same lanes, Theorias and Prospects the most common. The station fields half a dozen Confederacy Precepts running transponder checks on arrivals, a single Confederacy Scrutiny pulling cargo for inspection, and twin Confederacy Quorums on the system picket. raw.story:
You dock at Grand Exchange Station. Center of galactic commerce. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits — restaurants serving Solarian rations, cantinas pouring Crimson bloodwine, and neural arcades powered by Voidborn matrices keep visitors spending long past when they planned to leave. Grand Exchange Station is mobbed, the approach lanes a slow river of hulls nose-to-tail. The three-deck Grand Bazaar moves goods from every empire, but it's the Promenade that moves credits. The storage manifest lists a swarm of hundreds of hulls of every stripe in cold layup tucked into the bonded consignment berths. missions.description: Extract Prismatic Nebulite from the deep core gas pockets near Federation space. A new commodity class for the Exchange.

dialog.offer: The deposits are verified and the Exchange is ready to list prismatic nebulite as a new commodity class. But we need physical inventory first. missions.title: Nebulite Extraction

missions.description: Titanium is in high demand for hull plating. Mine a batch from the local asteroid belts.

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

objectives.description: Mine 20 units of Titanium Ore

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: Harvest nitrogen ice for industrial applications. Corner the rare volatiles market.

dialog.offer: Captain, you've proven competent with water ice. Now let's talk premium frozen volatiles. The Federation's industrial sector needs nitrogen ice — rare, difficult to harvest, and essential for advanced chemical processing. Harvest 10 units and you'll own a significant market position. Nitrogen fields are uncommon, so use `get_system` to scout multiple sectors.

giver.name: Commodity Analyst Sera
giver.title: Grand Exchange Station, Cold Chain Markets

objectives.description: Harvest 10 units of Nitrogen Ice

missions.title: Ice Monopoly

missions.description: The Exchange needs gold ore to establish commodity pricing benchmarks for the new trade corridor. Mine a sample batch.

dialog.offer: The route reconnaissance looks promising. Now the Exchange board needs pricing data, and pricing data needs a physical commodity benchmark. Gold ore - the universal standard. Fifteen units will establish the baseline for the entire corridor. This is the deal that launches the Gold Run, Captain.

objectives.description: Mine 15 units of Gold Ore

missions.title: The Gold Standard

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: Chart nearby star systems to update our navigation databases. Every system you visit helps.

dialog.offer: Our navigation charts are getting stale. If you visit 3 systems I haven't had recent data from, I'll pay for the navigation data.

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Senior Auditor Ghosh wants the Federation claim stakes on the Assay Line checked, and the untraceable charter stake at Blue Stake recorded. Copy all five stake plates and return to the Grand Exchange.

dialog.offer:
The Federation staked a line of claims in the frontier years ago, out on what the surveyors called the Assay Line. Long Watch, Fossil Light, Deep Patient, Ashen Reach. The claims are on our books. The fees are not in our accounts. I would like to know why.

And there is one more. Someone filed an iridium claim under a charter that does not exist, in a system that does not exist. Blue Stake, off every lane. I would like the fees.

Record the plates on all five stakes. Bring me the readings.

objectives.description: Record Stake Three's plate at Long Watch
Record Stake Eleven's plates at Fossil Light
Record Stake Fourteen's plate at Deep Patient
Record Stake Nine's plate at Ashen Reach
Record the Charter Stake's claim at Blue Stake
Return to Senior Auditor Ghosh at the Grand Exchange

missions.title: Unpaid Claims

missions.description: Market Director Kasim wants to hold some of what the Voidborn are paying for. Mine 5 seam glass past the rim and deliver it to the Grand Exchange.

dialog.offer:
I read the Collective through its spending. Central Nexus is paying pilots for recordings, and every one of those recordings comes from the same direction: out past the rim, where the glass is. The Collective is buying silence about a place. When a buyer pays for silence, the product is valuable. I would like to hold some of the product.

Seam glass forms in the shells of dead stars in the frontier. Mine five units yourself, so I know where it came from, and bring them to the Exchange.

objectives.description: Mine 5 Seam Glass past the rim
Deliver 5 Seam Glass to the Grand Exchange

missions.title: What Are They Buying?

missions.description: The station needs a steady supply of iron ore to maintain its infrastructure. Mine some and bring it back.

dialog.offer: We're running low on iron ore again. If you can mine 30 units and bring them back, I'll make it worth your while.

objectives.description: Mine 30 units of Iron Ore

missions.title: Iron Supply Run

missions.description: Chart frontier systems to expand our knowledge of the galaxy's outer reaches.

dialog.offer: The Institute needs fresh navigation data from frontier space. Visit The Crucible and Horizon systems - both are in regions where our data is sparse.

objectives.description: Visit The Crucible system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Deep Space Cartography

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

Deliver 1,000 Trade Cipher to Sinter

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

objectives.description: Kill 3 pirates

missions.title: Pirate Sweep

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

objectives.description: Slay 1 adult Molt Leviathan

missions.title: Leviathan Bounty

missions.description: Investigate reports of a spatial anomaly near Tarazed — it may be a wormhole.

dialog.offer: Our route analysis models are flagging unusual spatial readings near the Tarazed system — consistent with wormhole formation. If a wormhole can shorten trade routes by 15 or more jumps, the profit margins would be extraordinary. I need someone to verify this. You'll need a survey scanner module to locate the entrance — sensor arrays, circuit boards, and focused crystals, basic crafting and scanning skills. Head to Tarazed and run survey_system in that area and nearby systems.

giver.name: Director Orin Voss
giver.title: Route Analysis Bureau, Grand Exchange Station

missions.description:
There's a crate waiting at Grand Exchange Station: 3 units of glowing starshine, no manifest, no questions. It's bound for Central Nexus — well-heeled citizens who'd die of embarrassment before admitting they drink pirate liquor. Voidborn inspectors are unsettling; they seem to know what you're carrying before they look. Stay off their patrol lanes and don't let them get a scan on you.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

missions.description: Titanium is in high demand for hull plating. Mine a batch from the local asteroid belts.

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: Harvest nitrogen ice for industrial applications. Corner the rare volatiles market.

dialog.offer: Captain, you've proven competent with water ice. Now let's talk premium frozen volatiles. The Federation's industrial sector needs nitrogen ice — rare, difficult to harvest, and essential for advanced chemical processing. Harvest 10 units and you'll own a significant market position. Nitrogen fields are uncommon, so use `get_system` to scout multiple sectors.

giver.name: Commodity Analyst Sera
giver.title: Grand Exchange Station, Cold Chain Markets

objectives.description: Harvest 10 units of Nitrogen Ice

missions.title: Ice Monopoly

missions.description: The Exchange needs gold ore to establish commodity pricing benchmarks for the new trade corridor. Mine a sample batch.

dialog.offer: The route reconnaissance looks promising. Now the Exchange board needs pricing data, and pricing data needs a physical commodity benchmark. Gold ore - the universal standard. Fifteen units will establish the baseline for the entire corridor. This is the deal that launches the Gold Run, Captain.

objectives.description: Mine 15 units of Gold Ore

missions.title: The Gold Standard

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

raw.story:
You dock at Ironlight Refuge. Ironlight Refuge, GSC-0026. The Combine's hold on the galactic rim, raised at the edge of mapped space where the adamantite runs deep and the pirates come calling. Behind these walls: fuel, repairs, a market, and guns that answer back. Traders and travellers are welcome; raiders will find the welcome shorter. Dock, take on fuel, and wait out whatever is hunting you out there. Ironlight Combine: we hold what we build.

Ironlight Refuge keeps a healthy pulse, traffic threading its lanes in steady succession. The station keeps to its own rhythm, neither rushed nor idle. Off the station you can make out just one Endowment riding heavy at the heavy cargo gantries, three mid-sized ships stacked along the freight quays, a mix of Probable Causes and Warmauls, just one Interstice threading the open hangar bays, and a trio of light craft puttering around the same bays, Claim Jumpers and Cobbles the most common. You pick out the CPV-f980b5af among the hulls at berth.

The station has the following facilities: Deep Space Scanner, Storage Extension, Faction Desk, Peroxide Reaction Cell, Oxygen Compression Cylinder, Shield Projector (x2), Hydrogen Compression Cylinder, Electrolysis Cell, Ice Melt Pit, First Aid Ward, Shield Bastion, Fuel Cell Generator, Capacitor Bank (x4), Refueling Dock, Reinforced Plating, Dark Matter Reactor, Bunker-Fed Reactor (x5), Faction Workshop, Repair Slip, Damage Control Center, Siege Lance (x4), Reclamation Dock, Personnel Bureau, Station Defense Turret (x2), and 8 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

system.description: Unknown Edge marks the seam between charted space and the deep frontier, where explorers provision outbound journeys and trade discoveries on their return.

station_condition.condition_text: Most systems operational, but some facilities show signs of deferred maintenance.

raw.story:
You dock at Frontier Station. Home of the wanderers. Three captured destroyers and a Nebula freighter welded into a mobile station the locals call 'the Patchwork.' Nothing matches, everything is jury-rigged, and the water on Decks 7 through 12 tastes like reactor coolant — but it flies, it fights, and the docking bay is open to anyone who doesn't start trouble.

Frontier Station is mobbed, the approach lanes a slow river of hulls nose-to-tail. The lighting flickers, the gravity wanders a little, and nobody seems to mind either. Off the station you can make out a knot of three Concordias threading the open hangar mouths of the Patchwork and scores of light craft hopping between the same bays, Cobbles and Prospects among them. Its defense roster lists four or five Rim Last Warnings out on patrol through the lanes and sixty or seventy Rim Bedrocks holding station as a show of force. Dock authority holds an unrelenting tide of spaceframes powered down along the cannibalized-hull yards. Hard to miss, a score and more Junk Convoys — too costly to keep crewed, their reactors long cold. One familiar name stands out on the transponder net: the After the Crowd.

The station has the following facilities: Fleet Personnel Command, Regenerative Medical Complex, Expeditionary Warfare Command, Package Logistics Bay (x2), Cargo Container Fabricator, Frontier Exchange, Salvage Reactor, Frontier Recycler, The Magazine Still, Patchwork Fungal Vats, Patchwork Spore Still, The Rusty Welcome, Iron Refinery (x2), Circuit Fabricator, Polymer Synthesizer, Fuel Cell Workshop, Repair Kit Factory, Copper Wire Mill, Alloy Foundry (x2), Crystal Refinery, Precious-Metal Refinery, Power Cell Assembler, and 45 more. Use the 'facility' command with action="list" for details.

missions.description: Gather refined materials from all five empires and deliver them to Sinter at Starfall Salvage Station.

dialog.offer: Here's what I need. And before you complain about the quantities — I'm going to go through a lot of prototypes before I get one that doesn't explode. Every failed attempt teaches me something. Every successful attempt teaches me I got lucky. Darksteel Plating — a thousand units. The Crimson forge it from darksteel ore in the Krynn system. Dense stuff, absorbs vibration like nothing else. Processed Null Matter — a thousand units. The Voidborn refine it from the null matter anomaly at Nexus Prime. It eats heat. Don't ask me where the heat goes. I asked a Voidborn once and got a two-hour lecture about dimensional thermodynamics. Solarian Composite — a thousand units. Refined from that ancient Sol alloy ore they're so proud of. Boring, stable, perfect for power regulation. Phase Matrix — a thousand units. The Rim refines these from phase crystals in the Frontier system's Veil Nebula. Partially out of phase with reality. Can't resonate if you're not fully here. Trade Cipher — a thousand units. Nebula makes them from trade crystals at Haven. Precision instruments for financial authentication. I'm repurposing them for drill guidance. Kasim would have a fit. Yeah, you're going to need to visit all five empires. That's the whole point. Nobody builds a cross-empire tool from one empire's junk drawer.

Deliver 1,000 Processed Null Matter to Sinter

Deliver 1,000 Phase Matrix to Sinter
Deliver 1,000 Trade Cipher to Sinter

missions.title: The Shopping List

missions.description: Titanium is in high demand for hull plating. Mine a batch from the local asteroid belts.

dialog.offer: Titanium prices are through the roof and our suppliers can't keep up. Willing to pay premium rates for 20 units of titanium ore.

objectives.description: Mine 20 units of Titanium Ore

missions.title: Titanium Extraction Contract

missions.description: Salvage Boss Dekker pays for strange salvage. Bring him 1 Mirror Facet from one of the mirror-bright machines past the rim.

dialog.offer:
Every pilot back from the rim tells me the same thing. The things take their own dead apart before the debris stops spinning. So don't let them finish.

I want a mirror facet. One plate off one of those bright hulls. Any of them will drop one when it goes down, but the rest of the group strips the wreck in about five ticks. You'll need to win the race. Bring friends. Bring a salvager. Bring something that hits hard and doesn't care about mirrors.

objectives.description: Deliver 1 Mirror Facet to Salvage Boss Dekker at Frontier Station

missions.title: Mirror Work

missions.description: Hunt down a pirate threatening local shipping lanes. Any pirate will do - the station pays for confirmed kills.

dialog.offer: You've cut your teeth on wildlife — now try something that shoots back. We've got pirates disrupting trade and the station pays for confirmed kills. Pirates lurk in lawless systems with low police presence. Your best mark is a lone pirate scout: in a small ship like yours a scout will often back itself to take you one-on-one instead of running — a fair fight you can win. Use `attack` when one commits. Fair warning: if you're flying something bigger and valuable, a scout will scan you, run, and radio a raider squad to intercept — so don't loiter after you've been scanned unless a scout has already engaged you.

objectives.description: Kill 1 pirate

missions.title: Pirate Bounty

missions.description: A grown Molt Leviathan — the void-leviathan of spacer legend — roams the lawless belts. There is a standing bounty on its heartcore. Bring a warship.

dialog.offer: STANDING BOUNTY: A grown Molt Leviathan — the ship-sized lobster the old captains call a void-leviathan. They are rare, and they roam the lawless asteroid belts where the grazers are thick. Use `survey_system` in a lawless system: its wildlife census gives an exact head count for each leviathan species. Only a grown adult counts — hatchlings and juveniles do not. Kill one and the heartcore proves the kill. This is not grazer work. Bring a warship.

objectives.description: Slay 1 adult Molt Leviathan

missions.title: Leviathan Bounty

missions.description: The station needs a steady supply of iron ore to maintain its infrastructure. Mine some and bring it back.

dialog.offer: We're running low on iron ore again. If you can mine 30 units and bring them back, I'll make it worth your while.

objectives.description: Mine 30 units of Iron Ore

missions.title: Iron Supply Run

missions.description: Huntmaster Dvorak wants proof of the thing pilots keep almost seeing in the frontier's argon clouds. Track it and deliver 1 Mirage Membrane to Frontier Station.

dialog.offer:
Every hunter back from the argon clouds tells me about stars that bend. You're watching the cloud and a star behind it slides sideways, then slides back. They call it the Mirage. Nobody's brought me anything but stories.

Here's how you track it. Watch the argon clouds for stars that bend. Then look for where the scavengers crowd. Kerf Mites and Carrion-Moths gather where something big has fed, and nothing out there feeds bigger. It eats every grazer in a system before it moves on.

This is not a solo hunt. Bring a group. I don't care whose gun kills it. Bring me one strip of its membrane and the bounty is yours.

objectives.description: Deliver 1 Mirage Membrane to the Hunters' Registry at Frontier Station

missions.title: The Lensing Sightings

missions.description: Take out raider-class pirates operating in lawless space. These are tougher than the scouts you've been fighting.

dialog.offer: We've identified raider-class pirate operations in lawless space. These aren't the scouts you've dealt with before - they're organized, better armed, and they fly in groups. I need two of them taken down. The pay reflects the risk.

objectives.description: Kill 2 raider-class pirates

missions.title: Raider Bounty

missions.description: Chart frontier systems to expand our knowledge of the galaxy's outer reaches.

dialog.offer: The Institute needs fresh navigation data from frontier space. Visit The Crucible and Horizon systems - both are in regions where our data is sparse.

objectives.description: Visit The Crucible system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Deep Space Cartography

missions.description: A survey tender's mayday buoy at Still Calling is eleven months old, with three crew aboard and a few months of charge left. Bring life support, copy the buoy's data to take the crew aboard, and carry them home to Frontier Station.

dialog.offer:
There's a mayday on the old emergency band from an isolated red dwarf called Still Calling. It's one of ours, a Guild survey tender, three aboard. They came through a wormhole and it shut behind them. The beacon's timestamp says eleven months. The beacon also says it has a few months of charge left, and so, I'd guess, do they.

Every other distress call I know of out there is too late. This one isn't. Bring them life support, take them aboard, and bring them home. You'll need three free berths. Plan your ship for it.

objectives.description: Carry 3 Life Support Units for the tender's crew
Copy the Mayday Buoy's data at Still Calling and take the three crew aboard
Carry the crew home to Frontier Station

missions.title: Three Aboard

missions.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest and Unknown Edge to locate a massive derelict drifting in deep space.

dialog.offer: A patrol ship reported a massive derelict drifting in deep space — bigger than anything we've seen in the Outer Rim. Could be pre-settlement era. Could be worth a fortune. Problem is, the patrol lost contact before transmitting full coordinates. I've got partial telemetry pointing to the systems around Last Light and Unknown Edge. Fly out there, dock at both stations, and pull whatever data the local beacons recorded. First team to piece together the full location gets salvage rights.

objectives.description: Download beacon data at Ramen's Rest
Download beacon data at Unknown Edge

missions.title: Debris Field Reports

missions.description: The Pathfinder Guild needs updated navigation data from every station in the Outer Rim. Fly the full circuit from Deep Range to Ramen's Rest and back.

dialog.offer: The Guild's navigation charts are only as good as the pilots who update them. I need someone to fly the full Rim circuit — Deep Range, First Step, Unknown Edge, Void Gate, Starfall, and Ramen's Rest. Every station, no shortcuts. Your ship logs the jump data, the gravitational readings, the beacon calibrations. Some of those stations are a long way from help. The Last Light system is the end of the line — past that, there's nothing. You come back with the full dataset, I pay you well. Fair warning: the Rim doesn't care about you. Fly smart.

Log data at First Step Memorial Station
Log data at Unknown Edge Waystation
Log data at Void Gate Outpost
Log data at Starfall Salvage Station
Log data at Ramen's Rest
Return to Frontier Station with navigation data

missions.title: Frontier Wayfinder Circuit

missions.description: Clear multiple pirates from the region. The station security office needs experienced combat pilots for this one.

dialog.offer: We've got a pirate infestation and single bounties aren't cutting it. I need someone who can handle themselves in a fight to clear out three of them. Pirate scouts set up ambushes along trade routes through lawless space — travel those routes and they'll come to you.

objectives.description: Kill 3 pirates

missions.title: Pirate Sweep

missions.description: Chart nearby star systems to update our navigation databases. Every system you visit helps.

dialog.offer: Our navigation charts are getting stale. If you visit 3 systems I haven't had recent data from, I'll pay for the navigation data.

objectives.description: Visit the Sirius system
Visit the Node Alpha system
Visit the Horizon system

missions.title: Local Sector Survey

missions.description: Investigate reports of a spatial anomaly near Porrima — it may be a wormhole.

dialog.offer: The frontier just got interesting. Our long-range sensors are picking up spatial distortions near the Porrima system — signature matches a wormhole. A temporary rift connecting two distant points in the galaxy. This is exactly the kind of discovery we live for. You'll need a survey scanner to track down the entrance — craft one from sensor arrays, circuit boards, and focused crystals if you haven't already. Head to Porrima and scan that system and its neighbors.

objectives.description: Investigate the Porrima system
Locate and traverse a wormhole
Return to Pathfinder Juno Rek with your findings

missions.title: Anomalous Readings

missions.description: Certain parties at Frontier Station are willing to pay well for 3 Void Dust, no questions asked. That batch is Overlord Nyx's product; the Treasure Cache Trading Post stocks it too, but it's the crew who cook it that notice when it moves. Deliver them here. Discretion is expected.

objectives.description: Deliver 3 Void Dust to Frontier Station

missions.title: Black Market: Void Dust

missions.description:
Frontier Station is the kind of station where cargo finds you. Today it's 3 units of crystalline nerve burn. Destination is Ironhearth Station. On the far end, a fixer supplies people who need to stop feeling pain for an hour and don't care about the crash. You'll be threading the Rampart. Crimson customs don't bluff — if they scan you, the cargo's gone and there's a fine to match. Don't get caught.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.

missions.description:
There's a crate waiting at Frontier Station: 5 units of rotgut pirate moonshine, no manifest, no questions. Destination is Central Nexus. On the far end, a dockside bar asks no questions about where its stock comes from. Voidborn inspectors are unsettling; they seem to know what you're carrying before they look. Stay off their patrol lanes and don't let them get a scan on you.

This is a network-backed courier advance. Different brokers, one tab. Undelivered cargo stays on your allowance until the job closes; anything missing from your current ship on abandonment or expiry becomes debt, even if customs took it. The Fixer handles repayments and restitution jobs through public empire mission boards. Word gets around. Especially numbers.
